declarations.name: lookupAccount
declarations.doc: lookupAccount fetches details of an account and adds it to the prestate if it doesn't exist there.

declarations.name: lookupStorage
declarations.doc: lookupStorage fetches the requested storage slot and adds it to the prestate of the given contract. It assumes `lookupAccount` has been performed on the contract before.

declarations.name: init
declarations.doc: init registers itself this packages as a lookup for tracers.

declarations.name: lookup
declarations.doc: lookup returns a tracer, if one can be matched to the given name.

declarations.name: register
declarations.doc: register is used by native tracers to register their presence.

declarations.name: ctorFn
declarations.doc: ctorFn is the constructor signature of a native tracer.

declarations.name: BalanceAt
declarations.doc: BalanceAt returns the wei balance of the given account. The block number can be nil, in which case the balance is taken from the latest known block.

declarations.name: BlockByHash
declarations.doc: BlockByHash returns the given full block. Note that loading full blocks requires two requests. Use HeaderByHash if you don't need all transactions or uncle headers.

declarations.name: BlockByNumber
declarations.doc: BlockByNumber returns a block from the current canonical chain. If number is nil, the latest known block is returned. Note that loading full blocks requires two requests. Use HeaderByNumber if you don't need all transactions or uncle headers.

declarations.name: BlockNumber
declarations.doc: BlockNumber returns the most recent block number

declarations.name: CallContract
declarations.doc: CallContract executes a message call transaction, which is directly executed in the VM of the node, but never mined into the blockchain. blockNumber selects the block height at which the call runs. It can be nil, in which case the code is taken from the latest known block. Note that state from very old blocks might not be available.

declarations.name: CallContractAtHash
declarations.doc: CallContractAtHash is almost the same as CallContract except that it selects the block by block hash instead of block height.

declarations.name: ChainID
declarations.doc: ChainID retrieves the current chain ID for transaction replay protection.

declarations.name: CodeAt
declarations.doc: CodeAt returns the contract code of the given account. The block number can be nil, in which case the code is taken from the latest known block.

declarations.name: Dial
declarations.doc: Dial connects a client to the given URL.

declarations.name: EstimateGas
declarations.doc: EstimateGas tries to estimate the gas needed to execute a specific transaction based on the current pending state of the backend blockchain. There is no guarantee that this is the true gas limit requirement as other transactions may be added or removed by miners, but it should provide a basis for setting a reasonable default.

declarations.name: FilterLogs
declarations.doc: FilterLogs executes a filter query.

declarations.name: HeaderByHash
declarations.doc: HeaderByHash returns the block header with the given hash.

declarations.name: HeaderByNumber
declarations.doc: HeaderByNumber returns a block header from the current canonical chain. If number is nil, the latest known header is returned.

declarations.name: NetworkID
declarations.doc: NetworkID returns the network ID (also known as the chain ID) for this chain.

declarations.name: NewClient
declarations.doc: NewClient creates a client that uses the given RPC client.

declarations.name: NonceAt
declarations.doc: NonceAt returns the account nonce of the given account. The block number can be nil, in which case the nonce is taken from the latest known block.

declarations.name: PeerCount
declarations.doc: PeerCount returns the number of p2p peers as reported by the net_peerCount method.

declarations.name: PendingBalanceAt
declarations.doc: PendingBalanceAt returns the wei balance of the given account in the pending state.

declarations.name: PendingCallContract
declarations.doc: PendingCallContract executes a message call transaction using the EVM. The state seen by the contract call is the pending state.

declarations.name: PendingCodeAt
declarations.doc: PendingCodeAt returns the contract code of the given account in the pending state.

declarations.name: PendingNonceAt
declarations.doc: PendingNonceAt returns the account nonce of the given account in the pending state. This is the nonce that should be used for the next transaction.

declarations.name: PendingStorageAt
declarations.doc: PendingStorageAt returns the value of key in the contract storage of the given account in the pending state.

declarations.name: PendingTransactionCount
declarations.doc: PendingTransactionCount returns the total number of transactions in the pending state.

declarations.name: SendTransaction
declarations.doc: SendTransaction injects a signed transaction into the pending pool for execution. If the transaction was a contract creation use the TransactionReceipt method to get the contract address after the transaction has been mined.

declarations.name: SendTransactions
declarations.doc: SendTransactions injects signed transactions into the pending pool for execution. If the transaction was a contract creation use the TransactionReceipt method to get the contract address after the transaction has been mined.

declarations.name: StorageAt
declarations.doc: StorageAt returns the value of key in the contract storage of the given account. The block number can be nil, in which case the value is taken from the latest known block.

declarations.name: SubscribeFilterLogs
declarations.doc: SubscribeFilterLogs subscribes to the results of a streaming filter query.

declarations.name: SubscribeNewHead
declarations.doc: SubscribeNewHead subscribes to notifications about the current blockchain head on the given channel.

declarations.name: SuggestGasPrice
declarations.doc: SuggestGasPrice retrieves the currently suggested gas price to allow a timely execution of a transaction.

declarations.name: SuggestGasTipCap
declarations.doc: SuggestGasTipCap retrieves the currently suggested gas tip cap after 1559 to allow a timely execution of a transaction.

declarations.name: SyncProgress
declarations.doc: SyncProgress retrieves the current progress of the sync algorithm. If there's no sync currently running, it returns nil.

declarations.name: TransactionByHash
declarations.doc: TransactionByHash returns the transaction with the given hash.

declarations.name: TransactionCount
declarations.doc: TransactionCount returns the total number of transactions in the given block.

declarations.name: TransactionInBlock
declarations.doc: TransactionInBlock returns a single transaction at index in the given block.

declarations.name: TransactionReceipt
declarations.doc: TransactionReceipt returns the receipt of a transaction by transaction hash. Note that the receipt is not available for pending transactions.

declarations.name: TransactionSender
declarations.doc: TransactionSender returns the sender address of the given transaction. The transaction must be known to the remote node and included in the blockchain at the given block and index. The sender is the one derived by the protocol at the time of inclusion. There is a fast-path for transactions retrieved by TransactionByHash and TransactionInBlock. Getting their sender address can be done without an RPC interaction.

declarations.name: Client
declarations.doc: Client defines typed wrappers for the Ethereum RPC API.

declarations.name: rpcProgress
declarations.doc: rpcProgress is a copy of SyncProgress with hex-encoded fields.

declarations.name: senderFromServer
declarations.doc: senderFromServer is a types.Signer that remembers the sender address returned by the RPC server. It is stored in the transaction's sender address cache to avoid an additional request in TransactionSender.

declarations.name: CallContract
declarations.doc: CallContract executes a message call transaction, which is directly executed in the VM of the node, but never mined into the blockchain. blockNumber selects the block height at which the call runs. It can be nil, in which case the code is taken from the latest known block. Note that state from very old blocks might not be available. overrides specifies a map of contract states that should be overwritten before executing the message call. Please use ethclient.CallContract instead if you don't need the override functionality.

declarations.name: CreateAccessList
declarations.doc: CreateAccessList tries to create an access list for a specific transaction based on the current pending state of the blockchain.

declarations.name: GCStats
declarations.doc: GCStats retrieves the current garbage collection stats from a geth node.

declarations.name: GetNodeInfo
declarations.doc: GetNodeInfo retrieves the node info of a geth node.

declarations.name: GetProof
declarations.doc: GetProof returns the account and storage values of the specified account including the Merkle-proof. The block number can be nil, in which case the value is taken from the latest known block.

declarations.name: MemStats
declarations.doc: MemStats retrieves the current memory stats from a geth node.

declarations.name: New
declarations.doc: New creates a client that uses the given RPC client.

declarations.name: SetHead
declarations.doc: SetHead sets the current head of the local chain by block number. Note, this is a destructive action and may severely damage your chain. Use with extreme caution.

declarations.name: SubscribePendingTransactions
declarations.doc: SubscribePendingTransactions subscribes to new pending transactions.

declarations.name: AccountResult
declarations.doc: AccountResult is the result of a GetProof operation.

declarations.name: Client
declarations.doc: Client is a wrapper around rpc.Client that implements geth-specific functionality. If you want to use the standardized Ethereum RPC functionality, use ethclient.Client instead.

declarations.name: OverrideAccount
declarations.doc: OverrideAccount specifies the state of an account to be overridden.

declarations.name: StorageResult
declarations.doc: StorageResult provides a proof for a key-value pair.

declarations.name: Delete
declarations.doc: Delete removes the key from the key-value data store.

declarations.name: Put
declarations.doc: Put inserts the given value into the key-value data store.

declarations.name: Batch
declarations.doc: Batch is a write-only database that commits changes to its host database when Write is called. A batch cannot be used concurrently.

declarations.name: Batcher
declarations.doc: Batcher wraps the NewBatch method of a backing data store.

declarations.name: HookedBatch
declarations.doc: HookedBatch wraps an arbitrary batch where each operation may be hooked into to monitor from black box code.

declarations.name: AncientReader
declarations.doc: AncientReader is the extended ancient reader interface including 'batched' or 'atomic' reading.

declarations.name: AncientReaderOp
declarations.doc: AncientReaderOp contains the methods required to read from immutable ancient data.

declarations.name: AncientStater
declarations.doc: AncientStater wraps the Stat method of a backing data store.

declarations.name: AncientStore
declarations.doc: AncientStore contains all the methods required to allow handling different ancient data stores backing immutable chain data store.

declarations.name: AncientWriteOp
declarations.doc: AncientWriteOp is given to the function argument of ModifyAncients.

declarations.name: AncientWriter
declarations.doc: AncientWriter contains the methods required to write to immutable ancient data.

declarations.name: Compacter
declarations.doc: Compacter wraps the Compact method of a backing data store.

declarations.name: Database
declarations.doc: Database contains all the methods required by the high level database to not only access the key-value data store but also the chain freezer.

declarations.name: KeyValueReader
declarations.doc: KeyValueReader wraps the Has and Get method of a backing data store.

declarations.name: KeyValueStater
declarations.doc: KeyValueStater wraps the Stat method of a backing data store.

declarations.name: KeyValueStore
declarations.doc: KeyValueStore contains all the methods required to allow handling different key-value data stores backing the high level database.

declarations.name: KeyValueWriter
declarations.doc: KeyValueWriter wraps the Put method of a backing data store.

declarations.name: Reader
declarations.doc: Reader contains the methods required to read data from both key-value as well as immutable ancient data.

declarations.name: Stater
declarations.doc: Stater contains the methods required to retrieve states from both key-value as well as immutable ancient data.

declarations.name: Writer
declarations.doc: Writer contains the methods required to write data to both key-value as well as immutable ancient data.

declarations.name: Iteratee
declarations.doc: Iteratee wraps the NewIterator methods of a backing data store.

declarations.name: Iterator
declarations.doc: Iterator iterates over a database's key/value pairs in ascending key order. When it encounters an error any seek will return false and will yield no key/ value pairs. The error can be queried by calling the Error method. Calling Release is still necessary. An iterator must be released after use, but it is not necessary to read an iterator until exhaustion. An iterator is not safe for concurrent use, but it is safe to use multiple iterators concurrently.

declarations.name: Snapshotter
declarations.doc: Snapshotter wraps the Snapshot method of a backing data store.

declarations.name: TestDatabaseSuite
declarations.doc: TestDatabaseSuite runs a suite of tests against a KeyValueStore database implementation.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close stops the metrics collection, flushes any pending data to disk and closes all io accesses to the underlying key-value store.

declarations.name: Compact
declarations.doc: Compact flattens the underlying data store for the given key range. In essence, deleted and overwritten versions are discarded, and the data is rearranged to reduce the cost of operations needed to access them. A nil start is treated as a key before all keys in the data store; a nil limit is treated as a key after all keys in the data store. If both is nil then it will compact entire data store.

declarations.name: Delete
declarations.doc: Delete removes the key from the key-value store.

declarations.name: Delete
declarations.doc: Delete inserts the a key removal into the batch for later committing.

declarations.name: Delete
declarations.doc: Delete removes the key from the key-value data store.

declarations.name: Get
declarations.doc: Get retrieves the given key if it's present in the key-value store.

declarations.name: Get
declarations.doc: Get retrieves the given key if it's present in the snapshot backing by key-value data store.

declarations.name: Has
declarations.doc: Has retrieves if a key is present in the key-value store.

declarations.name: Has
declarations.doc: Has retrieves if a key is present in the snapshot backing by a key-value data store.

declarations.name: New
declarations.doc: New returns a wrapped LevelDB object. The namespace is the prefix that the metrics reporting should use for surfacing internal stats.

declarations.name: NewBatch
declarations.doc: NewBatch creates a write-only key-value store that buffers changes to its host database until a final write is called.

declarations.name: NewBatchWithSize

declarations.name: Feed

Feeds can only be used with a single type. The type is determined by the first Send or Subscribe operation. Subsequent calls to these methods panic if the type does not match. The zero value is ready to use.

declarations.name: Count

declarations.name: NewSubscription
declarations.doc: NewSubscription runs a producer function as a subscription in a new goroutine. The channel given to the producer is closed when Unsubscribe is called. If fn returns an error, it is sent on the subscription's error channel.

declarations.name: Resubscribe
declarations.doc: Resubscribe calls fn repeatedly to keep a subscription established. When the subscription is established, Resubscribe waits for it to fail and calls fn again. This process repeats until Unsubscribe is called or the active subscription ends successfully. Resubscribe applies backoff between calls to fn. The time between calls is adapted based on the error rate, but will never exceed backoffMax.

declarations.name: ResubscribeErr
declarations.doc: ResubscribeErr calls fn repeatedly to keep a subscription established. When the subscription is established, ResubscribeErr waits for it to fail and calls fn again. This process repeats until Unsubscribe is called or the active subscription ends successfully. The difference between Resubscribe and ResubscribeErr is that with ResubscribeErr, the error of the failing subscription is available to the callback for logging purposes. ResubscribeErr applies backoff between calls to fn. The time between calls is adapted based on the error rate, but will never exceed backoffMax.

declarations.name: Track
declarations.doc: Track starts tracking a subscription. If the scope is closed, Track returns nil. The returned subscription is a wrapper. Unsubscribing the wrapper removes it from the scope.

declarations.name: ResubscribeErrFunc
declarations.doc: A ResubscribeErrFunc attempts to establish a subscription. For every call but the first, the second argument to this function is the error that occurred with the previous subscription.

declarations.name: ResubscribeFunc
declarations.doc: A ResubscribeFunc attempts to establish a subscription.

declarations.name: Subscription
declarations.doc: Subscription represents a stream of events. The carrier of the events is typically a channel, but isn't part of the interface. Subscriptions can fail while established. Failures are reported through an error channel. It receives a value if there is an issue with the subscription (e.g. the network connection delivering the events has been closed). Only one value will ever be sent. The error channel is closed when the subscription ends successfully (i.e. when the source of events is closed). It is also closed when Unsubscribe is called. The Unsubscribe method cancels the sending of events. You must call Unsubscribe in all cases to ensure that resources related to the subscription are released. It can be called any number of times.

declarations.name: SubscriptionScope
declarations.doc: SubscriptionScope provides a facility to unsubscribe multiple subscriptions at once. For code that handle more than one subscription, a scope can be used to conveniently unsubscribe all of them with a single call. The example demonstrates a typical use in a larger program. The zero value is ready to use.

declarations.doc: InputLine writes the given text to the child's stdin. This method can also be called from an expect template, e.g.: geth.expect(`Passphrase: {{.InputLine "password"}}`)

declarations.name: Output
declarations.doc: Output reads all output from stdout, and returns the data.

declarations.name: Run
declarations.doc: Run exec's the current binary using name as argv[0] which will trigger the reexec init function for that name (e.g. "geth-test" in cmd/geth/run_test.go)

declarations.name: StderrText
declarations.doc: StderrText returns any stderr output written so far. The returned text holds all log lines after ExpectExit has returned.

declarations.name: runeTee
declarations.doc: runeTee collects text read through it into buf.

declarations.name: testlogger
declarations.doc: testlogger logs all written lines via t.Log and also collects them for later inspection.

declarations.name: BacktraceAt
declarations.doc: BacktraceAt sets the log backtrace location. See package log for details on the pattern syntax.

declarations.name: BlockProfile
declarations.doc: BlockProfile turns on goroutine profiling for nsec seconds and writes profile data to file. It uses a profile rate of 1 for most accurate information. If a different rate is desired, set the rate and write the profile manually.

declarations.name: CpuProfile
declarations.doc: CpuProfile turns on CPU profiling for nsec seconds and writes profile data to file.

declarations.name: EtcdDelete
declarations.doc: Remove an etcd key / value pair

declarations.name: EtcdGet
declarations.doc: Get etcd key's value

declarations.name: EtcdPut
declarations.doc: Remove an etcd key / value pair

declarations.name: FreeOSMemory
declarations.doc: FreeOSMemory forces a garbage collection.

declarations.name: GcStats
declarations.doc: GcStats returns GC statistics.

declarations.name: GoTrace
declarations.doc: GoTrace turns on tracing for nsec seconds and writes trace data to file.

declarations.name: MemStats
declarations.doc: MemStats returns detailed runtime memory statistics.

declarations.name: MutexProfile
declarations.doc: MutexProfile turns on mutex profiling for nsec seconds and writes profile data to file. It uses a profile rate of 1 for most accurate information. If a different rate is desired, set the rate and write the profile manually.

declarations.name: SetBlockProfileRate
declarations.doc: SetBlockProfileRate sets the rate of goroutine block profile data collection. rate 0 disables block profiling.

declarations.name: SetGCPercent
declarations.doc: SetGCPercent sets the garbage collection target percentage. It returns the previous setting. A negative value disables GC.

declarations.name: SetMutexProfileFraction
declarations.doc: SetMutexProfileFraction sets the rate of mutex profiling.

declarations.name: Stacks
declarations.doc: Stacks returns a printed representation of the stacks of all goroutines. It also permits the following optional filters to be used: - filter: boolean expression of packages to filter for

declarations.name: StartCPUProfile
declarations.doc: StartCPUProfile turns on CPU profiling, writing to the given file.

declarations.name: StopCPUProfile
declarations.doc: StopCPUProfile stops an ongoing CPU profile.

declarations.name: Verbosity
declarations.doc: Verbosity sets the log verbosity ceiling. The verbosity of individual packages and source files can be raised using Vmodule.

declarations.name: Vmodule
declarations.doc: Vmodule sets the log verbosity pattern. See package log for details on the pattern syntax.

declarations.name: WriteBlockProfile
declarations.doc: WriteBlockProfile writes a goroutine blocking profile to the given file.

declarations.name: WriteMemProfile
declarations.doc: WriteMemProfile writes an allocation profile to the given file. Note that the profiling rate cannot be set through the API, it must be set on the command line.

declarations.name: WriteMutexProfile
declarations.doc: WriteMutexProfile writes a goroutine blocking profile to the given file.

declarations.name: expandHome
declarations.doc: expands home directory in file paths. ~someuser/tmp will not be expanded.

declarations.name: HandlerT
declarations.doc: HandlerT implements the debugging API. Do not create values of this type, use the one in the Handler variable instead.

declarations.name: Exit
declarations.doc: Exit stops all running profiles, flushing their output to the respective file.

declarations.name: Setup
declarations.doc: Setup initializes profiling and logging based on the CLI flags. It should be called as early as possible in the program.

declarations.name: LoudPanic
declarations.doc: LoudPanic panics in a way that gets all goroutine stacks printed on stderr.

declarations.name: LoudPanic
declarations.doc: LoudPanic panics in a way that gets all goroutine stacks printed on stderr.

declarations.name: StartGoTrace
declarations.doc: StartGoTrace turns on tracing, writing to the given file.

declarations.name: StopGoTrace
declarations.doc: StopTrace stops an ongoing trace.

declarations.name: LockAddr
declarations.doc: LockAddr locks an account's mutex. This is used to prevent another tx getting the same nonce until the lock is released. The mutex prevents the (an identical nonce) from being read again during the time that the first transaction is being signed.

declarations.name: UnlockAddr
declarations.doc: UnlockAddr unlocks the mutex of the given account.

declarations.name: lock
declarations.doc: lock returns the lock of the given address.

declarations.name: AccessList
declarations.doc: AccessList creates an access list for the given transaction. If the accesslist creation fails an error is returned. If the transaction itself fails, an vmErr is returned.

declarations.name: Accounts
declarations.doc: Accounts returns the collection of accounts this node manages

declarations.name: Apply
declarations.doc: Apply overrides the fields of specified accounts into the given state.

declarations.name: BlockNumber
declarations.doc: BlockNumber returns the block number of the chain head.

declarations.name: Call
declarations.doc: Call executes the given transaction on the state for the given block number. Additionally, the caller can specify a batch of contract for fields overriding. Note, this function doesn't make and changes in the state/blockchain and is useful to execute and retrieve values.

declarations.name: ChainId
declarations.doc: ChainId is the EIP-155 replay-protection chain id for the current ethereum chain config.

declarations.name: ChaindbCompact
declarations.doc: ChaindbCompact flattens the entire key-value database into a single level, removing all unused slots and merging all keys.

declarations.name: ChaindbProperty
declarations.doc: ChaindbProperty returns leveldb properties of the key-value database.

declarations.name: Content
declarations.doc: Content returns the transactions contained within the transaction pool.

declarations.name: ContentFrom
declarations.doc: ContentFrom returns the transactions contained within the transaction pool.

declarations.name: CreateAccessList
declarations.doc: CreateAccessList creates a EIP-2930 type AccessList for the given transaction. Reexec and BlockNrOrHash can be specified to create the accessList on top of a certain state.

declarations.name: DeriveAccount
declarations.doc: DeriveAccount requests a HD wallet to derive a new account, optionally pinning it for later reuse.

declarations.name: EcRecover
declarations.doc: EcRecover returns the address for the account that was used to create the signature. Note, this function is compatible with eth_sign and personal_sign. As such it recovers the address of: hash = keccak256("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n"${message length}${message}) addr = ecrecover(hash, signature) Note, the signature must conform to the secp256k1 curve R, S and V values, where the V value must be 27 or 28 for legacy reasons. https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/wiki/Management-APIs#personal_ecRecover

declarations.name: EdPubKey
declarations.doc: Get ED25519 Public Key from address (same private key)

declarations.name: ErrorCode
declarations.doc: ErrorCode returns the JSON error code for a revertal. See: https://github.com/ethereum/wiki/wiki/JSON-RPC-Error-Codes-Improvement-Proposal

declarations.name: ErrorData
declarations.doc: ErrorData returns the hex encoded revert reason.

declarations.name: EstimateGas
declarations.doc: EstimateGas returns an estimate of the amount of gas needed to execute the given transaction against the current pending block.

declarations.name: FillTransaction
declarations.doc: FillTransaction fills the defaults (nonce, gas, gasPrice or 1559 fields) on a given unsigned transaction, and returns it to the caller for further processing (signing + broadcast).

declarations.name: GasPrice
declarations.doc: GasPrice returns a suggestion for a gas price for legacy transactions.

declarations.name: Genesis
declarations.doc: return genesis.json if available

declarations.name: GetBalance
declarations.doc: GetBalance returns the amount of wei for the given address in the state of the given block number. The rpc.LatestBlockNumber and rpc.PendingBlockNumber meta block numbers are also allowed.

declarations.name: GetBlockByHash
declarations.doc: GetBlockByHash returns the requested block. When fullTx is true all transactions in the block are returned in full detail, otherwise only the transaction hash is returned.

declarations.name: GetBlockByNumber
declarations.doc: GetBlockByNumber returns the requested canonical block. - When blockNr is -1 the chain head is returned. - When blockNr is -2 the pending chain head is returned. - When fullTx is true all transactions in the block are returned, otherwise only the transaction hash is returned.

declarations.name: GetBlockRlp
declarations.doc: GetBlockRlp retrieves the RLP encoded for of a single block.

declarations.name: GetBlockTransactionCountByHash
declarations.doc: GetBlockTransactionCountByHash returns the number of transactions in the block with the given hash.

declarations.name: GetBlockTransactionCountByNumber
declarations.doc: GetBlockTransactionCountByNumber returns the number of transactions in the block with the given block number.

declarations.name: GetCode
declarations.doc: GetCode returns the code stored at the given address in the state for the given block number.

declarations.name: GetHeaderByHash
declarations.doc: GetHeaderByHash returns the requested header by hash.

declarations.name: GetHeaderByNumber
declarations.doc: GetHeaderByNumber returns the requested canonical block header. * When blockNr is -1 the chain head is returned. * When blockNr is -2 the pending chain head is returned.

declarations.name: GetHeaderRlp
declarations.doc: GetHeaderRlp retrieves the RLP encoded for of a single header.

declarations.name: GetProof
declarations.doc: GetProof returns the Merkle-proof for a given account and optionally some storage keys.

declarations.name: GetRawReceipts
declarations.doc: GetRawReceipts retrieves the binary-encoded raw receipts of a single block.

declarations.name: GetRawTransactionByBlockHashAndIndex
declarations.doc: GetRawTransactionByBlockHashAndIndex returns the bytes of the transaction for the given block hash and index.

declarations.name: GetRawTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex
declarations.doc: GetRawTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex returns the bytes of the transaction for the given block number and index.

declarations.name: GetRawTransactionByHash
declarations.doc: GetRawTransactionByHash returns the bytes of the transaction for the given hash.

declarations.name: GetReceiptsByHash
declarations.doc: GetBlockReceipts returns all the transaction receipts for the given block hash.

declarations.name: GetStorageAt
declarations.doc: GetStorageAt returns the storage from the state at the given address, key and block number. The rpc.LatestBlockNumber and rpc.PendingBlockNumber meta block numbers are also allowed.

declarations.name: GetTransactionByBlockHashAndIndex
declarations.doc: GetTransactionByBlockHashAndIndex returns the transaction for the given block hash and index.

declarations.name: GetTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex
declarations.doc: GetTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex returns the transaction for the given block number and index.

declarations.name: GetTransactionByHash
declarations.doc: GetTransactionByHash returns the transaction for the given hash

declarations.name: GetTransactionCount
declarations.doc: GetTransactionCount returns the number of transactions the given address has sent for the given block number

declarations.name: GetTransactionReceipt
declarations.doc: GetTransactionReceipt returns the transaction receipt for the given transaction hash.

declarations.name: GetUncleByBlockHashAndIndex
declarations.doc: GetUncleByBlockHashAndIndex returns the uncle block for the given block hash and index.

declarations.name: GetUncleByBlockNumberAndIndex
declarations.doc: GetUncleByBlockNumberAndIndex returns the uncle block for the given block hash and index.

declarations.name: GetUncleCountByBlockHash
declarations.doc: GetUncleCountByBlockHash returns number of uncles in the block for the given block hash

declarations.name: GetUncleCountByBlockNumber
declarations.doc: GetUncleCountByBlockNumber returns number of uncles in the block for the given block number

declarations.name: ImportRawKey
declarations.doc: ImportRawKey stores the given hex encoded ECDSA key into the key directory, encrypting it with the passphrase.

declarations.name: InitializeWallet
declarations.doc: InitializeWallet initializes a new wallet at the provided URL, by generating and returning a new private key.

declarations.name: Inspect
declarations.doc: Inspect retrieves the content of the transaction pool and flattens it into an easily inspectable list.

declarations.name: ListAccounts
declarations.doc: ListAccounts will return a list of addresses for accounts this node manages.

declarations.name: ListWallets
declarations.doc: ListWallets will return a list of wallets this node manages.

declarations.name: Listening
declarations.doc: Listening returns an indication if the node is listening for network connections.

declarations.name: LockAccount
declarations.doc: LockAccount will lock the account associated with the given address when it's unlocked.

declarations.name: MaxPriorityFeePerGas
declarations.doc: MaxPriorityFeePerGas returns a suggestion for a gas tip cap for dynamic fee transactions.

declarations.name: NewAccount
declarations.doc: NewAccount will create a new account and returns the address for the new account.

declarations.name: NewPrivateAccountAPI
declarations.doc: NewPrivateAccountAPI create a new PrivateAccountAPI.

declarations.name: NewPrivateDebugAPI
declarations.doc: NewPrivateDebugAPI creates a new API definition for the private debug methods of the Ethereum service.

declarations.name: NewPublicAccountAPI
declarations.doc: NewPublicAccountAPI creates a new PublicAccountAPI.

declarations.name: NewPublicBlockChainAPI
declarations.doc: NewPublicBlockChainAPI creates a new Ethereum blockchain API.

declarations.name: NewPublicDebugAPI
declarations.doc: NewPublicDebugAPI creates a new API definition for the public debug methods of the Ethereum service.

declarations.name: NewPublicEthereumAPI
declarations.doc: NewPublicEthereumAPI creates a new Ethereum protocol API.

declarations.name: NewPublicNetAPI
declarations.doc: NewPublicNetAPI creates a new net API instance.

declarations.name: NewPublicTransactionPoolAPI
declarations.doc: NewPublicTransactionPoolAPI creates a new RPC service with methods specific for the transaction pool.

declarations.name: NewPublicTxPoolAPI
declarations.doc: NewPublicTxPoolAPI creates a new tx pool service that gives information about the transaction pool.

declarations.name: OpenWallet
declarations.doc: OpenWallet initiates a hardware wallet opening procedure, establishing a USB connection and attempting to authenticate via the provided passphrase. Note, the method may return an extra challenge requiring a second open (e.g. the Trezor PIN matrix challenge).

declarations.name: PeerCount
declarations.doc: PeerCount returns the number of connected peers

declarations.name: PendingTransactions
declarations.doc: PendingTransactions returns the transactions that are in the transaction pool and have a from address that is one of the accounts this node manages.

declarations.name: PrintBlock
declarations.doc: PrintBlock retrieves a block and returns its pretty printed form.

declarations.name: Prove
declarations.doc: VRF Prove

declarations.name: RPCMarshalBlock
declarations.doc: RPCMarshalBlock converts the given block to the RPC output which depends on fullTx. If inclTx is true transactions are returned. When fullTx is true the returned block contains full transaction details, otherwise it will only contain transaction hashes.

declarations.name: RPCMarshalHeader
declarations.doc: RPCMarshalHeader converts the given header to the RPC output .

declarations.name: Resend
declarations.doc: Resend accepts an existing transaction and a new gas price and limit. It will remove the given transaction from the pool and reinsert it with the new gas price and limit.

declarations.name: SeedHash
declarations.doc: SeedHash retrieves the seed hash of a block.

declarations.name: SendRawTransaction
declarations.doc: SendRawTransaction will add the signed transaction to the transaction pool. The sender is responsible for signing the transaction and using the correct nonce.

declarations.name: SendRawTransactions
declarations.doc: SendRawTransactions will add the signed transactions to the transaction pool. The sender is responsible for signing the transactions and using the correct nonces.

declarations.name: SendTransaction
declarations.doc: SendTransaction will create a transaction from the given arguments and tries to sign it with the key associated with args.From. If the given passwd isn't able to decrypt the key it fails.

declarations.name: SendTransaction
declarations.doc: SendTransaction creates a transaction for the given argument, sign it and submit it to the transaction pool.

declarations.name: SetHead
declarations.doc: SetHead rewinds the head of the blockchain to a previous block.

declarations.name: Sign
declarations.doc: Sign calculates an Ethereum ECDSA signature for: keccack256("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n" + len(message) + message)) Note, the produced signature conforms to the secp256k1 curve R, S and V values, where the V value will be 27 or 28 for legacy reasons. The key used to calculate the signature is decrypted with the given password. https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/wiki/Management-APIs#personal_sign

declarations.name: Sign
declarations.doc: Sign calculates an ECDSA signature for: keccack256("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n" + len(message) + message). Note, the produced signature conforms to the secp256k1 curve R, S and V values, where the V value will be 27 or 28 for legacy reasons. The account associated with addr must be unlocked. https://github.com/ethereum/wiki/wiki/JSON-RPC#eth_sign

declarations.name: SignAndSendTransaction
declarations.doc: SignAndSendTransaction was renamed to SendTransaction. This method is deprecated and will be removed in the future. It primary goal is to give clients time to update.

declarations.name: SignRawFeeDelegateTransaction
declarations.doc: fee delegation SignRawFeeDelegateTransaction will create a transaction from the given arguments and tries to sign it with the key associated with args.feePayer. If the given passwd isn't able to decrypt the key it fails. The transaction is returned in RLP-form, not broadcast to other nodes

declarations.name: SignRawFeeDelegateTransaction
declarations.doc: fee delegation SignRawFeeDelegateTransaction will sign the given feeDelegate transaction with the feePayer account. The node needs to have the private key of the account corresponding with the given from address and it needs to be unlocked.

declarations.name: SignTransaction
declarations.doc: SignTransaction will create a transaction from the given arguments and tries to sign it with the key associated with args.From. If the given passwd isn't able to decrypt the key it fails. The transaction is returned in RLP-form, not broadcast to other nodes

declarations.name: SignTransaction
declarations.doc: SignTransaction will sign the given transaction with the from account. The node needs to have the private key of the account corresponding with the given from address and it needs to be unlocked.

declarations.name: Status
declarations.doc: Status returns the number of pending and queued transaction in the pool.

declarations.name: SubmitTransaction
declarations.doc: SubmitTransaction is a helper function that submits tx to txPool and logs a message.

declarations.name: Syncing
declarations.doc: Syncing returns false in case the node is currently not syncing with the network. It can be up to date or has not yet received the latest block headers from its pears. In case it is synchronizing: - startingBlock: block number this node started to synchronise from - currentBlock: block number this node is currently importing - highestBlock: block number of the highest block header this node has received from peers - pulledStates: number of state entries processed until now - knownStates: number of known state entries that still need to be pulled

declarations.name: UnlockAccount
declarations.doc: UnlockAccount will unlock the account associated with the given address with the given password for duration seconds. If duration is nil it will use a default of 300 seconds. It returns an indication if the account was unlocked.

declarations.name: Unpair
declarations.doc: Unpair deletes a pairing between wallet and geth.

declarations.name: Verify
declarations.doc: VRF Verify

declarations.name: Version
declarations.doc: Version returns the current ethereum protocol version.

declarations.name: checkTxFee
declarations.doc: checkTxFee is an internal function used to check whether the fee of the given transaction is _reasonable_(under the cap).

declarations.name: fetchKeystore
declarations.doc: fetchKeystore retrieves the encrypted keystore from the account manager.

declarations.name: newRPCPendingTransaction
declarations.doc: newRPCPendingTransaction returns a pending transaction that will serialize to the RPC representation

declarations.name: newRPCRawTransactionFromBlockIndex
declarations.doc: newRPCRawTransactionFromBlockIndex returns the bytes of a transaction given a block and a transaction index.

declarations.name: newRPCTransaction
declarations.doc: newRPCTransaction returns a transaction that will serialize to the RPC representation, with the given location metadata set (if available).

declarations.name: newRPCTransactionFromBlockHash
declarations.doc: newRPCTransactionFromBlockHash returns a transaction that will serialize to the RPC representation.

declarations.name: newRPCTransactionFromBlockIndex
declarations.doc: newRPCTransactionFromBlockIndex returns a transaction that will serialize to the RPC representation.

declarations.name: rpcMarshalBlock
declarations.doc: rpcMarshalBlock uses the generalized output filler, then adds the total difficulty field, which requires a `PublicBlockchainAPI`.

declarations.name: rpcMarshalHeader
declarations.doc: rpcMarshalHeader uses the generalized output filler, then adds the total difficulty field, which requires a `PublicBlockchainAPI`.

declarations.name: sign
declarations.doc: sign is a helper function that signs a transaction with the private key of the given address.

declarations.name: signTransaction
declarations.doc: signTransaction sets defaults and signs the given transaction NOTE: the caller needs to ensure that the nonceLock is held, if applicable, and release it after the transaction has been submitted to the tx pool

declarations.name: toHexSlice
declarations.doc: toHexSlice creates a slice of hex-strings based on []byte.

declarations.name: AccountResult
declarations.doc: Result structs for GetProof

declarations.name: OverrideAccount
declarations.doc: OverrideAccount indicates the overriding fields of account during the execution of a message call. Note, state and stateDiff can't be specified at the same time. If state is set, message execution will only use the data in the given state. Otherwise if statDiff is set, all diff will be applied first and then execute the call message.

declarations.name: PrivateAccountAPI
declarations.doc: PrivateAccountAPI provides an API to access accounts managed by this node. It offers methods to create, (un)lock en list accounts. Some methods accept passwords and are therefore considered private by default.

declarations.name: PrivateDebugAPI
declarations.doc: PrivateDebugAPI is the collection of Ethereum APIs exposed over the private debugging endpoint.

declarations.name: PublicAccountAPI
declarations.doc: PublicAccountAPI provides an API to access accounts managed by this node. It offers only methods that can retrieve accounts.

declarations.name: PublicBlockChainAPI
declarations.doc: PublicBlockChainAPI provides an API to access the Ethereum blockchain. It offers only methods that operate on public data that is freely available to anyone.

declarations.name: PublicDebugAPI
declarations.doc: PublicDebugAPI is the collection of Ethereum APIs exposed over the public debugging endpoint.

declarations.name: PublicEthereumAPI
declarations.doc: PublicEthereumAPI provides an API to access Ethereum related information. It offers only methods that operate on public data that is freely available to anyone.

declarations.name: PublicNetAPI
declarations.doc: PublicNetAPI offers network related RPC methods

declarations.name: PublicTransactionPoolAPI
declarations.doc: PublicTransactionPoolAPI exposes methods for the RPC interface

declarations.name: PublicTxPoolAPI
declarations.doc: PublicTxPoolAPI offers and API for the transaction pool. It only operates on data that is non confidential.

declarations.name: RPCTransaction
declarations.doc: RPCTransaction represents a transaction that will serialize to the RPC representation of a transaction

declarations.name: SignTransactionResult
declarations.doc: SignTransactionResult represents a RLP encoded signed transaction.

declarations.name: StateOverride
declarations.doc: StateOverride is the collection of overridden accounts.

declarations.name: accessListResult
declarations.doc: accessListResult returns an optional accesslist Its the result of the `debug_createAccessList` RPC call. It contains an error if the transaction itself failed.

declarations.name: rawWallet
declarations.doc: rawWallet is a JSON representation of an accounts.Wallet interface, with its data contents extracted into plain fields.

declarations.name: revertError
declarations.doc: revertError is an API error that encompassas an EVM revertal with JSON error code and a binary data blob.

declarations.name: Backend
declarations.doc: Backend interface provides the common API services (that are provided by both full and light clients) with access to necessary functions.

declarations.name: DbAncient
declarations.doc: DbAncient retrieves an ancient binary blob from the append-only immutable files. It is a mapping to the `AncientReaderOp.Ancient` method

declarations.name: DbAncients
declarations.doc: DbAncients returns the ancient item numbers in the ancient store. It is a mapping to the `AncientReaderOp.Ancients` method

declarations.name: DbGet
declarations.doc: DbGet returns the raw value of a key stored in the database.

declarations.name: ToMessage
declarations.doc: ToMessage converts the transaction arguments to the Message type used by the core evm. This method is used in calls and traces that do not require a real live transaction.

declarations.name: ToTransaction
declarations.doc: ToTransaction converts the arguments to a transaction. This assumes that setDefaults has been called.

declarations.name: data
declarations.doc: data retrieves the transaction calldata. Input field is preferred.

declarations.name: from
declarations.doc: from retrieves the transaction sender address.

declarations.name: setDefaults
declarations.doc: setDefaults fills in default values for unspecified tx fields.

declarations.name: toTransaction
declarations.doc: toTransaction converts the arguments to a transaction. This assumes that setDefaults has been called.

declarations.name: TransactionArgs
declarations.doc: TransactionArgs represents the arguments to construct a new transaction or a message call.

declarations.name: NewApp
declarations.doc: NewApp creates an app with sane defaults.

declarations.name: ByCategory
declarations.doc: ByCategory sorts an array of FlagGroup by Name in the order defined in AppHelpFlagGroups.

declarations.name: FlagGroup
declarations.doc: FlagGroup is a collection of flags belonging to a single topic.

declarations.name: HelpData
declarations.doc: HelpData is a one shot struct to pass to the usage template

declarations.name: TestAccountManagement
declarations.doc: Tests that the account management snippets work correctly.

declarations.name: CompleteKeywords
declarations.doc: CompleteKeywords returns potential continuations for the given line. Since line is evaluated, callers need to make sure that evaluating line does not have side effects.

declarations.name: Compile
declarations.doc: Compile compiles and then runs a piece of JS code.

declarations.name: Do
declarations.doc: Do executes the given function on the JS event loop. When the runtime is stopped, fn will not execute.

declarations.name: Evaluate
declarations.doc: Evaluate executes code and pretty prints the result to the specified output stream.

declarations.name: Exec
declarations.doc: Exec(file) loads and runs the contents of a file if a relative path is given, the jsre's assetPath is used

declarations.name: Interrupt
declarations.doc: Interrupt stops the current JS evaluation.

declarations.name: MakeCallback
declarations.doc: MakeCallback turns the given function into a function that's callable by JS.

declarations.name: New
declarations.doc: runtime must be stopped with Stop() after use and cannot be used after stopping

declarations.name: Run
declarations.doc: Run runs a piece of JS code.

declarations.name: Set
declarations.doc: Set assigns value v to a variable in the JS environment.

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop terminates the event loop, optionally waiting for all timers to expire.

declarations.name: loadFile
declarations.doc: loadFile loads a file content as string

declarations.name: loadScript
declarations.doc: loadScript loads and executes a JS file.

declarations.name: msleep
declarations.doc: msleep sleeps in ms resolution

declarations.name: randomSource
declarations.doc: randomSource returns a pseudo random value generator.

declarations.name: runEventLoop
declarations.doc: Exported functions always access the vm through the event queue. You can call the functions of the goja vm directly to circumvent the queue. These functions should be used if and only if running a routine that was already called from JS through an RPC call.

declarations.name: Call

declarations.doc: gfLoop starts an event loop which updates the global cost factor which is calculated as a weighted average of the average estimate / serving time ratio. The applied weight equals the serving time if gfUsage is over a threshold, zero otherwise. gfUsage is the recent average serving time per time unit in an exponential moving window. This ensures that statistics are collected only under high-load circumstances where the measured serving times are relevant. The total recharge parameter of the flow control system which controls the total allowed serving time per second but nominated in cost units, should also be scaled with the cost factor and is also updated by this loop.

declarations.name: costTracker
declarations.doc: costTracker is responsible for calculating costs and cost estimates on the server side. It continuously updates the global cost factor which is defined as the number of cost units per nanosecond of serving time in a single thread. It is based on statistics collected during serving requests in high-load periods and practically acts as a one-dimension request price scaling factor over the pre-defined cost estimate table. The reason for dynamically maintaining the global factor on the server side is: the estimated time cost of the request is fixed(hardcoded) but the configuration of the machine running the server is really different. Therefore, the request serving time in different machine will vary greatly. And also, the request serving time in same machine may vary greatly with different request pressure. In order to more effectively limit resources, we apply the global factor to serving time to make the result as close as possible to the estimated time cost no matter the server is slow or fast. And also we scale the totalRecharge with global factor so that fast server can serve more requests than estimation and slow server can reduce request pressure. Instead of scaling the cost values, the real value of cost units is changed by applying the factor to the serving times. This is more convenient because the changes in the cost factor can be applied immediately without always notifying the clients about the changed cost tables.

Request order should be preserved but the callback itself should not block until it is sent because other peers might still be able to receive requests while one of them is blocking. Instead, the returned function is put in the peer's send queue.

declarations.name: fetchHeaders
declarations.doc: fetchHeaders keeps retrieving headers concurrently from the number requested, until no more are returned, potentially throttling on the way. To facilitate concurrency but still protect against malicious nodes sending bad headers, we construct a header chain skeleton using the "origin" peer we are syncing with, and fill in the missing headers using anyone else. Headers from other peers are only accepted if they map cleanly to the skeleton. If no one can fill in the skeleton - not even the origin peer - it's assumed invalid and the origin is dropped.

declarations.name: fetchParts
declarations.doc: fetchParts iteratively downloads scheduled block parts, taking any available peers, reserving a chunk of fetch requests for each, waiting for delivery and also periodically checking for timeouts. As the scheduling/timeout logic mostly is the same for all downloaded data types, this method is used by each for data gathering and is instrumented with various callbacks to handle the slight differences between processing them. The instrumentation parameters: - errCancel: error type to return if the fetch operation is cancelled (mostly makes logging nicer) - deliveryCh: channel from which to retrieve downloaded data packets (merged from all concurrent peers) - deliver: processing callback to deliver data packets into type specific download queues (usually within `queue`) - wakeCh: notification channel for waking the fetcher when new tasks are available (or sync completed) - expire: task callback method to abort requests that took too long and return the faulty peers (traffic shaping) - pending: task callback for the number of requests still needing download (detect completion/non-completability) - inFlight: task callback for the number of in-progress requests (wait for all active downloads to finish) - throttle: task callback to check if the processing queue is full and activate throttling (bound memory use) - reserve: task callback to reserve new download tasks to a particular peer (also signals partial completions) - fetchHook: tester callback to notify of new tasks being initiated (allows testing the scheduling logic) - fetch: network callback to actually send a particular download request to a physical remote peer - cancel: task callback to abort an in-flight download request and allow rescheduling it (in case of lost peer) - capacity: network callback to retrieve the estimated type-specific bandwidth capacity of a peer (traffic shaping) - idle: network callback to retrieve the currently (type specific) idle peers that can be assigned tasks - setIdle: network callback to set a peer back to idle and update its estimated capacity (traffic shaping) - kind: textual label of the type being downloaded to display in log messages

declarations.name: fillHeaderSkeleton
declarations.doc: fillHeaderSkeleton concurrently retrieves headers from all our available peers and maps them to the provided skeleton header chain. Any partial results from the beginning of the skeleton is (if possible) forwarded immediately to the header processor to keep the rest of the pipeline full even in the case of header stalls. The method returns the entire filled skeleton and also the number of headers already forwarded for processing.

In the rare scenario when we ended up on a long reorganisation (i.e. none of the head links match), we do a binary search to find the common ancestor.
