declarations.doc: Lacks retrieves whether the hash of a blockchain item is on the peers lacking list (i.e. whether we know that the peer does not have it).

declarations.name: Len
declarations.doc: Len returns if the current number of peers in the set.

declarations.name: MarkLacking
declarations.doc: MarkLacking appends a new entity to the set of items (blocks, receipts, states) that a peer is known not to have (i.e. have been requested before). If the set reaches its maximum allowed capacity, items are randomly dropped off.

declarations.name: NodeDataCapacity
declarations.doc: NodeDataCapacity retrieves the peers state download allowance based on its previously discovered throughput.

declarations.name: NodeDataIdlePeers
declarations.doc: NodeDataIdlePeers retrieves a flat list of all the currently node-data-idle peers within the active peer set, ordered by their reputation.

declarations.name: Peer
declarations.doc: Peer retrieves the registered peer with the given id.

declarations.name: ReceiptCapacity
declarations.doc: ReceiptCapacity retrieves the peers receipt download allowance based on its previously discovered throughput.

declarations.name: ReceiptIdlePeers
declarations.doc: ReceiptIdlePeers retrieves a flat list of all the currently receipt-idle peers within the active peer set, ordered by their reputation.

declarations.name: Register
declarations.doc: Register injects a new peer into the working set, or returns an error if the peer is already known. The method also sets the starting throughput values of the new peer to the average of all existing peers, to give it a realistic chance of being used for data retrievals.

declarations.name: Reset
declarations.doc: Reset clears the internal state of a peer entity.

declarations.name: Reset
declarations.doc: Reset iterates over the current peer set, and resets each of the known peers to prepare for a next batch of block retrieval.

declarations.name: SetBodiesIdle
declarations.doc: SetBodiesIdle sets the peer to idle, allowing it to execute block body retrieval requests. Its estimated body retrieval throughput is updated with that measured just now.

declarations.name: SetHeadersIdle
declarations.doc: SetHeadersIdle sets the peer to idle, allowing it to execute new header retrieval requests. Its estimated header retrieval throughput is updated with that measured just now.

declarations.name: SetNodeDataIdle
declarations.doc: SetNodeDataIdle sets the peer to idle, allowing it to execute new state trie data retrieval requests. Its estimated state retrieval throughput is updated with that measured just now.

declarations.name: SetReceiptsIdle
declarations.doc: SetReceiptsIdle sets the peer to idle, allowing it to execute new receipt retrieval requests. Its estimated receipt retrieval throughput is updated with that measured just now.

declarations.name: SubscribeNewPeers
declarations.doc: SubscribeNewPeers subscribes to peer arrival events.

declarations.name: SubscribePeerDrops
declarations.doc: SubscribePeerDrops subscribes to peer departure events.

declarations.name: Unregister
declarations.doc: Unregister removes a remote peer from the active set, disabling any further actions to/from that particular entity.

declarations.name: idlePeers
declarations.doc: idlePeers retrieves a flat list of all currently idle peers satisfying the protocol version constraints, using the provided function to check idleness. The resulting set of peers are sorted by their capacity.

declarations.name: newPeerConnection
declarations.doc: newPeerConnection creates a new downloader peer.

declarations.name: newPeerSet
declarations.doc: newPeerSet creates a new peer set top track the active download sources.

declarations.name: LightPeer
declarations.doc: LightPeer encapsulates the methods required to synchronise with a remote light peer.

declarations.name: Peer
declarations.doc: Peer encapsulates the methods required to synchronise with a remote full peer.

declarations.name: lightPeerWrapper
declarations.doc: lightPeerWrapper wraps a LightPeer struct, stubbing out the Peer-only methods.

declarations.name: peerCapacitySort
declarations.doc: peerCapacitySort implements sort.Interface. It sorts peer connections by capacity (descending).

declarations.name: peerConnection
declarations.doc: peerConnection represents an active peer from which hashes and blocks are retrieved.

declarations.name: peerSet
declarations.doc: peerSet represents the collection of active peer participating in the chain download procedure.

declarations.name: AllDone
declarations.doc: AllDone checks if item is done.

declarations.name: CancelBodies
declarations.doc: CancelBodies aborts a body fetch request, returning all pending headers to the task queue.

declarations.name: CancelHeaders
declarations.doc: CancelHeaders aborts a fetch request, returning all pending skeleton indexes to the queue.

declarations.name: CancelReceipts
declarations.doc: CancelReceipts aborts a body fetch request, returning all pending headers to the task queue.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close marks the end of the sync, unblocking Results. It may be called even if the queue is already closed.

declarations.name: DeliverBodies
declarations.doc: DeliverBodies injects a block body retrieval response into the results queue. The method returns the number of blocks bodies accepted from the delivery and also wakes any threads waiting for data delivery.

declarations.name: DeliverHeaders
declarations.doc: DeliverHeaders injects a header retrieval response into the header results cache. This method either accepts all headers it received, or none of them if they do not map correctly to the skeleton. If the headers are accepted, the method makes an attempt to deliver the set of ready headers to the processor to keep the pipeline full. However it will not block to prevent stalling other pending deliveries.

declarations.name: DeliverReceipts
declarations.doc: DeliverReceipts injects a receipt retrieval response into the results queue. The method returns the number of transaction receipts accepted from the delivery and also wakes any threads waiting for data delivery.

declarations.name: Done
declarations.doc: Done checks if the given type is done already

declarations.name: ExpireBodies
declarations.doc: ExpireBodies checks for in flight block body requests that exceeded a timeout allowance, canceling them and returning the responsible peers for penalisation.

declarations.name: ExpireHeaders
declarations.doc: ExpireHeaders checks for in flight requests that exceeded a timeout allowance, canceling them and returning the responsible peers for penalisation.

declarations.name: ExpireReceipts
declarations.doc: ExpireReceipts checks for in flight receipt requests that exceeded a timeout allowance, canceling them and returning the responsible peers for penalisation.

declarations.name: Idle
declarations.doc: Idle returns if the queue is fully idle or has some data still inside.

declarations.name: InFlightBlocks
declarations.doc: InFlightBlocks retrieves whether there are block fetch requests currently in flight.

declarations.name: InFlightHeaders
declarations.doc: InFlightHeaders retrieves whether there are header fetch requests currently in flight.

declarations.name: InFlightReceipts
declarations.doc: InFlightReceipts retrieves whether there are receipt fetch requests currently in flight.

declarations.name: PendingBlocks
declarations.doc: PendingBlocks retrieves the number of block (body) requests pending for retrieval.

declarations.name: PendingHeaders
declarations.doc: PendingHeaders retrieves the number of header requests pending for retrieval.

declarations.name: PendingReceipts
declarations.doc: PendingReceipts retrieves the number of block receipts pending for retrieval.

declarations.name: Prepare
declarations.doc: Prepare configures the result cache to allow accepting and caching inbound fetch results.

declarations.name: ReserveBodies
declarations.doc: ReserveBodies reserves a set of body fetches for the given peer, skipping any previously failed downloads. Beside the next batch of needed fetches, it also returns a flag whether empty blocks were queued requiring processing.

declarations.name: ReserveHeaders
declarations.doc: ReserveHeaders reserves a set of headers for the given peer, skipping any previously failed batches.

declarations.name: ReserveReceipts
declarations.doc: ReserveReceipts reserves a set of receipt fetches for the given peer, skipping any previously failed downloads. Beside the next batch of needed fetches, it also returns a flag whether empty receipts were queued requiring importing.

declarations.name: Reset
declarations.doc: Reset clears out the queue contents.

declarations.name: Results
declarations.doc: Results retrieves and permanently removes a batch of fetch results from the cache. the result slice will be empty if the queue has been closed. Results can be called concurrently with Deliver and Schedule, but assumes that there are not two simultaneous callers to Results

declarations.name: RetrieveHeaders
declarations.doc: RetrieveHeaders retrieves the header chain assemble based on the scheduled skeleton.

declarations.name: Revoke
declarations.doc: Revoke cancels all pending requests belonging to a given peer. This method is meant to be called during a peer drop to quickly reassign owned data fetches to remaining nodes.

declarations.name: Schedule
declarations.doc: Schedule adds a set of headers for the download queue for scheduling, returning the new headers encountered.

declarations.name: ScheduleSkeleton
declarations.doc: ScheduleSkeleton adds a batch of header retrieval tasks to the queue to fill up an already retrieved header skeleton.

declarations.name: SetBodyDone
declarations.doc: SetBodyDone flags the body as finished.

declarations.name: SetReceiptsDone
declarations.doc: SetReceiptsDone flags the receipts as finished.

declarations.name: cancel
declarations.doc: Cancel aborts a fetch request, returning all pending hashes to the task queue.

declarations.name: deliver
declarations.doc: deliver injects a data retrieval response into the results queue. Note, this method expects the queue lock to be already held for writing. The reason this lock is not obtained in here is because the parameters already need to access the queue, so they already need a lock anyway.

declarations.name: expire
declarations.doc: expire is the generic check that move expired tasks from a pending pool back into a task pool, returning all entities caught with expired tasks. Note, this method expects the queue lock to be already held. The reason the lock is not obtained in here is because the parameters already need to access the queue, so they already need a lock anyway.

declarations.name: newQueue
declarations.doc: newQueue creates a new download queue for scheduling block retrieval.

declarations.name: reserveHeaders
declarations.doc: reserveHeaders reserves a set of data download operations for a given peer, skipping any previously failed ones. This method is a generic version used by the individual special reservation functions. Note, this method expects the queue lock to be already held for writing. The reason the lock is not obtained in here is because the parameters already need to access the queue, so they already need a lock anyway. Returns: item - the fetchRequest progress - whether any progress was made throttle - if the caller should throttle for a while

declarations.name: fetchRequest
declarations.doc: fetchRequest is a currently running data retrieval operation.

declarations.name: fetchResult
declarations.doc: fetchResult is a struct collecting partial results from data fetchers until all outstanding pieces complete and the result as a whole can be processed.

declarations.name: queue
declarations.doc: queue represents hashes that are either need fetching or are being fetched

declarations.name: XTestDelivery
declarations.doc: XTestDelivery does some more extensive testing of events that happen, blocks that become known and peers that make reservations and deliveries. disabled since it's not really a unit-test, but can be executed to test some more advanced scenarios

declarations.name: makeChain
declarations.doc: makeChain creates a chain of n blocks starting at and including parent. the returned hash chain is ordered head->parent. In addition, every 3rd block contains a transaction and every 5th an uncle to allow testing correct block reassembly.

declarations.name: network
declarations.doc: represents the network

declarations.name: AddFetch
declarations.doc: AddFetch adds a header for body/receipt fetching. This is used when the queue wants to reserve headers for fetching. It returns the following: stale - if true, this item is already passed, and should not be requested again throttled - if true, the store is at capacity, this particular header is not prio now item - the result to store data into err - any error that occurred

declarations.name: GetCompleted
declarations.doc: GetCompleted returns the next batch of completed fetchResults

declarations.name: GetDeliverySlot
declarations.doc: GetDeliverySlot returns the fetchResult for the given header. If the 'stale' flag is true, that means the header has already been delivered 'upstream'. This method does not bubble up the 'throttle' flag, since it's moot at the point in time when the item is downloaded and ready for delivery

declarations.name: HasCompletedItems
declarations.doc: hasCompletedItems returns true if there are processable items available this method is cheaper than countCompleted

declarations.name: Prepare
declarations.doc: Prepare initialises the offset with the given block number

declarations.name: SetThrottleThreshold
declarations.doc: SetThrottleThreshold updates the throttling threshold based on the requested limit and the total queue capacity. It returns the (possibly capped) threshold

declarations.name: countCompleted
declarations.doc: countCompleted returns the number of items ready for delivery, stopping at the first non-complete item. The mthod assumes (at least) rlock is held.

declarations.name: getFetchResult
declarations.doc: getFetchResult returns the fetchResult corresponding to the given item, and the index where the result is stored.

declarations.name: resultStore
declarations.doc: resultStore implements a structure for maintaining fetchResults, tracking their download-progress and delivering (finished) results.

declarations.name: Cancel
declarations.doc: Cancel cancels the sync and waits until it has shut down.

declarations.name: Wait
declarations.doc: Wait blocks until the sync is done or canceled.

declarations.name: assignTasks
declarations.doc: assignTasks attempts to assign new tasks to all idle peers, either from the batch currently being retried, or fetching new data from the trie sync itself.

declarations.name: fillTasks
declarations.doc: fillTasks fills the given request object with a maximum of n state download tasks to send to the remote peer.

declarations.name: loop
declarations.doc: loop is the main event loop of a state trie sync. It it responsible for the assignment of new tasks to peers (including sending it to them) as well as for the processing of inbound data. Note, that the loop does not directly receive data from peers, rather those are buffered up in the downloader and pushed here async. The reason is to decouple processing from data receipt and timeouts.

declarations.name: newStateSync
declarations.doc: newStateSync creates a new state trie download scheduler. This method does not yet start the sync. The user needs to call run to initiate.

declarations.name: process
declarations.doc: process iterates over a batch of delivered state data, injecting each item into a running state sync, re-queuing any items that were requested but not delivered. Returns whether the peer actually managed to deliver anything of value, and any error that occurred.

declarations.name: processNodeData
declarations.doc: processNodeData tries to inject a trie node data blob delivered from a remote peer into the state trie, returning whether anything useful was written or any error occurred.

declarations.name: run
declarations.doc: run starts the task assignment and response processing loop, blocking until it finishes, and finally notifying any goroutines waiting for the loop to finish.

declarations.name: runStateSync
declarations.doc: runStateSync runs a state synchronisation until it completes or another root hash is requested to be switched over to.

declarations.name: spindownStateSync
declarations.doc: spindownStateSync 'drains' the outstanding requests; some will be delivered and other will time out. This is to ensure that when the next stateSync starts working, all peers are marked as idle and de facto _are_ idle.

declarations.name: stateFetcher
declarations.doc: stateFetcher manages the active state sync and accepts requests on its behalf.

declarations.name: syncState
declarations.doc: syncState starts downloading state with the given root hash.

declarations.name: timedOut
declarations.doc: timedOut returns if this request timed out.

declarations.name: updateStats
declarations.doc: updateStats bumps the various state sync progress counters and displays a log message for the user to see.

declarations.name: codeTask
declarations.doc: codeTask represents a single byte code download task, containing a set of peers already attempted retrieval from to detect stalled syncs and abort.

declarations.name: stateReq
declarations.doc: stateReq represents a batch of state fetch requests grouped together into a single data retrieval network packet.

declarations.name: stateSync
declarations.doc: stateSync schedules requests for downloading a particular state trie defined by a given state root.

declarations.name: stateSyncStats
declarations.doc: stateSyncStats is a collection of progress stats to report during a state trie sync to RPC requests as well as to display in user logs.

declarations.name: trieTask
declarations.doc: trieTask represents a single trie node download task, containing a set of peers already attempted retrieval from to detect stalled syncs and abort.

declarations.name: bodies
declarations.doc: bodies returns the block bodies of the given block hashes.

declarations.name: generate
declarations.doc: generate creates a chain of n blocks starting at and including parent. the returned hash chain is ordered head->parent. In addition, every 22th block contains a transaction and every 5th an uncle to allow testing correct block reassembly.

declarations.name: headBlock
declarations.doc: headBlock returns the head of the chain.

declarations.name: headersByHash
declarations.doc: headersByHash returns headers in order from the given hash.

declarations.name: headersByNumber
declarations.doc: headersByNumber returns headers from the given number.

declarations.name: len
declarations.doc: len returns the total number of blocks in the chain.

declarations.name: makeFork
declarations.doc: makeFork creates a fork on top of the test chain.

declarations.name: newTestChain
declarations.doc: newTestChain creates a blockchain of the given length.

declarations.name: receipts
declarations.doc: receipts returns the receipts of the given block hashes.

declarations.name: shorten
declarations.doc: shorten creates a copy of the chain with the given length. It panics if the length is longer than the number of available blocks.

declarations.name: td
declarations.doc: td returns the total difficulty of the given block.

declarations.name: bodyPack
declarations.doc: bodyPack is a batch of block bodies returned by a peer.

declarations.name: dataPack
declarations.doc: dataPack is a data message returned by a peer for some query.

declarations.name: headerPack
declarations.doc: headerPack is a batch of block headers returned by a peer.

declarations.name: peerDropFn
declarations.doc: peerDropFn is a callback type for dropping a peer detected as malicious.

declarations.name: receiptPack
declarations.doc: receiptPack is a batch of receipts returned by a peer.

declarations.name: statePack
declarations.doc: statePack is a batch of states returned by a peer.

declarations.name: Enqueue
declarations.doc: Enqueue tries to fill gaps the fetcher's future import queue.

declarations.name: FilterBodies
declarations.doc: FilterBodies extracts all the block bodies that were explicitly requested by the fetcher, returning those that should be handled differently.

declarations.name: FilterHeaders
declarations.doc: FilterHeaders extracts all the headers that were explicitly requested by the fetcher, returning those that should be handled differently.

declarations.name: NewBlockFetcher
declarations.doc: NewBlockFetcher creates a block fetcher to retrieve blocks based on hash announcements.

declarations.name: Notify
declarations.doc: Notify announces the fetcher of the potential availability of a new block in the network.

declarations.name: Start
declarations.doc: Start boots up the announcement based synchroniser, accepting and processing hash notifications and block fetches until termination requested.

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop terminates the announcement based synchroniser, canceling all pending operations.

declarations.name: enqueue
declarations.doc: enqueue schedules a new header or block import operation, if the component to be imported has not yet been seen.

declarations.name: forgetBlock
declarations.doc: forgetBlock removes all traces of a queued block from the fetcher's internal state.

declarations.name: forgetHash
declarations.doc: forgetHash removes all traces of a block announcement from the fetcher's internal state.

declarations.name: hash
declarations.doc: number returns the block hash of the injected object.

declarations.name: importBlocks
declarations.doc: importBlocks spawns a new goroutine to run a block insertion into the chain. If the block's number is at the same height as the current import phase, it updates the phase states accordingly.

declarations.name: importHeaders
declarations.doc: importHeaders spawns a new goroutine to run a header insertion into the chain. If the header's number is at the same height as the current import phase, it updates the phase states accordingly.

declarations.name: loop
declarations.doc: Loop is the main fetcher loop, checking and processing various notification events.

declarations.name: number
declarations.doc: number returns the block number of the injected object.

declarations.name: rescheduleComplete
declarations.doc: rescheduleComplete resets the specified completion timer to the next fetch timeout.

declarations.name: rescheduleFetch
declarations.doc: rescheduleFetch resets the specified fetch timer to the next blockAnnounce timeout.

declarations.name: BlockFetcher
declarations.doc: BlockFetcher is responsible for accumulating block announcements from various peers and scheduling them for retrieval.

declarations.name: HeaderRetrievalFn
declarations.doc: HeaderRetrievalFn is a callback type for retrieving a header from the local chain.

declarations.name: blockAnnounce
declarations.doc: blockAnnounce is the hash notification of the availability of a new block in the network.

declarations.name: blockBroadcasterFn
declarations.doc: blockBroadcasterFn is a callback type for broadcasting a block to connected peers.

declarations.name: blockOrHeaderInject
declarations.doc: blockOrHeaderInject represents a schedules import operation.

declarations.name: blockRetrievalFn
declarations.doc: blockRetrievalFn is a callback type for retrieving a block from the local chain.

declarations.name: bodyFilterTask
declarations.doc: bodyFilterTask represents a batch of block bodies (transactions and uncles) needing fetcher filtering.

declarations.name: bodyRequesterFn
declarations.doc: bodyRequesterFn is a callback type for sending a body retrieval request.

declarations.name: chainHeightFn
declarations.doc: chainHeightFn is a callback type to retrieve the current chain height.

declarations.name: chainInsertFn
declarations.doc: chainInsertFn is a callback type to insert a batch of blocks into the local chain.

declarations.name: headerFilterTask
declarations.doc: headerFilterTask represents a batch of headers needing fetcher filtering.

declarations.name: headerRequesterFn
declarations.doc: headerRequesterFn is a callback type for sending a header retrieval request.

declarations.name: headerVerifierFn
declarations.doc: headerVerifierFn is a callback type to verify a block's header for fast propagation.

declarations.name: headersInsertFn
declarations.doc: headersInsertFn is a callback type to insert a batch of headers into the local chain.

declarations.name: peerDropFn
declarations.doc: peerDropFn is a callback type for dropping a peer detected as malicious.

declarations.name: TestBlockMemoryExhaustionAttack
declarations.doc: Tests that blocks sent to the fetcher (either through propagation or via hash announces and retrievals) don't pile up indefinitely, exhausting available system memory.

declarations.name: TestDistantPropagationDiscarding
declarations.doc: Tests that blocks with numbers much lower or higher than out current head get discarded to prevent wasting resources on useless blocks from faulty peers.

declarations.name: TestEmptyBlockShortCircuit
declarations.doc: Tests that if a block is empty (i.e. header only), no body request should be made, and instead the header should be assembled into a whole block in itself.

declarations.name: TestFullConcurrentAnnouncements
declarations.doc: Tests that if blocks are announced by multiple peers (or even the same buggy peer), they will only get downloaded at most once.

declarations.name: TestFullDistantAnnouncementDiscarding
declarations.doc: Tests that announcements with numbers much lower or higher than out current head get discarded to prevent wasting resources on useless blocks from faulty peers.

declarations.name: TestFullInvalidNumberAnnouncement
declarations.doc: Tests that peers announcing blocks with invalid numbers (i.e. not matching the headers provided afterwards) get dropped as malicious.

declarations.name: TestFullOverlappingAnnouncements
declarations.doc: Tests that announcements arriving while a previous is being fetched still results in a valid import.

declarations.name: TestFullPendingDeduplication
declarations.doc: Tests that announces already being retrieved will not be duplicated.

declarations.name: TestFullRandomArrivalImport
declarations.doc: Tests that announcements retrieved in a random order are cached and eventually imported when all the gaps are filled in.

declarations.name: TestFullSequentialAnnouncements
declarations.doc: Tests that a fetcher accepts block/header announcements and initiates retrievals for them, successfully importing into the local chain.

declarations.name: TestHashMemoryExhaustionAttack
declarations.doc: Tests that a peer is unable to use unbounded memory with sending infinite block announcements to a node, but that even in the face of such an attack, the fetcher remains operational.

declarations.name: TestImportDeduplication
declarations.doc: Tests that blocks arriving from various sources (multiple propagations, hash announces, etc) do not get scheduled for import multiple times.

declarations.name: TestQueueGapFill
declarations.doc: Tests that direct block enqueues (due to block propagation vs. hash announce) are correctly schedule, filling and import queue gaps.

declarations.name: broadcastBlock
declarations.doc: broadcastBlock is a nop placeholder for the block broadcasting.

declarations.name: chainHeight
declarations.doc: chainHeight retrieves the current height (block number) of the chain.

declarations.name: dropPeer
declarations.doc: dropPeer is an emulator for the peer removal, simply accumulating the various peers dropped by the fetcher.

declarations.name: getBlock
declarations.doc: getBlock retrieves a block from the tester's block chain.

declarations.name: getHeader
declarations.doc: getHeader retrieves a header from the tester's block chain.

declarations.name: insertChain
declarations.doc: insertChain injects a new blocks into the simulated chain.

declarations.name: insertHeaders
declarations.doc: insertChain injects a new headers into the simulated chain.

declarations.name: makeBodyFetcher
declarations.doc: makeBodyFetcher retrieves a block body fetcher associated with a simulated peer.

declarations.name: makeChain
declarations.doc: makeChain creates a chain of n blocks starting at and including parent. the returned hash chain is ordered head->parent. In addition, every 3rd block contains a transaction and every 5th an uncle to allow testing correct block reassembly.

declarations.name: makeHeaderFetcher
declarations.doc: makeHeaderFetcher retrieves a block header fetcher associated with a simulated peer.

declarations.name: newTester
declarations.doc: newTester creates a new fetcher test mocker.

declarations.name: verifyChainHeight
declarations.doc: verifyChainHeight verifies the chain height is as expected.

declarations.name: verifyCompletingEvent
declarations.doc: verifyCompletingEvent verifies that one single event arrive on an completing channel.

declarations.name: verifyFetchingEvent
declarations.doc: verifyFetchingEvent verifies that one single event arrive on a fetching channel.

declarations.name: verifyHeader
declarations.doc: verifyHeader is a nop placeholder for the block header verification.

declarations.name: verifyImportCount
declarations.doc: verifyImportCount verifies that exactly count number of events arrive on an import hook channel.

declarations.name: verifyImportDone
declarations.doc: verifyImportDone verifies that no more events are arriving on an import channel.

declarations.name: verifyImportEvent
declarations.doc: verifyImportEvent verifies that one single event arrive on an import channel.

declarations.name: fetcherTester
declarations.doc: fetcherTester is a test simulator for mocking out local block chain.

declarations.name: AcceptRequest
declarations.doc: AcceptRequest returns whether a new request can be accepted and the missing buffer amount if it was rejected due to a buffer underrun. If accepted, maxCost is deducted from the flow control buffer.

declarations.name: BufferStatus
declarations.doc: BufferStatus returns the current buffer value and limit

declarations.name: CanSend
declarations.doc: CanSend returns the minimum waiting time required before sending a request with the given maximum estimated cost. Second return value is the relative estimated buffer level after sending the request (divided by BufLimit).

declarations.name: Disconnect
declarations.doc: Disconnect should be called when a client is disconnected

declarations.name: DumpLogs
declarations.doc: DumpLogs dumps the event log if logging is used

declarations.name: Freeze
declarations.doc: Freeze notifies the client manager about a client freeze event in which case the total capacity allowance is slightly reduced.

declarations.name: NewClientNode
declarations.doc: NewClientNode returns a new ClientNode

declarations.name: NewServerNode
declarations.doc: NewServerNode returns a new ServerNode

declarations.name: OneTimeCost
declarations.doc: OneTimeCost subtracts the given amount from the node's buffer. Note: this call can take the buffer into the negative region internally. In this case zero buffer value is returned by exported calls and no requests are accepted.

declarations.name: QueuedRequest
declarations.doc: QueuedRequest should be called when the request has been assigned to the given server node, before putting it in the send queue. It is mandatory that requests are sent in the same order as the QueuedRequest calls are made.

declarations.name: ReceivedReply
declarations.doc: ReceivedReply adjusts estimated buffer value according to the value included in the latest request reply.

declarations.name: RequestProcessed
declarations.doc: RequestProcessed should be called when the request has been processed

declarations.name: ResumeFreeze
declarations.doc: ResumeFreeze cleans all pending requests and sets the buffer estimate to the reported value after resuming from a frozen state

declarations.name: UpdateParams
declarations.doc: UpdateParams updates the flow control parameters of a client node

declarations.name: UpdateParams
declarations.doc: UpdateParams updates the flow control parameters of the node

declarations.name: NewClientManager
declarations.doc: NewClientManager returns a new client manager. Client manager enhances flow control performance by allowing client buffers to recharge quicker than the minimum guaranteed recharge rate if possible. The sum of all minimum recharge rates (sumRecharge) is updated each time a clients starts or finishes buffer recharging. Then an adjusted total recharge rate is calculated using a piecewise linear recharge curve: totalRecharge = curve(sumRecharge) (totalRecharge >= sumRecharge is enforced) Then the "bonus" buffer recharge is distributed between currently recharging clients proportionally to their minimum recharge rates. Note: total recharge is proportional to the average number of parallel running serving threads. A recharge value of 1000000 corresponds to one thread in average. The maximum number of allowed serving threads should always be considerably higher than the targeted average number. Note 2: although it is possible to specify a curve allowing the total target recharge starting from zero sumRecharge, it makes sense to add a linear ramp starting from zero in order to not let a single low-priority client use up the entire server capacity and thus ensure quick availability for others at any moment.

declarations.name: ExpirationFactor
declarations.doc: ExpirationFactor is calculated from logOffset. 1 <= Factor < 2 and Factor*2^Exp describes the multiplier applicable for additions and the divider for readouts. If logOffset changes slowly then it saves some expensive operations to not calculate them for each addition and readout but cache this intermediate form for some time. It is also useful for structures where multiple values are expired with the same Expirer.

declarations.name: ExpiredValue
declarations.doc: ExpiredValue is a scalar value that is continuously expired (decreased exponentially) based on the provided logarithmic expiration offset value. The formula for value calculation is: base*2^(exp-logOffset). In order to simplify the calculation of ExpiredValue, its value is expressed in the form of an exponent with a base of 2. Also here is a trick to reduce a lot of calculations. In theory, when a value X decays over time and then a new value Y is added, the final result should be X*2^(exp-logOffset)+Y. However it's very hard to represent in memory. So the trick is using the idea of inflation instead of exponential decay. At this moment the temporary value becomes: X*2^exp+Y*2^logOffset_1, apply the exponential decay when we actually want to calculate the value. e.g. t0: V = 100 t1: add 30, inflationary value is: 100 + 30/0.3, 0.3 is the decay coefficient t2: get value, decay coefficient is 0.2 now, final result is: 200*0.2 = 40

declarations.name: Expirer
declarations.doc: Expirer changes logOffset with a linear rate which can be changed during operation. It is not thread safe, if access by multiple goroutines is needed then it should be encapsulated into a locked structure. Note that if neither SetRate nor SetLogOffset are used during operation then LogOffset is thread safe.

declarations.name: basketItem

Value is the total relative request value accumulated for served requests while amount is the counter for each request type. Note that these values are both scaled up by basketFactor because of the exponential expiration.

declarations.name: referenceBasket
declarations.doc: referenceBasket keeps track of global request usage statistics and the usual prices of each used request type relative to each other. The amounts in the basket are scaled up by basketFactor because of the exponential expiration of long-term statistical data. Values are scaled so that the sum of all amounts and the sum of all values are equal. reqValues represent the internal relative value estimates for each request type and are calculated as value / amount. The average reqValue of all used requests is 1. In other words: SUM(refBasket[type].amount * reqValue[type]) = SUM(refBasket[type].amount)

declarations.name: requestBasket
declarations.doc: requestBasket holds amounts and values for each request type. These values are exponentially expired (see utils.ExpiredValue). The power of 2 exponent is applicable to all values within.

declarations.name: serverBasket
declarations.doc: serverBasket collects served request amount and value statistics for a single server. Values are gradually transferred to the global reference basket with a long time constant so that each server basket represents long term usage and price statistics. When the transferred part is added to the reference basket the values are scaled so that their sum equals the total value calculated according to the previous reqValues. The ratio of request values coming from the server basket represent the pricing of the specific server and modify the global estimates with a weight proportional to the amount of service provided by the server.

declarations.doc: TimeToStatScale converts a response time to a distribution vector index. The index is represented by a float64 so that linear interpolation can be applied.

declarations.name: Timeout
declarations.doc: Timeout suggests a timeout value based on the previous distribution. The parameter is the desired rate of timeouts assuming a similar distribution in the future. Note that the actual timeout should have a sensible minimum bound so that operating under ideal working conditions for a long time (for example, using a local server with very low response times) will not make it very hard for the system to accommodate longer response times in the future.

declarations.name: TimeoutWeights
declarations.doc: TimeoutWeights calculates the weight function used for calculating service value based on the response time distribution of the received service. It is based on the request timeout value of the system. It consists of a half cosine function starting with 1, crossing zero at timeout and reaching -1 at 2*timeout. After 2*timeout the weight is constant -1.

declarations.name: Value
declarations.doc: Value calculates the total service value based on the given distribution, using the specified weight function.

declarations.name: setExp
declarations.doc: setExp sets the power of 2 exponent of the structure, scaling base values (the vector itself) up or down if necessary.

declarations.name: ResponseTimeStats
declarations.doc: ResponseTimeStats is the response time distribution of a set of answered requests, weighted with request value, either served by a single server or aggregated for multiple servers. It it a fixed length (timeStatLength) distribution vector with linear interpolation. The X axis (the time values) are not linear, they should be transformed with TimeToStatScale and StatScaleToTime.

declarations.name: ResponseTimeWeights
declarations.doc: ResponseTimeStats is the response time distribution of a set of answered requests, weighted with request value, either served by a single server or aggregated for multiple servers. It it a fixed length (timeStatLength) distribution vector with linear interpolation. The X axis (the time values) are not linear, they should be transformed with TimeToStatScale and StatScaleToTime.

declarations.name: RtDistribution
declarations.doc: RtDistribution represents a distribution as a series of (X, Y) chart coordinates, where the X axis is the response time in seconds while the Y axis is the amount of service value received with a response time close to the X coordinate.

declarations.name: GetNode
declarations.doc: GetNode returns an individual server node's value tracker. If it did not exist before then a new node is created.

declarations.name: NewValueTracker
declarations.doc: NewValueTracker creates a new ValueTracker and loads its previously saved state from the database if possible.

declarations.name: Register
declarations.doc: Register adds a server node to the value tracker

declarations.name: RequestStats
declarations.doc: RequestStats returns the current contents of the reference request basket, with request values meaning average per request rather than total.

declarations.name: RtStats
declarations.doc: RtStats returns the node's own response time distribution statistics

declarations.name: RtStats
declarations.doc: RtStats returns the global response time distribution statistics

declarations.name: Served
declarations.doc: Served adds a served request to the node's statistics. An actual request may be composed of one or more request types (service vector indices).

declarations.name: StatsExpFactor
declarations.doc: StatsExpirer returns the current expiration factor so that other values can be expired with the same rate as the service value statistics.

declarations.name: StatsExpirer
declarations.doc: StatsExpirer returns the statistics expirer so that other values can be expired with the same rate as the service value statistics.

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop saves the value tracker's state and each loaded node's individual state and returns after shutting the internal goroutines down.

declarations.name: Unregister
declarations.doc: Unregister removes a server node from the value tracker

declarations.name: UpdateCosts
declarations.doc: UpdateCosts updates the node value tracker's request cost table

declarations.name: loadFromDb
declarations.doc: loadFromDb loads the value tracker's state from the database and converts saved request basket index mapping if it does not match the specified index to name mapping.

declarations.name: loadOrNewNode
declarations.doc: loadOrNewNode returns an individual server node's value tracker. If it did not exist before then a new node is created.

declarations.name: periodicUpdate
declarations.doc: periodicUpdate transfers individual node data to the global statistics, normalizes the reference basket and updates request values. The global state is also saved to the database with each update.

declarations.name: saveNode
declarations.doc: saveNode saves a server node's value tracker to the database

declarations.name: saveToDb
declarations.doc: saveToDb saves the value tracker's state to the database

declarations.name: transferStats
declarations.doc: transferStats returns request basket and response time statistics that should be added to the global statistics. The contents of the server's own request basket are gradually transferred to the main reference basket and removed from the server basket with the specified transfer rate. The response time statistics are retained at both places and therefore the global distribution is always the sum of the individual server distributions.

declarations.name: updateCosts
declarations.doc: updateCosts updates the request cost table of the server. The request value factor is also updated based on the given cost table and the current reference basket. Note that the contents of the referenced reqValues slice will not change; a new reference is passed if the values are updated by ValueTracker.

declarations.name: NodeValueTracker
declarations.doc: NodeValueTracker collects service value statistics for a specific server node

declarations.name: RequestInfo
declarations.doc: RequestInfo is an initializer structure for the service vector.

declarations.name: ValueTracker
declarations.doc: ValueTracker coordinates service value calculation for individual servers and updates global statistics

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close ends the iterator.

declarations.name: NewWrsIterator
declarations.doc: NewWrsIterator creates a new WrsIterator. Nodes are selectable if they have all the required and none of the disabled flags set. When a node is selected the selectedFlag is set which also disables further selectability until it is removed or times out.

declarations.name: Next
declarations.doc: Next selects the next node.

declarations.name: Node
declarations.doc: Node returns the current node.

declarations.name: WrsIterator
declarations.doc: WrsIterator returns nodes from the specified selectable set with a weighted random selection. Selection weights are provided by a callback function.

declarations.name: AddBalance
declarations.doc: AddBalance adds the given amount to the positive balance and returns the balance before and after the operation. Exceeding maxBalance results in an error (balance is unchanged) while adding a negative amount higher than the current balance results in zero balance. Note: this function should run inside a NodeStateMachine operation

declarations.name: GetBalance
declarations.doc: GetBalance returns the current positive and negative balance.

declarations.name: GetPriceFactors
declarations.doc: GetPriceFactors returns the price factors

declarations.name: GetRawBalance
declarations.doc: GetRawBalance returns the current positive and negative balance but in the raw(expired value) format.

declarations.name: RequestServed
declarations.doc: RequestServed should be called after serving a request for the given peer

declarations.name: SetBalance
declarations.doc: SetBalance sets the positive and negative balance to the given values Note: this function should run inside a NodeStateMachine operation

declarations.name: SetPriceFactors
declarations.doc: SetPriceFactors sets the price factors. TimeFactor is the price of a nanosecond of connection while RequestFactor is the price of a request cost unit.

declarations.name: activate
declarations.doc: activate starts time/capacity cost deduction.

declarations.name: addCallback
declarations.doc: addCallback sets up a one-time callback to be called when priority reaches the threshold. If it has already reached the threshold the callback is called immediately. Note: should be called while n.lock is held Note 2: the callback function runs inside a NodeStateMachine operation

declarations.name: addValue
declarations.doc: addValue adds the value of a given amount to the balance. The original value and updated value will also be returned if the addition is successful. Returns the error if the given value is too large and the value overflows.

declarations.name: balanceExhausted
declarations.doc: balanceExhausted should be called when the positive balance is exhausted (priority goes to zero/negative) Note: this function should run inside a NodeStateMachine operation

declarations.name: balanceToPriority
declarations.doc: balanceToPriority converts a balance to a priority value. Lower priority means first to disconnect. Positive balance translates to positive priority. If positive balance is zero then negative balance translates to a negative priority.

declarations.name: checkCallbacks
declarations.doc: checkCallbacks checks whether the threshold of any of the active callbacks have been reached and returns triggered callbacks. Note: checkCallbacks assumes that the balance has been recently updated.

declarations.name: checkPriorityStatus
declarations.doc: checkPriorityStatus checks whether the node has gained priority status and sets the priority callback and flag if necessary. It assumes that the balance has been recently updated. Note that the priority flag has to be set by the caller after the mutex has been released.

declarations.name: connectionPrice
declarations.doc: connectionPrice returns the price of connection per nanosecond at the given capacity and the estimated average request cost.

declarations.name: deactivate
declarations.doc: deactivate stops time/capacity cost deduction and saves the balances in the database

declarations.name: estimatePriority
declarations.doc: EstMinPriority gives a lower estimate for the priority at a given time in the future. An average request cost per time is assumed that is twice the average cost per time in the current session. If update is true then a priority callback is added that turns updateFlag on and off in case the priority goes below the estimated minimum.

declarations.name: negValue
declarations.doc: negValue returns the value of negative balance at a given timestamp.

declarations.name: posValue
declarations.doc: posValue returns the value of positive balance at a given timestamp.

declarations.name: priority
declarations.doc: priority returns the actual priority based on the current balance

declarations.name: priorityToBalance
declarations.doc: priorityToBalance converts a target priority to a requested balance value. If the priority is negative, then minimal negative balance is returned; otherwise the minimal positive balance is returned.

declarations.name: reducedBalance
declarations.doc: reducedBalance estimates the reduced balance at a given time in the fututre based on the given balance, the time factor and an estimated average request cost per time ratio

declarations.name: removeCallback
declarations.doc: removeCallback removes the given callback and returns true if it was active Note: should be called while n.lock is held

declarations.name: scheduleCheck
declarations.doc: scheduleCheck sets up or updates a scheduled event to ensure that it will be called again just after the next threshold has been reached.

declarations.name: setCapacity
declarations.doc: setCapacity updates the capacity value used for priority calculation Note: capacity should never be zero Note 2: this function should run inside a NodeStateMachine operation

declarations.name: setValue
declarations.doc: setValue sets the internal balance amount to the given values. Returns the error if the given value is too large.

declarations.name: signalPriorityUpdate
declarations.doc: signalPriorityUpdate signals that the priority fell below the previous minimum estimate Note: this function should run inside a NodeStateMachine operation

declarations.name: storeBalance
declarations.doc: storeBalance stores the positive and/or negative balance of the node in the database

declarations.name: timeUntil
declarations.doc: timeUntil calculates the remaining time needed to reach a given priority level assuming that no requests are processed until then. If the given level is never reached then (0, false) is returned. If it has already been reached then (0, true) is returned. Note: the function assumes that the balance has been recently updated and calculates the time starting from the last update.

declarations.name: updateAfter
declarations.doc: updateAfter schedules a balance update and callback check in the future

declarations.name: updateBalance
declarations.doc: updateBalance updates balance based on the time factor

declarations.name: AtomicBalanceOperator
declarations.doc: AtomicBalanceOperator provides operations permitted in an atomic BalanceOperation

declarations.name: ConnectedBalance
declarations.doc: ConnectedBalance provides operations permitted on connected nodes (non-read-only operations are not permitted inside a BalanceOperation)

declarations.name: PriceFactors
declarations.doc: PriceFactors determine the pricing policy (may apply either to positive or negative balances which may have different factors). - TimeFactor is cost unit per nanosecond of connection time - CapacityFactor is cost unit per nanosecond of connection time per 1000000 capacity - RequestFactor is cost unit per request "realCost" unit

declarations.name: ReadOnlyBalance
declarations.doc: ReadOnlyBalance provides read-only operations on the node balance

declarations.name: balance
declarations.doc: balance represents a pair of positive and negative balances

declarations.name: balanceCallback
declarations.doc: balanceCallback represents a single callback that is activated when client priority reaches the given threshold

declarations.name: nodeBalance
declarations.doc: nodeBalance keeps track of the positive and negative balances of a connected client and calculates actual and projected future priority values. Implements nodePriority interface.

declarations.name: nodePriority
declarations.doc: nodePriority interface provides current and estimated future priorities on demand

declarations.name: BalanceOperation
declarations.doc: BalanceOperation allows atomic operations on the balance of a node regardless of whether it is currently connected or not

declarations.name: GetExpirationTCs
declarations.doc: GetExpirationTCs returns the current positive and negative token expiration time constants

declarations.name: GetPosBalanceIDs
declarations.doc: GetPosBalanceIDs lists node IDs with an associated positive balance

declarations.name: SetDefaultFactors
declarations.doc: SetDefaultFactors sets the default price factors applied to subsequently connected clients

declarations.name: SetExpirationTCs
declarations.doc: SetExpirationTCs sets positive and negative token expiration time constants. Specified in seconds, 0 means infinite (no expiration).

declarations.name: TotalTokenAmount
declarations.doc: TotalTokenAmount returns the current total amount of service tokens in existence

declarations.name: canDropBalance
declarations.doc: canDropBalance tells whether a positive or negative balance is below the threshold and therefore can be dropped from the database

declarations.name: newBalanceTracker
declarations.doc: newBalanceTracker creates a new balanceTracker

declarations.name: newNodeBalance
declarations.doc: newNodeBalance loads balances from the database and creates a nodeBalance instance for the given node. It also sets the priorityFlag and adds balanceCallbackZero if the node has a positive balance. Note: this function should run inside a NodeStateMachine operation

declarations.name: stop
declarations.doc: Stop saves expiration offset and unsaved node balances and shuts balanceTracker down

declarations.name: storeBalance
declarations.doc: storeBalance stores either a positive or a negative balance in the database

declarations.name: updateTotalBalance
declarations.doc: updateTotalBalance adjusts the total balance after executing given callback.

declarations.name: balanceTracker
declarations.doc: balanceTracker tracks positive and negative balances for connected nodes. After clientField is set externally, a nodeBalance is created and previous balance values are loaded from the database. Both balances are exponentially expired values. Costs are deducted from the positive balance if present, otherwise added to the negative balance. If the capacity is non-zero then a time cost is applied continuously while individual request costs are applied immediately. The two balances are translated into a single priority value that also depends on the actual capacity.

declarations.name: expireNodes
declarations.doc: expireNodes iterates the whole node db and checks whether the token balances can be deleted.

declarations.name: forEachBalance
declarations.doc: forEachBalance iterates all balances and passes values to callback.

declarations.name: getPosBalanceIDs
declarations.doc: getPosBalanceIDs returns a lexicographically ordered list of IDs of accounts with a positive balance

declarations.name: Handle
declarations.doc: Handle implements Service

declarations.name: NewClientPool
declarations.doc: NewClientPool creates a new client pool

declarations.name: Register
declarations.doc: Register registers the peer into the client pool. If the peer has insufficient priority and remains inactive for longer than the allowed timeout then it will be disconnected by calling the Disconnect function of the clientPeer interface.

declarations.name: SetCapacity
declarations.doc: SetCapacity sets the assigned capacity of a connected client

declarations.name: SetConnectedBias
declarations.doc: SetConnectedBias sets the connection bias, which is applied to already connected clients So that already connected client won't be kicked out very soon and we can ensure all connected clients can have enough time to request or sync some data.

declarations.name: Start
declarations.doc: Start starts the client pool. Should be called before Register/Unregister.

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop shuts the client pool down. The clientPeer interface callbacks will not be called after Stop. Register calls will return nil.

declarations.name: Unregister
declarations.doc: Unregister removes the peer from the client pool

declarations.name: serveCapQuery
declarations.doc: serveCapQuery serves a vflux capacity query. It receives multiple token amount values and a bias time value. For each given token amount it calculates the maximum achievable capacity in case the amount is added to the balance.

declarations.name: ClientPool
declarations.doc: ClientPool implements a client database that assigns a priority to each client based on a positive and negative balance. Positive balance is externally assigned to prioritized clients and is decreased with connection time and processed requests (unless the price factors are zero). If the positive balance is zero then negative balance is accumulated. Balance tracking and priority calculation for connected clients is done by balanceTracker. PriorityQueue ensures that clients with the lowest positive or highest negative balance get evicted when the total capacity allowance is full and new clients with a better balance want to connect. Already connected nodes receive a small bias in their favor in order to avoid accepting and instantly kicking out clients. In theory, we try to ensure that each client can have several minutes of connection time. Balances of disconnected clients are stored in nodeDB including positive balance and negative banalce. Boeth positive balance and negative balance will decrease exponentially. If the balance is low enough, then the record will be dropped.

declarations.name: clientPeer
declarations.doc: clientPeer represents a peer in the client pool. None of the callbacks should block.

declarations.name: Active
declarations.doc: Active returns the number and total capacity of currently active nodes

declarations.name: Inactive
declarations.doc: Inactive returns the number of currently inactive nodes

declarations.name: Limits
declarations.doc: Limits returns the maximum allowed number and total capacity of active nodes

declarations.name: SetLimits
declarations.doc: SetLimits sets the maximum number and total capacity of simultaneously active nodes

declarations.name: activeMaxPriority
declarations.doc: activeMaxPriority callback returns estimated maximum priority of ppNodeInfo item in activeQueue

declarations.name: activePriority
declarations.doc: activePriority callback returns actual priority of ppNodeInfo item in activeQueue

declarations.name: activeSetIndex
declarations.doc: activeSetIndex callback updates ppNodeInfo item index in activeQueue

declarations.name: connectNode
declarations.doc: connectNode is called when a new node has been added to the pool (inactiveFlag set) Note: this function should run inside a NodeStateMachine operation

declarations.name: disconnectNode
declarations.doc: disconnectNode is called when a node has been removed from the pool (both inactiveFlag and activeFlag reset) Note: this function should run inside a NodeStateMachine operation

declarations.name: enforceLimits
declarations.doc: enforceLimits enforces active node count and total capacity limits. It returns the lowest active node priority. Note that this function is performed on the temporary internal state.

declarations.name: exclude
declarations.doc: exclude returns a capacityCurve with the given node excluded from the original curve

declarations.name: finalizeChanges
declarations.doc: finalizeChanges either commits or reverts temporary changes. The necessary capacity field and according flag updates are not performed here but returned in a list because they should be performed while the mutex is not held.

declarations.name: getCapacityCurve
declarations.doc: getCapacityCurve returns a new or recently cached capacityCurve based on the contents of the pool

declarations.name: inactivePriority
declarations.doc: inactivePriority callback returns actual priority of ppNodeInfo item in inactiveQueue

declarations.name: inactiveSetIndex
declarations.doc: inactiveSetIndex callback updates ppNodeInfo item index in inactiveQueue

declarations.name: invertPriority
declarations.doc: invertPriority inverts a priority value. The active queue uses inverted priorities because the node on the top is the first to be deactivated.

declarations.name: maxCapacity
declarations.doc: maxCapacity calculates the maximum capacity available for a node with a given (monotonically decreasing) priority vs. capacity function. Note that if the requesting node is already in the pool then it should be excluded from the curve in order to get the correct result.

declarations.name: newPriorityPool
declarations.doc: newPriorityPool creates a new priorityPool

declarations.name: requestCapacity
declarations.doc: requestCapacity tries to set the capacity of a connected node to the highest possible value inside the given target range. If maxTarget is not reachable then the capacity is iteratively reduced in fine steps based on the fineStepDiv parameter until minTarget is reached. The function returns the new capacity if successful and the original capacity otherwise. Note: this function should run inside a NodeStateMachine operation

declarations.name: setActiveBias
declarations.doc: setActiveBias sets the bias applied when trying to activate inactive nodes

declarations.name: setTempBias
declarations.doc: setTempBias changes the connection bias of a node in the temporary state.

declarations.name: setTempCapacity
declarations.doc: setTempCapacity changes the capacity of a node in the temporary state and adjusts activeCap and activeCount accordingly. Since this change is performed in the temporary state it should be called after setTempState and before finalizeChanges.

declarations.name: setTempState
declarations.doc: setTempState internally puts a node in a temporary state that can either be reverted or confirmed later. This temporary state allows changing the capacity of a node and moving it between the active and inactive queue. activeFlag/inactiveFlag and capacityField are not changed while the changes are still temporary.

declarations.name: setTempStepDiv
declarations.doc: setTempStepDiv changes the capacity divisor of a node in the temporary state.

declarations.name: tryActivate
declarations.doc: tryActivate tries to activate inactive nodes if possible

declarations.name: unsetTempState
declarations.doc: unsetTempState revokes the temp status of the node and reset all internal fields to the default value.

declarations.name: updateFlags
declarations.doc: updateFlags performs capacityField and activeFlag/inactiveFlag updates while the pool mutex is not held Note: this function should run inside a NodeStateMachine operation

declarations.name: updatePriority
declarations.doc: updatePriority gets the current priority value of the given node from the nodePriority interface and performs the necessary changes. It is triggered by updateFlag. Note: this function should run inside a NodeStateMachine operation

declarations.name: capUpdate
declarations.doc: capUpdate describes a capacityField and activeFlag/inactiveFlag update

declarations.name: capacityCurve
declarations.doc: capacityCurve is a snapshot of the priority pool contents in a format that can efficiently estimate how much capacity could be granted to a given node at a given priority level.

declarations.name: ppNodeInfo
declarations.doc: ppNodeInfo is the internal node descriptor of priorityPool

declarations.name: priorityPool
declarations.doc: priorityPool handles a set of nodes where each node has a capacity (a scalar value) and a priority (which can change over time and can also depend on the capacity). A node is active if it has at least the necessary minimal amount of capacity while inactive nodes have 0 capacity (values between 0 and the minimum are not allowed). The pool ensures that the number and total capacity of all active nodes are limited and the highest priority nodes are active at all times (limits can be changed during operation with immediate effect). When activating clients a priority bias is applied in favor of the already active nodes in order to avoid nodes quickly alternating between active and inactive states when their priorities are close to each other. The bias is specified in terms of duration (time) because priorities are expected to usually get lower over time and therefore a future minimum prediction (see EstMinPriority) should monotonously decrease with the specified time parameter. This time bias can be interpreted as minimum expected active time at the given capacity (if the threshold priority stays the same). Nodes in the pool always have either inactiveFlag or activeFlag set. A new node is added to the pool by externally setting inactiveFlag. priorityPool can switch a node between inactiveFlag and activeFlag at any time. Nodes can be removed from the pool by externally resetting both flags. activeFlag should not be set externally. The highest priority nodes in "inactive" state are moved to "active" state as soon as the minimum capacity can be granted for them. The capacity of lower priority active nodes is reduced or they are demoted to "inactive" state if their priority is insufficient even at minimal capacity.

declarations.name: NewServer
declarations.doc: NewServer creates a new Server

declarations.name: Register
declarations.doc: Register registers a Service

declarations.name: Serve
declarations.doc: Serve serves a vflux request batch Note: requests are served by the Handle functions of the registered services. Serve may be called concurrently but the Handle functions are called sequentially and therefore thread safety is guaranteed.

declarations.name: ServeEncoded
declarations.doc: ServeEncoded serves an encoded vflux request batch and returns the encoded replies

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop shuts down the server

declarations.name: Server
declarations.doc: Server serves vflux requests

declarations.name: Service
declarations.doc: Service is a service registered at the Server and identified by a string id

declarations.name: newServerSetup
declarations.doc: newServerSetup initializes the setup for state machine and returns the flags/fields group.

declarations.name: serverSetup
declarations.doc: serverSetup is a wrapper of the node state machine setup, which contains all the created flags and fields used in the vflux server side.

declarations.name: AddTrustedCheckpoint
declarations.doc: AddTrustedCheckpoint adds a trusted checkpoint to the blockchain

declarations.name: Config
declarations.doc: Config retrieves the header chain's chain configuration.

declarations.name: CurrentHeader
declarations.doc: CurrentHeader retrieves the current head header of the canonical chain. The header is retrieved from the HeaderChain's internal cache.

declarations.name: DisableCheckFreq
declarations.doc: DisableCheckFreq disables header validation. This is used for ultralight mode.

declarations.name: EnableCheckFreq
declarations.doc: EnableCheckFreq enables header validation.

declarations.name: Engine
declarations.doc: Engine retrieves the light chain's consensus engine.

declarations.name: GasLimit
declarations.doc: GasLimit returns the gas limit of the current HEAD block.

declarations.name: Genesis
declarations.doc: Genesis returns the genesis block

declarations.name: GetAncestor
declarations.doc: GetAncestor retrieves the Nth ancestor of a given block. It assumes that either the given block or a close ancestor of it is canonical. maxNonCanonical points to a downwards counter limiting the number of blocks to be individually checked before we reach the canonical chain. Note: ancestor == 0 returns the same block, 1 returns its parent and so on.

declarations.name: GetBlock
declarations.doc: GetBlock retrieves a block from the database or ODR service by hash and number, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetBlockByHash
declarations.doc: GetBlockByHash retrieves a block from the database or ODR service by hash, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetBlockByNumber
declarations.doc: GetBlockByNumber retrieves a block from the database or ODR service by number, caching it (associated with its hash) if found.

declarations.name: GetBody
declarations.doc: GetBody retrieves a block body (transactions and uncles) from the database or ODR service by hash, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetBodyRLP
declarations.doc: GetBodyRLP retrieves a block body in RLP encoding from the database or ODR service by hash, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetCanonicalHash
declarations.doc: GetCanonicalHash returns the canonical hash for a given block number

declarations.name: GetHeader
declarations.doc: GetHeader retrieves a block header from the database by hash and number, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetHeaderByHash
declarations.doc: GetHeaderByHash retrieves a block header from the database by hash, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetHeaderByNumber
declarations.doc: GetHeaderByNumber retrieves a block header from the database by number, caching it (associated with its hash) if found.

declarations.name: GetHeaderByNumberOdr
declarations.doc: GetHeaderByNumberOdr retrieves a block header from the database or network by number, caching it (associated with its hash) if found.

declarations.name: GetTd
declarations.doc: GetTd retrieves a block's total difficulty in the canonical chain from the database by hash and number, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetTdOdr
declarations.doc: GetHeaderByNumberOdr retrieves the total difficult from the database or network by hash and number, caching it (associated with its hash) if found.

declarations.name: HasBlock
declarations.doc: HasBlock checks if a block is fully present in the database or not, caching it if present.

declarations.name: HasHeader
declarations.doc: HasHeader checks if a block header is present in the database or not, caching it if present.

declarations.name: HeaderChain
declarations.doc: HeaderChain returns the underlying header chain.

declarations.name: InsertHeaderChain
declarations.doc: InsertHeaderChain attempts to insert the given header chain in to the local chain, possibly creating a reorg. If an error is returned, it will return the index number of the failing header as well an error describing what went wrong. The verify parameter can be used to fine tune whether nonce verification should be done or not. The reason behind the optional check is because some of the header retrieval mechanisms already need to verfy nonces, as well as because nonces can be verified sparsely, not needing to check each. In the case of a light chain, InsertHeaderChain also creates and posts light chain events when necessary.

declarations.name: LockChain
declarations.doc: LockChain locks the chain mutex for reading so that multiple canonical hashes can be retrieved while it is guaranteed that they belong to the same version of the chain

declarations.name: NewLightChain
declarations.doc: NewLightChain returns a fully initialised light chain using information available in the database. It initialises the default Ethereum header validator.

declarations.name: Odr
declarations.doc: Odr returns the ODR backend of the chain

declarations.name: Reset
declarations.doc: Reset purges the entire blockchain, restoring it to its genesis state.

declarations.name: ResetWithGenesisBlock
declarations.doc: ResetWithGenesisBlock purges the entire blockchain, restoring it to the specified genesis state.

declarations.name: Rollback
declarations.doc: Rollback is designed to remove a chain of links from the database that aren't certain enough to be valid.

declarations.name: SetHead
declarations.doc: SetHead rewinds the local chain to a new head. Everything above the new head will be deleted and the new one set.

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop stops the blockchain service. If any imports are currently in progress it will abort them using the procInterrupt.

declarations.name: StopInsert
declarations.doc: StopInsert interrupts all insertion methods, causing them to return errInsertionInterrupted as soon as possible. Insertion is permanently disabled after calling this method.

declarations.name: SubscribeChainEvent
declarations.doc: SubscribeChainEvent registers a subscription of ChainEvent.

declarations.name: SubscribeChainHeadEvent
declarations.doc: SubscribeChainHeadEvent registers a subscription of ChainHeadEvent.

declarations.name: SubscribeChainSideEvent
declarations.doc: SubscribeChainSideEvent registers a subscription of ChainSideEvent.

declarations.name: SubscribeLogsEvent
declarations.doc: SubscribeLogsEvent implements the interface of filters.Backend LightChain does not send logs events, so return an empty subscription.

declarations.name: SubscribeRemovedLogsEvent
declarations.doc: SubscribeRemovedLogsEvent implements the interface of filters.Backend LightChain does not send core.RemovedLogsEvent, so return an empty subscription.

declarations.name: SyncCheckpoint
declarations.doc: SyncCheckpoint fetches the checkpoint point block header according to the checkpoint provided by the remote peer. Note if we are running the clique, fetches the last epoch snapshot header which covered by checkpoint.

declarations.name: UnlockChain
declarations.doc: UnlockChain unlocks the chain mutex

declarations.name: loadLastState
declarations.doc: loadLastState loads the last known chain state from the database. This method assumes that the chain manager mutex is held.

declarations.name: postChainEvents
declarations.doc: postChainEvents iterates over the events generated by a chain insertion and posts them into the event feed.

declarations.name: LightChain
declarations.doc: LightChain represents a canonical chain that by default only handles block headers, downloading block bodies and receipts on demand through an ODR interface. It only does header validation during chain insertion.

declarations.name: TestBadHeaderHashes
declarations.doc: Tests that the insertion functions detect banned hashes.

declarations.name: TestBrokenHeaderChain
declarations.doc: Tests that chains missing links do not get accepted by the processor.

declarations.name: TestEqualForkHeaders
declarations.doc: Tests that given a starting canonical chain of a given size, creating equal forks do take canonical ownership.

declarations.name: TestExtendCanonicalHeaders
declarations.doc: Tests that given a starting canonical chain of a given size, it can be extended with various length chains.

declarations.name: TestLongerForkHeaders
declarations.doc: Tests that given a starting canonical chain of a given size, creating longer forks do take canonical ownership.

declarations.name: TestReorgBadHeaderHashes
declarations.doc: Tests that bad hashes are detected on boot, and the chan rolled back to a good state prior to the bad hash.

declarations.name: TestReorgLongHeaders
declarations.doc: Tests that reorganizing a long difficult chain after a short easy one overwrites the canonical numbers and links in the database.

declarations.name: TestReorgShortHeaders
declarations.doc: Tests that reorganizing a short difficult chain after a long easy one overwrites the canonical numbers and links in the database.

declarations.name: TestShorterForkHeaders
declarations.doc: Tests that given a starting canonical chain of a given size, creating shorter forks do not take canonical ownership.

declarations.name: makeHeaderChain
declarations.doc: makeHeaderChain creates a deterministic chain of headers rooted at parent.

declarations.name: newCanonical
declarations.doc: newCanonical creates a chain database, and injects a deterministic canonical chain. Depending on the full flag, if creates either a full block chain or a header only chain.

declarations.name: newTestLightChain
declarations.doc: newTestLightChain creates a LightChain that doesn't validate anything.

declarations.name: testFork
declarations.doc: Test fork of length N starting from block i

declarations.name: testHeaderChainImport
declarations.doc: testHeaderChainImport tries to process a chain of header, writing them into the database if successful.

declarations.doc: Store writes the contents of the list to the given database

declarations.name: NodeSet
declarations.doc: NodeSet stores a set of trie nodes. It implements trie.Database and can also act as a cache for another trie.Database.

declarations.doc: StateTrieID returns a TrieID for a state trie belonging to a certain block header.

declarations.name: StorageTrieID
declarations.doc: StorageTrieID returns a TrieID for a contract storage trie at a given account of a given state trie. It also requires the root hash of the trie for checking Merkle proofs.

declarations.name: BloomRequest
declarations.doc: BloomRequest is the ODR request type for retrieving bloom filters from a CHT structure

declarations.name: ChtRequest
declarations.doc: ChtRequest is the ODR request type for retrieving header by Canonical Hash Trie

declarations.name: CodeRequest
