declarations.doc: OdrBackend is an interface to a backend service that handles ODR retrievals type

declarations.name: OdrRequest
declarations.doc: OdrRequest is an interface for retrieval requests

declarations.name: ReceiptsRequest
declarations.doc: ReceiptsRequest is the ODR request type for retrieving receipts.

declarations.name: TrieID
declarations.doc: TrieID identifies a state or account storage trie

declarations.name: TrieRequest
declarations.doc: TrieRequest is the ODR request type for state/storage trie entries

declarations.name: TxStatus
declarations.doc: TxStatus describes the status of a transaction

declarations.name: TxStatusRequest
declarations.doc: TxStatusRequest is the ODR request type for retrieving transaction status

declarations.name: GetBlock
declarations.doc: GetBlock retrieves an entire block corresponding to the hash, assembling it back from the stored header and body.

declarations.name: GetBlockLogs
declarations.doc: GetBlockLogs retrieves the logs generated by the transactions included in a block given by its hash.

declarations.name: GetBlockReceipts
declarations.doc: GetBlockReceipts retrieves the receipts generated by the transactions included in a block given by its hash.

declarations.name: GetBloomBits
declarations.doc: GetBloomBits retrieves a batch of compressed bloomBits vectors belonging to the given bit index and section indexes.

declarations.name: GetBody
declarations.doc: GetBody retrieves the block body (transactions, uncles) corresponding to the hash.

declarations.name: GetBodyRLP
declarations.doc: GetBodyRLP retrieves the block body (transactions and uncles) in RLP encoding.

declarations.name: GetCanonicalHash
declarations.doc: GetCanonicalHash retrieves the canonical block hash corresponding to the number.

declarations.name: GetHeaderByNumber
declarations.doc: GetHeaderByNumber retrieves the canonical block header corresponding to the given number. The returned header is proven by local CHT.

declarations.name: GetTd
declarations.doc: GetTd retrieves the total difficulty corresponding to the number and hash.

declarations.name: GetTransaction
declarations.doc: GetTransaction retrieves a canonical transaction by hash and also returns its position in the chain. There is no guarantee in the LES protocol that the mined transaction will be retrieved back for sure because of different reasons(the transaction is unindexed, the malicous server doesn't reply it deliberately, etc). Therefore, unretrieved transactions will receive a certain number of retrys, thus giving a weak guarantee.

declarations.name: GetUntrustedBlockLogs
declarations.doc: GetUntrustedBlockLogs retrieves the logs generated by the transactions included in a block. The retrieved logs are regarded as untrusted and will not be stored in the database. This function should only be used in light client checkpoint syncing.

declarations.doc: PruneSections implements core.ChainIndexerBackend which deletes all chain data(except hash<->number mappings) older than the specified threshold.

declarations.doc: StoreChtRoot writes the CHT root associated to the given section into the database

declarations.name: fetchMissingNodes
declarations.doc: fetchMissingNodes tries to retrieve the last entries of the latest trusted bloom trie from the ODR backend in order to be able to add new entries and calculate subsequent root hashes

declarations.name: fetchMissingNodes
declarations.doc: fetchMissingNodes tries to retrieve the last entry of the latest trusted CHT from the ODR backend in order to be able to add new entries and calculate subsequent root hashes

declarations.doc: BloomTrieIndexerBackend implements core.ChainIndexerBackend

declarations.name: ChtNode
declarations.doc: ChtNode structures are stored in the Canonical Hash Trie in an RLP encoded format

declarations.name: IndexerConfig
declarations.doc: IndexerConfig includes a set of configs for chain indexers.

declarations.name: do
declarations.doc: do runs fn and attempts to fill in missing nodes by retrieving.

declarations.name: do
declarations.doc: do tries and retries to execute a function until it returns with no error or an error type other than MissingNodeError

declarations.name: Add
declarations.doc: Add adds a transaction to the pool if valid and passes it to the tx relay backend

declarations.name: AddBatch
declarations.doc: AddTransactions adds all valid transactions to the pool and passes them to the tx relay backend

declarations.name: Content
declarations.doc: Content retrieves the data content of the transaction pool, returning all the pending as well as queued transactions, grouped by account and nonce.

declarations.name: ContentFrom
declarations.doc: ContentFrom retrieves the data content of the transaction pool, returning the pending as well as queued transactions of this address, grouped by nonce.

declarations.name: GetNonce
declarations.doc: GetNonce returns the "pending" nonce of a given address. It always queries the nonce belonging to the latest header too in order to detect if another client using the same key sent a transaction.

declarations.name: GetTransaction
declarations.doc: GetTransaction returns a transaction if it is contained in the pool and nil otherwise.

declarations.name: GetTransactions
declarations.doc: GetTransactions returns all currently processable transactions. The returned slice may be modified by the caller.

declarations.name: NewTxPool
declarations.doc: NewTxPool creates a new light transaction pool

declarations.name: RemoveTransactions
declarations.doc: RemoveTransactions removes all given transactions from the pool.

declarations.name: RemoveTx
declarations.doc: RemoveTx removes the transaction with the given hash from the pool.

declarations.name: Stats
declarations.doc: Stats returns the number of currently pending (locally created) transactions

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop stops the light transaction pool

declarations.name: SubscribeNewTxsEvent
declarations.doc: SubscribeNewTxsEvent registers a subscription of core.NewTxsEvent and starts sending event to the given channel.

declarations.name: add
declarations.doc: add validates a new transaction and sets its state pending if processable. It also updates the locally stored nonce if necessary.

declarations.name: checkMinedTxs
declarations.doc: checkMinedTxs checks newly added blocks for the currently pending transactions and marks them as mined if necessary. It also stores block position in the db and adds them to the received txStateChanges map.

declarations.name: currentState
declarations.doc: currentState returns the light state of the current head header

declarations.name: eventLoop
declarations.doc: eventLoop processes chain head events and also notifies the tx relay backend about the new head hash and tx state changes

declarations.name: getLists
declarations.doc: getLists creates lists of mined and rolled back tx hashes

declarations.name: reorgOnNewHead
declarations.doc: reorgOnNewHead sets a new head header, processing (and rolling back if necessary) the blocks since the last known head and returns a txStateChanges map containing the recently mined and rolled back transaction hashes. If an error (context timeout) occurs during checking new blocks, it leaves the locally known head at the latest checked block and still returns a valid txStateChanges, making it possible to continue checking the missing blocks at the next chain head event

declarations.name: rollbackTxs
declarations.doc: rollbackTxs marks the transactions contained in recently rolled back blocks as rolled back. It also removes any positional lookup entries.

declarations.name: setState
declarations.doc: setState sets the status of a tx to either recently mined or recently rolled back

declarations.name: validateTx
declarations.doc: validateTx checks whether a transaction is valid according to the consensus rules.

declarations.name: TxPool
declarations.doc: TxPool implements the transaction pool for light clients, which keeps track of the status of locally created transactions, detecting if they are included in a block (mined) or rolled back. There are no queued transactions since we always receive all locally signed transactions in the same order as they are created.

declarations.name: TxRelayBackend
declarations.doc: TxRelayBackend provides an interface to the mechanism that forwards transacions to the ETH network. The implementations of the functions should be non-blocking. Send instructs backend to forward new transactions NewHead notifies backend about a new head after processed by the tx pool, including mined and rolled back transactions since the last event Discard notifies backend about transactions that should be discarded either because they have been replaced by a re-send or because they have been mined long ago and no rollback is expected

declarations.name: txStateChanges
declarations.doc: txStateChanges stores the recent changes between pending/mined states of transactions. True means mined, false means rolled back, no entry means no change

declarations.name: minedTx
declarations.doc: txs included in block i or before that (minedTx(i) <= sentTx(i))

declarations.name: sentTx
declarations.doc: txs sent before block i

declarations.name: FormatFunc
declarations.doc: FormatFunc returns a new Format object which uses the given function to perform record formatting.

declarations.name: FormatLogfmtInt64
declarations.doc: FormatLogfmtInt64 formats n with thousand separators.

declarations.name: FormatLogfmtUint64
declarations.doc: FormatLogfmtUint64 formats n with thousand separators.

declarations.name: JSONFormat
declarations.doc: JSONFormat formats log records as JSON objects separated by newlines. It is the equivalent of JSONFormatEx(false, true).

declarations.name: JSONFormatEx
declarations.doc: JSONFormatEx formats log records as JSON objects. If pretty is true, records will be pretty-printed. If lineSeparated is true, records will be logged with a new line between each record.

declarations.name: JSONFormatOrderedEx
declarations.doc: JSONFormatOrderedEx formats log records as JSON arrays. If pretty is true, records will be pretty-printed. If lineSeparated is true, records will be logged with a new line between each record.

declarations.name: LogfmtFormat
declarations.doc: LogfmtFormat prints records in logfmt format, an easy machine-parseable but human-readable format for key/value pairs. For more details see: http://godoc.org/github.com/kr/logfmt

declarations.name: PrintOrigins
declarations.doc: PrintOrigins sets or unsets log location (file:line) printing for terminal format output.

declarations.name: TerminalFormat
declarations.doc: TerminalFormat formats log records optimized for human readability on a terminal with color-coded level output and terser human friendly timestamp. This format should only be used for interactive programs or while developing. [LEVEL] [TIME] MESSAGE key=value key=value ... Example: [DBUG] [May 16 20:58:45] remove route ns=haproxy addr=127.0.0.1:50002

declarations.name: escapeString
declarations.doc: escapeString checks if the provided string needs escaping/quoting, and calls strconv.Quote if needed

declarations.name: formatLogfmtBigInt
declarations.doc: formatLogfmtBigInt formats n with thousand separators.

declarations.name: formatLogfmtValue
declarations.doc: formatValue formats a value for serialization

declarations.name: TerminalStringer
declarations.doc: TerminalStringer is an analogous interface to the stdlib stringer, allowing own types to have custom shortened serialization formats when printed to the screen.

declarations.name: BufferedHandler
declarations.doc: BufferedHandler writes all records to a buffered channel of the given size which flushes into the wrapped handler whenever it is available for writing. Since these writes happen asynchronously, all writes to a BufferedHandler never return an error and any errors from the wrapped handler are ignored.

declarations.name: CallerFileHandler
declarations.doc: CallerFileHandler returns a Handler that adds the line number and file of the calling function to the context with key "caller".

declarations.name: CallerFuncHandler
declarations.doc: CallerFuncHandler returns a Handler that adds the calling function name to the context with key "fn".

declarations.name: CallerStackHandler
declarations.doc: CallerStackHandler returns a Handler that adds a stack trace to the context with key "stack". The stack trace is formatted as a space separated list of call sites inside matching []'s. The most recent call site is listed first. Each call site is formatted according to format. See the documentation of package github.com/go-stack/stack for the list of supported formats.

declarations.name: ChannelHandler
declarations.doc: ChannelHandler writes all records to the given channel. It blocks if the channel is full. Useful for async processing of log messages, it's used by BufferedHandler.

declarations.name: DiscardHandler
declarations.doc: DiscardHandler reports success for all writes but does nothing. It is useful for dynamically disabling logging at runtime via a Logger's SetHandler method.

declarations.name: FailoverHandler
declarations.doc: FailoverHandler writes all log records to the first handler specified, but will failover and write to the second handler if the first handler has failed, and so on for all handlers specified. For example you might want to log to a network socket, but failover to writing to a file if the network fails, and then to standard out if the file write fails: log.FailoverHandler( log.Must.NetHandler("tcp", ":9090", log.JSONFormat()), log.Must.FileHandler("/var/log/app.log", log.LogfmtFormat()), log.StdoutHandler) All writes that do not go to the first handler will add context with keys of the form "failover_err_{idx}" which explain the error encountered while trying to write to the handlers before them in the list.

declarations.name: FileHandler
declarations.doc: FileHandler returns a handler which writes log records to the give file using the given format. If the path already exists, FileHandler will append to the given file. If it does not, FileHandler will create the file with mode 0644.

declarations.name: FilterHandler
declarations.doc: FilterHandler returns a Handler that only writes records to the wrapped Handler if the given function evaluates true. For example, to only log records where the 'err' key is not nil: logger.SetHandler(FilterHandler(func(r *Record) bool { for i := 0; i < len(r.Ctx); i += 2 { if r.Ctx[i] == "err" { return r.Ctx[i+1] != nil } } return false }, h))

declarations.name: FuncHandler
declarations.doc: FuncHandler returns a Handler that logs records with the given function.

declarations.name: LazyHandler
declarations.doc: LazyHandler writes all values to the wrapped handler after evaluating any lazy functions in the record's context. It is already wrapped around StreamHandler and SyslogHandler in this library, you'll only need it if you write your own Handler.

declarations.name: LvlFilterHandler
declarations.doc: LvlFilterHandler returns a Handler that only writes records which are less than the given verbosity level to the wrapped Handler. For example, to only log Error/Crit records: log.LvlFilterHandler(log.LvlError, log.StdoutHandler)

declarations.name: MatchFilterHandler
declarations.doc: MatchFilterHandler returns a Handler that only writes records to the wrapped Handler if the given key in the logged context matches the value. For example, to only log records from your ui package: log.MatchFilterHandler("pkg", "app/ui", log.StdoutHandler)

declarations.name: MultiHandler
declarations.doc: MultiHandler dispatches any write to each of its handlers. This is useful for writing different types of log information to different locations. For example, to log to a file and standard error: log.MultiHandler( log.Must.FileHandler("/var/log/app.log", log.LogfmtFormat()), log.StderrHandler)

declarations.name: NetHandler
declarations.doc: NetHandler opens a socket to the given address and writes records over the connection.

declarations.name: StreamHandler
declarations.doc: StreamHandler writes log records to an io.Writer with the given format. StreamHandler can be used to easily begin writing log records to other outputs. StreamHandler wraps itself with LazyHandler and SyncHandler to evaluate Lazy objects and perform safe concurrent writes.

declarations.name: SyncHandler
declarations.doc: SyncHandler can be wrapped around a handler to guarantee that only a single Log operation can proceed at a time. It's necessary for thread-safe concurrent writes.

declarations.name: formatCall
declarations.doc: This function is here to please go vet on Go < 1.8.

declarations.name: Handler
declarations.doc: Handler defines where and how log records are written. A Logger prints its log records by writing to a Handler. Handlers are composable, providing you great flexibility in combining them to achieve the logging structure that suits your applications.

declarations.name: closingHandler
declarations.doc: XXX: closingHandler is essentially unused at the moment it's meant for a future time when the Handler interface supports a possible Close() operation

declarations.name: BacktraceAt
declarations.doc: BacktraceAt sets the glog backtrace location. When set to a file and line number holding a logging statement, a stack trace will be written to the Info log whenever execution hits that statement. Unlike with Vmodule, the ".go" must be present.

declarations.name: Log
declarations.doc: Log implements Handler.Log, filtering a log record through the global, local and backtrace filters, finally emitting it if either allow it through.

declarations.name: NewGlogHandler
declarations.doc: NewGlogHandler creates a new log handler with filtering functionality similar to Google's glog logger. The returned handler implements Handler.

declarations.name: SetHandler
declarations.doc: SetHandler updates the handler to write records to the specified sub-handler.

declarations.name: Verbosity
declarations.doc: Verbosity sets the glog verbosity ceiling. The verbosity of individual packages and source files can be raised using Vmodule.

declarations.name: Vmodule
declarations.doc: Vmodule sets the glog verbosity pattern. The syntax of the argument is a comma-separated list of pattern=N, where the pattern is a literal file name or "glob" pattern matching and N is a V level. For instance: pattern="gopher.go=3" sets the V level to 3 in all Go files named "gopher.go" pattern="foo=3" sets V to 3 in all files of any packages whose import path ends in "foo" pattern="foo/*=3" sets V to 3 in all files of any packages whose import path contains "foo"

declarations.name: GlogHandler
declarations.doc: GlogHandler is a log handler that mimics the filtering features of Google's glog logger: setting global log levels; overriding with callsite pattern matches; and requesting backtraces at certain positions.

declarations.name: pattern
declarations.doc: pattern contains a filter for the Vmodule option, holding a verbosity level and a file pattern to match.

declarations.name: swapHandler
declarations.doc: swapHandler wraps another handler that may be swapped out dynamically at runtime in a thread-safe fashion.

declarations.name: swapHandler
declarations.doc: swapHandler wraps another handler that may be swapped out dynamically at runtime in a thread-safe fashion.

declarations.name: AlignedString
declarations.doc: AlignedString returns a 5-character string containing the name of a Lvl.

declarations.name: LvlFromString
declarations.doc: LvlFromString returns the appropriate Lvl from a string name. Useful for parsing command line args and configuration files.

declarations.name: String
declarations.doc: Strings returns the name of a Lvl.

declarations.name: Ctx
declarations.doc: Ctx is a map of key/value pairs to pass as context to a log function Use this only if you really need greater safety around the arguments you pass to the logging functions.

declarations.name: Lazy
declarations.doc: Lazy allows you to defer calculation of a logged value that is expensive to compute until it is certain that it must be evaluated with the given filters. Lazy may also be used in conjunction with a Logger's New() function to generate a child logger which always reports the current value of changing state. You may wrap any function which takes no arguments to Lazy. It may return any number of values of any type.

declarations.name: Logger
declarations.doc: A Logger writes key/value pairs to a Handler

declarations.name: Record
declarations.doc: A Record is what a Logger asks its handler to write

declarations.name: RecordKeyNames
declarations.doc: RecordKeyNames gets stored in a Record when the write function is executed.

declarations.name: Crit
declarations.doc: Crit is a convenient alias for Root().Crit

declarations.name: Debug
declarations.doc: Debug is a convenient alias for Root().Debug

declarations.name: Error
declarations.doc: Error is a convenient alias for Root().Error

declarations.name: Info
declarations.doc: Info is a convenient alias for Root().Info

declarations.name: New
declarations.doc: New returns a new logger with the given context. New is a convenient alias for Root().New

declarations.name: Output
declarations.doc: Output is a convenient alias for write, allowing for the modification of the calldepth (number of stack frames to skip). calldepth influences the reported line number of the log message. A calldepth of zero reports the immediate caller of Output. Non-zero calldepth skips as many stack frames.

declarations.name: Root
declarations.doc: Root returns the root logger

declarations.name: Trace
declarations.doc: Trace is a convenient alias for Root().Trace

declarations.doc: GetSealingBlockAsync requests to generate a sealing block according to the given parameters. Regardless of whether the generation is successful or not, there is always a result that will be returned through the result channel. The difference is that if the execution fails, the returned result is nil and the concrete error is dropped silently.

declarations.name: GetSealingBlockSync

declarations.name: update
declarations.doc: update keeps track of the downloader events. Please be aware that this is a one shot type of update loop. It's entered once and as soon as `Done` or `Failed` has been broadcasted the events are unregistered and the loop is exited. This to prevent a major security vuln where external parties can DOS you with blocks and halt your mining operation for as long as the DOS continues.

declarations.doc: TestMinerDownloaderFirstFails tests that mining is only permitted to run indefinitely once the downloader sees a DoneEvent (success). An initial FailedEvent should allow mining to stop on a subsequent downloader StartEvent.

declarations.name: TestMinerSetEtherbase

declarations.doc: Shift drops all unconfirmed blocks from the set which exceed the unconfirmed sets depth allowance, checking them against the canonical chain for inclusion or staleness report.

declarations.name: newUnconfirmedBlocks

declarations.name: chainRetriever
declarations.doc: chainRetriever is used by the unconfirmed block set to verify whether a previously mined block is part of the canonical chain or not.

declarations.name: unconfirmedBlock
declarations.doc: unconfirmedBlock is a small collection of metadata about a locally mined block that is placed into a unconfirmed set for canonical chain inclusion tracking.

declarations.name: unconfirmedBlocks
declarations.doc: unconfirmedBlocks implements a data structure to maintain locally mined blocks have not yet reached enough maturity to guarantee chain inclusion. It is used by the miner to provide logs to the user when a previously mined block has a high enough guarantee to not be reorged out of the canonical chain.

declarations.name: TestUnconfirmedInsertBounds
declarations.doc: Tests that inserting blocks into the unconfirmed set accumulates them until the desired depth is reached, after which they begin to be dropped.

declarations.name: TestUnconfirmedShifts
declarations.doc: Tests that shifting blocks out of the unconfirmed set works both for normal cases as well as for corner cases such as empty sets, empty shifts or full shifts.

declarations.name: noopChainRetriever

declarations.name: ancestorTimes

declarations.name: commitEx

declarations.name: NewEnode
declarations.doc: NewEnode parses a node designator. There are two basic forms of node designators - incomplete nodes, which only have the public key (node ID) - complete nodes, which contain the public key and IP/Port information For incomplete nodes, the designator must look like one of these enode://<hex node id> <hex node id> For complete nodes, the node ID is encoded in the username portion of the URL, separated from the host by an @ sign. The hostname can only be given as an IP address, DNS domain names are not allowed. The port in the host name section is the TCP listening port. If the TCP and UDP (discovery) ports differ, the UDP port is specified as query parameter "discport". In the following example, the node URL describes a node with IP address 10.3.58.6, TCP listening port 30303 and UDP discovery port 30301. enode://<hex node id>@10.3.58.6:30303?discport=30301

declarations.name: removeStatic

declarations.doc: resolve attempts to find the current endpoint for the destination using discovery. Resolve operations are throttled with backoff to avoid flooding the discovery network with useless queries for nodes that don't exist. The backoff delay resets when the node is found.

declarations.doc: startStaticDials starts n static dial tasks.

declarations.name: updateStaticPool
declarations.doc: updateStaticPool attempts to move the given static dial back into staticPool.

declarations.doc: NodeDialer is used to connect to nodes in the network, typically by using an underlying net.Dialer but also using net.Pipe in tests.

declarations.doc: dialer creates outbound connections and submits them into Server. Two types of peer connections can be created: - static dials are pre-configured connections. The dialer attempts keep these nodes connected at all times. - dynamic dials are created from node discovery results. The dialer continuously reads candidate nodes from its input iterator and attempts to create peer connections to nodes arriving through the iterator.

declarations.name: dialTask

declarations.name: tcpDialer

declarations.name: Close

declarations.name: Node

declarations.name: addNodes

declarations.doc: completeDials unblocks calls to Dial for the given nodes.

declarations.name: waitForDials
declarations.doc: waitForDials waits for calls to Dial with the given nodes as argument. Those calls will be held blocking until completeDials is called with the same nodes.

declarations.name: dialTestDialer
declarations.doc: dialTestDialer is the NodeDialer used by runDialTest.

declarations.name: dialTestIterator
declarations.doc: dialTestIterator is the input iterator for dialer tests. This works a bit like a channel with infinite buffer: nodes are added to the buffer with addNodes, which unblocks Next and returns them from the iterator.

declarations.name: dialTestResolver
declarations.doc: dialTestResolver tracks calls to resolve.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close unblocks any pending ReadMsg and WriteMsg calls on both ends of the pipe. They will return ErrPipeClosed. Close also interrupts any reads from a message payload.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close closes the underlying MsgReadWriter if it implements the io.Closer interface

declarations.name: Decode
declarations.doc: Decode parses the RLP content of a message into the given value, which must be a pointer. For the decoding rules, please see package rlp.

declarations.name: Discard
declarations.doc: Discard reads any remaining payload data into a black hole.

declarations.name: ExpectMsg
declarations.doc: ExpectMsg reads a message from r and verifies that its code and encoded RLP content match the provided values. If content is nil, the payload is discarded and not verified.

declarations.name: MsgPipe
declarations.doc: MsgPipe creates a message pipe. Reads on one end are matched with writes on the other. The pipe is full-duplex, both ends implement MsgReadWriter.

declarations.name: Read
declarations.doc: note: when using eofSignal to detect whether a message payload has been read, Read might not be called for zero sized messages.

declarations.name: ReadMsg
declarations.doc: ReadMsg returns a message sent on the other end of the pipe.

declarations.name: ReadMsg
declarations.doc: ReadMsg reads a message from the underlying MsgReadWriter and emits a "message received" event

declarations.name: Send
declarations.doc: Send writes an RLP-encoded message with the given code. data should encode as an RLP list.

declarations.name: SendItems
declarations.doc: SendItems writes an RLP with the given code and data elements. For a call such as: SendItems(w, code, e1, e2, e3) the message payload will be an RLP list containing the items: [e1, e2, e3]

declarations.name: WriteMsg
declarations.doc: WriteMsg sends a message on the pipe. It blocks until the receiver has consumed the message payload.

declarations.name: WriteMsg
declarations.doc: WriteMsg writes a message to the underlying MsgReadWriter and emits a "message sent" event

declarations.name: newMsgEventer
declarations.doc: newMsgEventer returns a msgEventer which sends message events to the given feed

declarations.name: Msg
declarations.doc: Msg defines the structure of a p2p message. Note that a Msg can only be sent once since the Payload reader is consumed during sending. It is not possible to create a Msg and send it any number of times. If you want to reuse an encoded structure, encode the payload into a byte array and create a separate Msg with a bytes.Reader as Payload for each send.

declarations.name: MsgPipeRW
declarations.doc: MsgPipeRW is an endpoint of a MsgReadWriter pipe.

declarations.name: MsgReadWriter
declarations.doc: MsgReadWriter provides reading and writing of encoded messages. Implementations should ensure that ReadMsg and WriteMsg can be called simultaneously from multiple goroutines.

declarations.name: eofSignal
declarations.doc: eofSignal wraps a reader with eof signaling. the eof channel is closed when the wrapped reader returns an error or when count bytes have been read.

declarations.name: msgEventer
declarations.doc: msgEventer wraps a MsgReadWriter and sends events whenever a message is sent or received

declarations.name: TestMsgPipeConcurrentClose
declarations.doc: This test should panic if concurrent close isn't implemented correctly.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close delegates a close operation to the underlying connection, unregisters the peer from the traffic registries and emits close event.

declarations.name: Read

declarations.name: Write

declarations.name: newMeteredConn
declarations.doc: newMeteredConn creates a new metered connection, bumps the ingress or egress connection meter and also increases the metered peer count. If the metrics system is disabled, function returns the original connection.

declarations.name: meteredConn
declarations.doc: meteredConn is a wrapper around a net.Conn that meters both the inbound and outbound network traffic.

declarations.name: Caps
declarations.doc: Caps returns the capabilities (supported subprotocols) of the remote peer.

declarations.name: Disconnect
declarations.doc: Disconnect terminates the peer connection with the given reason. It returns immediately and does not wait until the connection is closed.

declarations.name: Fullname

declarations.name: ID

declarations.name: Inbound

declarations.name: Info

declarations.name: RemoteAddr
declarations.doc: RemoteAddr returns the remote address of the network connection.

declarations.name: RunningCap

declarations.name: String

declarations.name: getProto

declarations.name: matchProtocols
declarations.doc: matchProtocols creates structures for matching named subprotocols.

declarations.name: PeerEvent

declarations.doc: PeerInfo represents a short summary of the information known about a connected peer. Sub-protocol independent fields are contained and initialized here, with protocol specifics delegated to all connected sub-protocols.

declarations.name: protoHandshake

declarations.name: Protocol

declarations.doc: AddPeer adds the given node to the static node set. When there is room in the peer set, the server will connect to the node. If the connection fails for any reason, the server will attempt to reconnect the peer.

declarations.doc: AddTrustedPeer adds the given node to a reserved trusted list which allows the node to always connect, even if the slot are full.

declarations.doc: fakeAddrListener is a listener that creates connections with a mocked remote address.

declarations.name: advance
declarations.doc: advance advances the lookup until any new nodes have been found. It returns false when the lookup has ended.

declarations.name: run
declarations.doc: run runs the lookup to completion and returns the closest nodes found.

declarations.name: lookup
declarations.doc: lookup performs a network search for nodes close to the given target. It approaches the target by querying nodes that are closer to it on each iteration. The given target does not need to be an actual node identifier.

declarations.name: lookupIterator
declarations.doc: lookupIterator performs lookup operations and iterates over all seen nodes. When a lookup finishes, a new one is created through nextLookup.

declarations.name: node
declarations.doc: node represents a host on the network. The fields of Node may not be modified.

declarations.name: checkClockDrift
declarations.doc: checkClockDrift queries an NTP server for clock drifts and warns the user if one large enough is detected.

declarations.name: sntpDrift
declarations.doc: sntpDrift does a naive time resolution against an NTP server and returns the measured drift. This method uses the simple version of NTP. It's not precise but should be fine for these purposes. Note, it executes two extra measurements compared to the number of requested ones to be able to discard the two extremes as outliers.

declarations.name: durationSlice
declarations.doc: durationSlice attaches the methods of sort.Interface to []time.Duration, sorting in increasing order.

declarations.name: ReadRandomNodes
declarations.doc: ReadRandomNodes fills the given slice with random nodes from the table. The results are guaranteed to be unique for a single invocation, no node will appear twice.

declarations.name: addSeenNode
declarations.doc: addSeenNode adds a node which may or may not be live to the end of a bucket. If the bucket has space available, adding the node succeeds immediately. Otherwise, the node is added to the replacements list. The caller must not hold tab.mutex.

declarations.name: addVerifiedNode
declarations.doc: addVerifiedNode adds a node whose existence has been verified recently to the front of a bucket. If the node is already in the bucket, it is moved to the front. If the bucket has no space, the node is added to the replacements list. There is an additional safety measure: if the table is still initializing the node is not added. This prevents an attack where the table could be filled by just sending ping repeatedly. The caller must not hold tab.mutex.

declarations.name: bucket
declarations.doc: bucket returns the bucket for the given node ID hash.

declarations.name: bucketLen
declarations.doc: bucketLen returns the number of nodes in the bucket for the given ID.

declarations.name: bumpInBucket
declarations.doc: bumpInBucket moves the given node to the front of the bucket entry list if it is contained in that list.

declarations.name: close
declarations.doc: close terminates the network listener and flushes the node database.

declarations.name: copyLiveNodes
declarations.doc: copyLiveNodes adds nodes from the table to the database if they have been in the table longer than seedMinTableTime.

declarations.name: delete
declarations.doc: delete removes an entry from the node table. It is used to evacuate dead nodes.

declarations.name: deleteNode
declarations.doc: deleteNode removes n from list.

declarations.name: doRefresh
declarations.doc: doRefresh performs a lookup for a random target to keep buckets full. seed nodes are inserted if the table is empty (initial bootstrap or discarded faulty peers).

declarations.name: doRevalidate
declarations.doc: doRevalidate checks that the last node in a random bucket is still live and replaces or deletes the node if it isn't.

declarations.name: findnodeByID
declarations.doc: findnodeByID returns the n nodes in the table that are closest to the given id. This is used by the FINDNODE/v4 handler. The preferLive parameter says whether the caller wants liveness-checked results. If preferLive is true and the table contains any verified nodes, the result will not contain unverified nodes. However, if there are no verified nodes at all, the result will contain unverified nodes.

declarations.name: getNode
declarations.doc: getNode returns the node with the given ID or nil if it isn't in the table.

declarations.name: isInitDone
declarations.doc: isInitDone returns whether the table's initial seeding procedure has completed.

declarations.name: len
declarations.doc: len returns the number of nodes in the table.

declarations.name: loop
declarations.doc: loop schedules runs of doRefresh, doRevalidate and copyLiveNodes.

declarations.name: nodeToRevalidate
declarations.doc: nodeToRevalidate returns the last node in a random, non-empty bucket.

declarations.name: push
declarations.doc: push adds the given node to the list, keeping the total size below maxElems.

declarations.name: pushNode
declarations.doc: pushNode adds n to the front of list, keeping at most max items.

declarations.name: replace
declarations.doc: replace removes n from the replacement list and replaces 'last' with it if it is the last entry in the bucket. If 'last' isn't the last entry, it has either been replaced with someone else or became active.

declarations.name: setFallbackNodes
declarations.doc: setFallbackNodes sets the initial points of contact. These nodes are used to connect to the network if the table is empty and there are no known nodes in the database.

declarations.doc: Table is the 'node table', a Kademlia-like index of neighbor nodes. The table keeps itself up-to-date by verifying the liveness of neighbors and requesting their node records when announcements of a new record version are received.

declarations.doc: bucket contains nodes, ordered by their last activity. the entry that was most recently active is the first element in entries.

declarations.name: nodesByDistance
declarations.doc: nodesByDistance is a list of nodes, ordered by distance to target.

declarations.name: transport

declarations.doc: dispatch runs in its own goroutine, handles incoming packets and deals with calls. For any destination node there is at most one 'active call', stored in the t.activeCall* maps. A call is made active when it is sent. The active call can be answered by a matching response, in which case c.ch receives the response; or by timing out, in which case c.err receives the error. When the function that created the call signals the active call is done through callDone, the next call from the call queue is started. Calls may also be answered by a WHOAREYOU packet referencing the call packet's authTag. When that happens the call is simply re-sent to complete the handshake. We allow one handshake attempt per call.

A good way to set the timeout is deciding how long you'd want to wait for a node on average. Passing a negative timeout makes the mixer completely fair.

declarations.name: ReadNodes
declarations.doc: ReadNodes reads at most n nodes from the given iterator. The return value contains no duplicates and no nil values. To prevent looping indefinitely for small repeating node sequences, this function calls Next at most n times.

declarations.name: FairMix
declarations.doc: FairMix aggregates multiple node iterators. The mixer itself is an iterator which ends only when Close is called. Source iterators added via AddSource are removed from the mix when they end. The distribution of nodes returned by Next is approximately fair, i.e. FairMix attempts to draw from all sources equally often. However, if a certain source is slow and doesn't return a node within the configured timeout, a node from any other source will be returned. It's safe to call AddSource and Close concurrently with Next.

declarations.name: Iterator
declarations.doc: Iterator represents a sequence of nodes. The Next method moves to the next node in the sequence. It returns false when the sequence has ended or the iterator is closed. Close may be called concurrently with Next and Node, and interrupts Next if it is blocked.

declarations.doc: ensureExpirer is a small helper method ensuring that the data expiration mechanism is running. If the expiration goroutine is already running, this method simply returns. The goal is to start the data evacuation only after the network successfully bootstrapped itself (to prevent dumping potentially useful seed nodes). Since it would require significant overhead to exactly trace the first successful convergence, it's simpler to "ensure" the correct state when an appropriate condition occurs (i.e. a successful bonding), and discard further events.

declarations.name: ParseV4
declarations.doc: ParseV4 parses a node URL. There are two basic forms of node URLs: - incomplete nodes, which only have the public key (node ID) - complete nodes, which contain the public key and IP/Port information For incomplete nodes, the designator must look like one of these enode://<hex node id> <hex node id> For complete nodes, the node ID is encoded in the username portion of the URL, separated from the host by an @ sign. The hostname can only be given as an IP address or using DNS domain name. The port in the host name section is the TCP listening port. If the TCP and UDP (discovery) ports differ, the UDP port is specified as query parameter "discport". In the following example, the node URL describes a node with IP address 10.3.58.6, TCP listening port 30303 and UDP discovery port 30301. enode://<hex node id>@10.3.58.6:30303?discport=30301

declarations.name: Capacity
declarations.doc: Capacity calculates the number of items the peer is estimated to be able to retrieve within the alloted time slot. The method will round up any division errors and will add an additional overestimation ratio on top. The reason for overshooting the capacity is because certain message types might not increase the load proportionally to the requested items, so fetching a bit more might still take the same RTT. By forcefully overshooting by a small amount, we can avoid locking into a lower-that-real capacity.

declarations.name: Capacity
declarations.doc: Capacity is a helper function to access a specific tracker without having to track it explicitly outside.

declarations.name: MeanCapacities
declarations.doc: MeanCapacities returns the capacities averaged across all the added trackers. The purpos of the mean capacities are to initialize a new peer with some sane starting values that it will hopefully outperform. If the mean overshoots, the peer will be cut back to minimal capacity and given another chance.

declarations.name: MedianRoundTrip
declarations.doc: MedianRoundTrip returns the median RTT across all known trackers. The purpose of the median RTT is to initialize a new peer with sane statistics that it will hopefully outperform. If it seriously underperforms, there's a risk of dropping the peer, but that is ok as we're aiming for a strong median.

declarations.name: NewTracker
declarations.doc: NewTracker creates a new message rate tracker for a specific peer. An initial RTT is needed to avoid a peer getting marked as an outlier compared to others right after joining. It's suggested to use the median rtt across all peers to init a new peer tracker.

declarations.name: NewTrackers
declarations.doc: NewTrackers creates an empty set of trackers to be filled with peers.

declarations.name: TargetRoundTrip
declarations.doc: TargetRoundTrip returns the current target round trip time for a request to complete in.The returned RTT is slightly under the estimated RTT. The reason is that message rate estimation is a 2 dimensional problem which is solvable for any RTT. The goal is to gravitate towards smaller RTTs instead of large messages, to result in a stabler download stream.

declarations.name: TargetTimeout
declarations.doc: TargetTimeout returns the timeout allowance for a single request to finish under. The timeout is proportional to the roundtrip, but also takes into consideration the tracker's confidence in said roundtrip and scales it accordingly. The final value is capped to avoid runaway requests.

If the delivery is zero, the peer is assumed to have either timed out or to not have the requested data, resulting in a slash to 0 capacity. This avoids assigning the peer retrievals that it won't be able to honour.

declarations.name: Tracker
declarations.doc: Tracker estimates the throughput capacity of a peer with regard to each data type it can deliver. The goal is to dynamically adjust request sizes to max out network throughput without overloading either the peer or th elocal node. By tracking in real time the latencies and bandiwdths peers exhibit for each packet type, it's possible to prevent overloading by detecting a slowdown on one type when another type is pushed too hard. Similarly, real time measurements also help avoid overloading the local net connection if our peers would otherwise be capable to deliver more, but the local link is saturated. In that case, the live measurements will force us to reduce request sizes until the throughput gets stable. Lastly, message rate measurements allows us to detect if a peer is unsuaully slow compared to other peers, in which case we can decide to keep it around or free up the slot so someone closer. Since throughput tracking and estimation adapts dynamically to live network conditions, it's fine to have multiple trackers locally track the same peer in different subsystem. The throughput will simply be distributed across the two trackers if both are highly active.

declarations.name: Trackers
declarations.doc: Trackers is a set of message rate trackers across a number of peers with the goal of aggregating certain measurements across the entire set for outlier filtering and newly joining initialization.

"" or "none" return nil "extip:77.12.33.4" will assume the local machine is reachable on the given IP "any" uses the first auto-detected mechanism "upnp" uses the Universal Plug and Play protocol "pmp" uses NAT-PMP with an auto-detected gateway address "pmp:192.168.0.1" uses NAT-PMP with the given gateway address

This type is useful because discovery can take a while but we want return an Interface value from UPnP, PMP and Auto immediately.

declarations.name: NodeStateMachine
declarations.doc: NodeStateMachine implements a network node-related event subscription system. It can assign binary state flags and fields of arbitrary type to each node and allows subscriptions to flag/field changes which can also modify further flags and fields, potentially triggering further subscriptions. An operation includes an initial change and all resulting subsequent changes and always ends in a consistent global state. It is initiated by a "top level" SetState/SetField call that blocks (also blocking other top-level functions) until the operation is finished. Callbacks making further changes should use the non-blocking SetStateSub/SetFieldSub functions. The tree of events resulting from the initial changes is traversed in a breadth-first order, ensuring for each subscription callback that all other callbacks caused by the same change triggering the current callback are processed before anything is triggered by the changes made in the current callback. In practice this logic ensures that all subscriptions "see" events in the logical order, callbacks are never called concurrently and "back and forth" effects are also possible. The state machine design should ensure that infinite event cycles cannot happen. The caller can also add timeouts assigned to a certain node and a subset of state flags. If the timeout elapses, the flags are reset. If all relevant flags are reset then the timer is dropped. State flags with no timeout are persisted in the database if the flag descriptor enables saving. If a node has no state flags set at any moment then it is discarded. Note: in order to avoid mutex deadlocks the callbacks should never lock a mutex that might be locked when the top level SetState/SetField functions are called. If a function potentially performs state/field changes then it is recommended to mention this fact in the function description, along with whether it should run inside an operation callback.

declarations.doc: readBuffer implements buffering for network reads. declarations.name: Bytes
