declarations.name: Decode
declarations.doc: Decode parses RLP-encoded data from r and stores the result in the value pointed to by val. Please see package-level documentation for the decoding rules. Val must be a non-nil pointer. If r does not implement ByteReader, Decode will do its own buffering. Note that Decode does not set an input limit for all readers and may be vulnerable to panics cause by huge value sizes. If you need an input limit, use NewStream(r, limit).Decode(val)

declarations.name: Decode
declarations.doc: Decode decodes a value and stores the result in the value pointed to by val. Please see the documentation for the Decode function to learn about the decoding rules.

declarations.name: DecodeBytes
declarations.doc: DecodeBytes parses RLP data from b into val. Please see package-level documentation for the decoding rules. The input must contain exactly one value and no trailing data.

declarations.name: Kind
declarations.doc: Kind returns the kind and size of the next value in the input stream. The returned size is the number of bytes that make up the value. For kind == Byte, the size is zero because the value is contained in the type tag. The first call to Kind will read size information from the input reader and leave it positioned at the start of the actual bytes of the value. Subsequent calls to Kind (until the value is decoded) will not advance the input reader and return cached information.

declarations.name: List
declarations.doc: List starts decoding an RLP list. If the input does not contain a list, the returned error will be ErrExpectedList. When the list's end has been reached, any Stream operation will return EOL.

declarations.name: ListEnd
declarations.doc: ListEnd returns to the enclosing list. The input reader must be positioned at the end of a list.

declarations.name: MoreDataInList
declarations.doc: MoreDataInList reports whether the current list context contains more data to be read.

declarations.name: NewListStream
declarations.doc: NewListStream creates a new stream that pretends to be positioned at an encoded list of the given length.

declarations.name: NewStream
declarations.doc: NewStream creates a new decoding stream reading from r. If r implements the ByteReader interface, Stream will not introduce any buffering. For non-toplevel values, Stream returns ErrElemTooLarge for values that do not fit into the enclosing list. Stream supports an optional input limit. If a limit is set, the size of any toplevel value will be checked against the remaining input length. Stream operations that encounter a value exceeding the remaining input length will return ErrValueTooLarge. The limit can be set by passing a non-zero value for inputLimit. If r is a bytes.Reader or strings.Reader, the input limit is set to the length of r's underlying data unless an explicit limit is provided.

declarations.name: Raw
declarations.doc: Raw reads a raw encoded value including RLP type information.

declarations.name: ReadBytes
declarations.doc: ReadBytes decodes the next RLP value and stores the result in b. The value size must match len(b) exactly.

declarations.name: Reset
declarations.doc: Reset discards any information about the current decoding context and starts reading from r. This method is meant to facilitate reuse of a preallocated Stream across many decoding operations. If r does not also implement ByteReader, Stream will do its own buffering.

declarations.name: Uint
declarations.doc: Uint reads an RLP string of up to 8 bytes and returns its contents as an unsigned integer. If the input does not contain an RLP string, the returned error will be ErrExpectedString. Deprecated: use s.Uint64 instead.

declarations.name: listLimit
declarations.doc: listLimit returns the amount of data remaining in the innermost list.

declarations.name: makeNilPtrDecoder
declarations.doc: makeNilPtrDecoder creates a decoder that decodes empty values as nil. Non-empty values are decoded into a value of the element type, just like makePtrDecoder does. This decoder is used for pointer-typed struct fields with struct tag "nil".

declarations.name: makePtrDecoder
declarations.doc: makePtrDecoder creates a decoder that decodes into the pointer's element type.

declarations.name: readByte
declarations.doc: readByte reads a single byte from the underlying stream.

declarations.name: readFull
declarations.doc: readFull reads into buf from the underlying stream.

declarations.name: willRead
declarations.doc: willRead is called before any read from the underlying stream. It checks n against size limits, and updates the limits if n doesn't overflow them.

declarations.name: ByteReader
declarations.doc: ByteReader must be implemented by any input reader for a Stream. It is implemented by e.g. bufio.Reader and bytes.Reader.

declarations.name: Decoder
declarations.doc: Decoder is implemented by types that require custom RLP decoding rules or need to decode into private fields. The DecodeRLP method should read one value from the given Stream. It is not forbidden to read less or more, but it might be confusing.

declarations.name: Kind
declarations.doc: Kind represents the kind of value contained in an RLP stream.

declarations.name: Stream
declarations.doc: Stream can be used for piecemeal decoding of an input stream. This is useful if the input is very large or if the decoding rules for a type depend on the input structure. Stream does not keep an internal buffer. After decoding a value, the input reader will be positioned just before the type information for the next value. When decoding a list and the input position reaches the declared length of the list, all operations will return error EOL. The end of the list must be acknowledged using ListEnd to continue reading the enclosing list. Stream is not safe for concurrent use.

declarations.name: TestDecodeWithEncReader
declarations.doc: This is a regression test checking that decoding from encReader works for RLP values of size 8192 bytes or more.

declarations.name: TestDecoderInByteSlice
declarations.doc: This test verifies that the byte slice/byte array logic does not kick in for element types implementing Decoder.

declarations.name: TestInvalidOptionalField
declarations.doc: This tests the validity checks for fields with struct tag "optional".

declarations.name: plainReader
declarations.doc: plainReader reads from a byte slice but does not implement ReadByte. It is also not recognized by the size validation. This is useful to test how the decoder behaves on a non-buffered input stream.

declarations.name: AppendToBytes
declarations.doc: AppendToBytes appends the encoded bytes to dst.

declarations.name: Flush
declarations.doc: Flush writes encoded RLP data to the output writer. This can only be called once. If you want to re-use the buffer after Flush, you must call Reset.

declarations.name: List
declarations.doc: List starts a list. It returns an internal index. Call EndList with this index after encoding the content to finish the list.

declarations.name: ListEnd
declarations.doc: ListEnd finishes the given list.

declarations.name: NewEncoderBuffer
declarations.doc: NewEncoderBuffer creates an encoder buffer.

declarations.name: Reset
declarations.doc: Reset truncates the buffer and sets the output destination.

declarations.name: ToBytes
declarations.doc: ToBytes returns the encoded bytes.

declarations.name: Write
declarations.doc: Write implements io.Writer and appends b directly to the output.

declarations.name: Write
declarations.doc: Write appends b directly to the encoder output.

declarations.name: WriteBigInt
declarations.doc: WriteBigInt encodes a big.Int as an RLP string. Note: Unlike with Encode, the sign of i is ignored.

declarations.name: WriteBool
declarations.doc: WriteBool writes b as the integer 0 (false) or 1 (true).

declarations.name: WriteBytes
declarations.doc: WriteBytes encodes b as an RLP string.

declarations.name: WriteString
declarations.doc: WriteBytes encodes s as an RLP string.

declarations.name: WriteUint64
declarations.doc: WriteUint64 encodes an unsigned integer.

declarations.name: list
declarations.doc: list adds a new list header to the header stack. It returns the index of the header. Call listEnd with this index after encoding the content of the list.

declarations.name: makeBytes
declarations.doc: makeBytes creates the encoder output.

declarations.name: next
declarations.doc: next returns the next piece of data to be read. it returns nil at EOF.

declarations.name: size
declarations.doc: size returns the length of the encoded data.

declarations.name: writeBigInt
declarations.doc: writeBigInt writes i as an integer.

declarations.name: writeBool
declarations.doc: writeBool writes b as the integer 0 (false) or 1 (true).

declarations.name: writeTo
declarations.doc: writeTo writes the encoder output to w.

declarations.name: EncoderBuffer
declarations.doc: EncoderBuffer is a buffer for incremental encoding. The zero value is NOT ready for use. To get a usable buffer, create it using NewEncoderBuffer or call Reset.

declarations.name: encReader
declarations.doc: encReader is the io.Reader returned by EncodeToReader. It releases its encbuf at EOF.

declarations.name: Encode
declarations.doc: Encode writes the RLP encoding of val to w. Note that Encode may perform many small writes in some cases. Consider making w buffered. Please see package-level documentation of encoding rules.

declarations.name: EncodeToBytes
declarations.doc: EncodeToBytes returns the RLP encoding of val. Please see package-level documentation for the encoding rules.

declarations.name: EncodeToReader
declarations.doc: EncodeToReader returns a reader from which the RLP encoding of val can be read. The returned size is the total size of the encoded data. Please see the documentation of Encode for the encoding rules.

declarations.name: encode
declarations.doc: encode writes head to the given buffer, which must be at least 9 bytes long. It returns the encoded bytes.

declarations.name: headsize
declarations.doc: headsize returns the size of a list or string header for a value of the given size.

declarations.name: intsize
declarations.doc: intsize computes the minimum number of bytes required to store i.

declarations.name: makeWriter
declarations.doc: makeWriter creates a writer function for the given type.

declarations.name: puthead
declarations.doc: puthead writes a list or string header to buf. buf must be at least 9 bytes long.

declarations.name: putint
declarations.doc: putint writes i to the beginning of b in big endian byte order, using the least number of bytes needed to represent i.

declarations.name: Encoder
declarations.doc: Encoder is implemented by types that require custom encoding rules or want to encode private fields.

declarations.name: TestEncodeToReaderReturnToPool
declarations.doc: This is a regression test verifying that encReader returns its encbuf to the pool only once.

declarations.name: EncodeRLP
declarations.doc: EncodeRLP writes x as RLP list [a, b] that omits the Name field.

declarations.name: NewListIterator
declarations.doc: NewListIterator creates an iterator for the (list) represented by data TODO: Consider removing this implementation, as it is no longer used.

declarations.name: Next
declarations.doc: Next forwards the iterator one step, returns true if it was not at end yet

declarations.name: Value
declarations.doc: Value returns the current value

declarations.name: TestIterator
declarations.doc: TestIterator tests some basic things about the ListIterator. A more comprehensive test can be found in core/rlp_test.go, where we can use both types and rlp without dependency cycles

declarations.name: AppendUint64
declarations.doc: AppendUint64 appends the RLP encoding of i to b, and returns the resulting slice.

declarations.name: CountValues
declarations.doc: CountValues counts the number of encoded values in b.

declarations.name: IntSize
declarations.doc: IntSize returns the encoded size of the integer x.

declarations.name: ListSize
declarations.doc: ListSize returns the encoded size of an RLP list with the given content size.

declarations.name: Split
declarations.doc: Split returns the content of first RLP value and any bytes after the value as subslices of b.

declarations.name: SplitList
declarations.doc: SplitList splits b into the content of a list and any remaining bytes after the list.

declarations.name: SplitString
declarations.doc: SplitString splits b into the content of an RLP string and any remaining bytes after the string.

declarations.name: SplitUint64
declarations.doc: SplitUint64 decodes an integer at the beginning of b. It also returns the remaining data after the integer in 'rest'.

declarations.name: RawValue
declarations.doc: RawValue represents an encoded RLP value and can be used to delay RLP decoding or to precompute an encoding. Note that the decoder does not verify whether the content of RawValues is valid RLP.

declarations.name: byteArrayBytes
declarations.doc: byteArrayBytes returns a slice of the byte array v.

declarations.name: firstOptionalField
declarations.doc: firstOptionalField returns the index of the first field with "optional" tag.

declarations.name: rtypeToStructType
declarations.doc: rtypeToStructType converts typ to rlpstruct.Type.

declarations.name: structFields
declarations.doc: structFields resolves the typeinfo of all public fields in a struct type.

declarations.name: typeNilKind
declarations.doc: typeNilKind gives the RLP value kind for nil pointers to 'typ'.

declarations.name: typeinfo
declarations.doc: typeinfo is an entry in the type cache.

declarations.name: typekey
declarations.doc: typekey is the key of a type in typeCache. It includes the struct tags because they might generate a different decoder.

declarations.name: byteArrayBytes
declarations.doc: byteArrayBytes returns a slice of the byte array v.

declarations.name: DefaultNilValue
declarations.doc: defaultNilValue determines whether a nil pointer to t encodes/decodes as an empty string or empty list.

declarations.name: ProcessFields
declarations.doc: ProcessFields filters the given struct fields, returning only fields that should be considered for encoding/decoding.

declarations.name: Field
declarations.doc: Field represents a struct field.

declarations.name: NilKind
declarations.doc: NilKind is the RLP value encoded in place of nil pointers.

declarations.name: TagError
declarations.doc: TagError is raised for invalid struct tags.

declarations.name: Tags
declarations.doc: Tags represents struct tags.

declarations.name: Type
declarations.doc: Type represents the attributes of a Go type.

declarations.name: generateDecoder
declarations.doc: generateDecoder generates the DecodeRLP method on 'typ'.

declarations.name: generateEncoder
declarations.doc: generateEncoder generates the EncodeRLP method on 'typ'.

declarations.name: importsList
declarations.doc: importsList returns all packages that need to be imported.

declarations.name: qualify
declarations.doc: qualify is the types.Qualifier used for printing types.

declarations.name: typeToStructType
declarations.doc: typeToStructType converts typ to rlpstruct.Type.

declarations.name: basicOp
declarations.doc: basicOp handles basic types bool, uint*, string.

declarations.name: bigIntOp
declarations.doc: bigIntNoPtrOp handles non-pointer big.Int. This exists because big.Int has it's own decoder operation on rlp.Stream, but the decode method returns *big.Int, so it needs to be dereferenced.

declarations.name: buildContext
declarations.doc: buildContext keeps the data needed for make*Op.

declarations.name: byteArrayOp
declarations.doc: byteArrayOp handles [...]byte.

declarations.name: encoderDecoderOp
declarations.doc: encoderDecoderOp handles rlp.Encoder and rlp.Decoder. In order to be used with this, the type must implement both interfaces. This restriction may be lifted in the future by creating separate ops for encoding and decoding.

declarations.name: genContext
declarations.doc: genContext is passed to the gen* methods of op when generating the output code. It tracks packages to be imported by the output file and assigns unique names of temporary variables.

declarations.name: ptrOp
declarations.doc: ptrOp handles pointer types.

declarations.name: sliceOp
declarations.doc: sliceOp handles slice types.

declarations.name: structOp
declarations.doc: structOp handles struct types.

declarations.name: process
declarations.doc: process generates the Go code.

declarations.name: isBigInt
declarations.doc: isBigInt checks whether 'typ' is "math/big".Int.

declarations.name: isByte
declarations.doc: isByte checks whether the underlying type of 'typ' is uint8.

declarations.name: nonZeroCheck
declarations.doc: nonZeroCheck returns the expression that checks whether 'v' is a non-zero value of type 'vtyp'.

declarations.name: typeReflectKind
declarations.doc: typeReflectKind gives the reflect.Kind that represents typ.

declarations.name: BatchCall
declarations.doc: BatchCall sends all given requests as a single batch and waits for the server to return a response for all of them. In contrast to Call, BatchCall only returns I/O errors. Any error specific to a request is reported through the Error field of the corresponding BatchElem. Note that batch calls may not be executed atomically on the server side.

declarations.name: BatchCallContext
declarations.doc: BatchCallContext sends all given requests as a single batch and waits for the server to return a response for all of them. The wait duration is bounded by the context's deadline. In contrast to CallContext, BatchCallContext only returns errors that have occurred while sending the request. Any error specific to a request is reported through the Error field of the corresponding BatchElem. Note that batch calls may not be executed atomically on the server side.

declarations.name: Call
declarations.doc: Call performs a JSON-RPC call with the given arguments and unmarshals into result if no error occurred. The result must be a pointer so that package json can unmarshal into it. You can also pass nil, in which case the result is ignored.

declarations.name: CallContext
declarations.doc: CallContext performs a JSON-RPC call with the given arguments. If the context is canceled before the call has successfully returned, CallContext returns immediately. The result must be a pointer so that package json can unmarshal into it. You can also pass nil, in which case the result is ignored.

declarations.name: ClientFromContext
declarations.doc: ClientFromContext retrieves the client from the context, if any. This can be used to perform 'reverse calls' in a handler method.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close closes the client, aborting any in-flight requests.

declarations.name: Dial
declarations.doc: Dial creates a new client for the given URL. The currently supported URL schemes are "http", "https", "ws" and "wss". If rawurl is a file name with no URL scheme, a local socket connection is established using UNIX domain sockets on supported platforms and named pipes on Windows. If you want to configure transport options, use DialHTTP, DialWebsocket or DialIPC instead. For websocket connections, the origin is set to the local host name. The client reconnects automatically if the connection is lost.

declarations.name: DialContext
declarations.doc: DialContext creates a new RPC client, just like Dial. The context is used to cancel or time out the initial connection establishment. It does not affect subsequent interactions with the client.

declarations.name: EthSubscribe
declarations.doc: EthSubscribe registers a subscription under the "eth" namespace.

declarations.name: Notify
declarations.doc: Notify sends a notification, i.e. a method call that doesn't expect a response.

declarations.name: RegisterName
declarations.doc: RegisterName creates a service for the given receiver type under the given name. When no methods on the given receiver match the criteria to be either a RPC method or a subscription an error is returned. Otherwise a new service is created and added to the service collection this client provides to the server.

declarations.name: SetHeader
declarations.doc: SetHeader adds a custom HTTP header to the client's requests. This method only works for clients using HTTP, it doesn't have any effect for clients using another transport.

declarations.name: ShhSubscribe
declarations.doc: ShhSubscribe registers a subscription under the "shh" namespace. Deprecated: use Subscribe(ctx, "shh", ...).

declarations.name: Subscribe
declarations.doc: Subscribe calls the "<namespace>_subscribe" method with the given arguments, registering a subscription. Server notifications for the subscription are sent to the given channel. The element type of the channel must match the expected type of content returned by the subscription. The context argument cancels the RPC request that sets up the subscription but has no effect on the subscription after Subscribe has returned. Slow subscribers will be dropped eventually. Client buffers up to 20000 notifications before considering the subscriber dead. The subscription Err channel will receive ErrSubscriptionQueueOverflow. Use a sufficiently large buffer on the channel or ensure that the channel usually has at least one reader to prevent this issue.

declarations.name: SupportedModules
declarations.doc: SupportedModules calls the rpc_modules method, retrieving the list of APIs that are available on the server.

declarations.name: dispatch
declarations.doc: dispatch is the main loop of the client. It sends read messages to waiting calls to Call and BatchCall and subscription notifications to registered subscriptions.

declarations.name: drainRead
declarations.doc: drainRead drops read messages until an error occurs.

declarations.name: read
declarations.doc: read decodes RPC messages from a codec, feeding them into dispatch.

declarations.name: send
declarations.doc: send registers op with the dispatch loop, then sends msg on the connection. if sending fails, op is deregistered.

declarations.name: BatchElem
declarations.doc: BatchElem is an element in a batch request.

declarations.name: Client
declarations.doc: Client represents a connection to an RPC server.

declarations.name: subscribeBlocks
declarations.doc: subscribeBlocks runs in its own goroutine and maintains a subscription for new blocks.

declarations.name: TestClientCancelWebsocket
declarations.doc: func TestClientCancelInproc(t *testing.T) { testClientCancel("inproc", t) }

declarations.name: TestClientCloseUnsubscribeRace
declarations.doc: This test reproduces https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/17837 where the client hangs during shutdown when Unsubscribe races with Client.Close.

declarations.name: TestClientErrorData
declarations.doc: This test checks that server-returned errors with code and data come out of Client.Call.

declarations.name: TestClientNotificationStorm
declarations.doc: This test checks that Client doesn't lock up when a single subscriber doesn't read subscription events.

declarations.name: TestClientSubscribeClose
declarations.doc: In this test, the connection drops while Subscribe is waiting for a response.

declarations.name: TestClientSubscriptionChannelClose
declarations.doc: This checks that the subscribed channel can be closed after Unsubscribe. It is the reproducer for https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/22322

declarations.name: TestClientSubscriptionUnsubscribeServer
declarations.doc: This checks that Client calls the _unsubscribe method on the server when Unsubscribe is called on a subscription.

declarations.name: testClientCancel
declarations.doc: This test checks that requests made through CallContext can be canceled by canceling the context.

declarations.name: flakeyListener
declarations.doc: flakeyListener kills accepted connections after a random timeout.

declarations.name: unsubscribeRecorder
declarations.doc: unsubscribeRecorder collects the subscription IDs of *_unsubscribe calls.

declarations.name: StartIPCEndpoint
declarations.doc: StartIPCEndpoint starts an IPC endpoint.

declarations.name: DataError
declarations.doc: A DataError contains some data in addition to the error message.

declarations.name: Error
declarations.doc: Error wraps RPC errors, which contain an error code in addition to the message.

declarations.name: HTTPError
declarations.doc: HTTPError is returned by client operations when the HTTP status code of the response is not a 2xx status.

declarations.name: invalidMessageError
declarations.doc: received message is invalid

declarations.name: invalidParamsError
declarations.doc: unable to decode supplied params, or an invalid number of parameters

declarations.name: invalidRequestError
declarations.doc: received message isn't a valid request

declarations.name: parseError
declarations.doc: Invalid JSON was received by the server.

declarations.name: addRequestOp
declarations.doc: addRequestOp registers a request operation.

declarations.name: cancelAllRequests
declarations.doc: cancelAllRequests unblocks and removes pending requests and active subscriptions.

declarations.name: cancelServerSubscriptions
declarations.doc: cancelServerSubscriptions removes all subscriptions and closes their error channels.

declarations.name: close
declarations.doc: close cancels all requests except for inflightReq and waits for call goroutines to shut down.

declarations.name: handleBatch
declarations.doc: handleBatch executes all messages in a batch and returns the responses.

declarations.name: handleCall
declarations.doc: handleCall processes method calls.

declarations.name: handleCallMsg
declarations.doc: handleCallMsg executes a call message and returns the answer.

declarations.name: handleImmediate
declarations.doc: handleImmediate executes non-call messages. It returns false if the message is a call or requires a reply.

declarations.name: handleMsg
declarations.doc: handleMsg handles a single message.

declarations.name: handleResponse
declarations.doc: handleResponse processes method call responses.

declarations.name: handleSubscribe
declarations.doc: handleSubscribe processes *_subscribe method calls.

declarations.name: handleSubscriptionResult
declarations.doc: handleSubscriptionResult processes subscription notifications.

declarations.name: removeRequestOp
declarations.doc: removeRequestOps stops waiting for the given request IDs.

declarations.name: runMethod
declarations.doc: runMethod runs the Go callback for an RPC method.

declarations.name: startCallProc
declarations.doc: startCallProc runs fn in a new goroutine and starts tracking it in the h.calls wait group.

declarations.name: unsubscribe
declarations.doc: unsubscribe is the callback function for all *_unsubscribe calls.

declarations.name: handler
declarations.doc: handler handles JSON-RPC messages. There is one handler per connection. Note that handler is not safe for concurrent use. Message handling never blocks indefinitely because RPCs are processed on background goroutines launched by handler. The entry points for incoming messages are: h.handleMsg(message) h.handleBatch(message) Outgoing calls use the requestOp struct. Register the request before sending it on the connection: op := &requestOp{ids: ...} h.addRequestOp(op) Now send the request, then wait for the reply to be delivered through handleMsg: if err := op.wait(...); err != nil { h.removeRequestOp(op) // timeout, etc. }

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close does nothing and always returns nil.

declarations.name: DialHTTP
declarations.doc: DialHTTP creates a new RPC client that connects to an RPC server over HTTP.

declarations.name: DialHTTPWithClient
declarations.doc: DialHTTPWithClient creates a new RPC client that connects to an RPC server over HTTP using the provided HTTP Client.

declarations.name: RemoteAddr
declarations.doc: RemoteAddr returns the peer address of the underlying connection.

declarations.name: ServeHTTP
declarations.doc: ServeHTTP serves JSON-RPC requests over HTTP.

declarations.name: SetWriteDeadline
declarations.doc: SetWriteDeadline does nothing and always returns nil.

declarations.name: validateRequest
declarations.doc: validateRequest returns a non-zero response code and error message if the request is invalid.

declarations.name: HTTPTimeouts
declarations.doc: HTTPTimeouts represents the configuration params for the HTTP RPC server.

declarations.name: httpServerConn
declarations.doc: httpServerConn turns a HTTP connection into a Conn.

declarations.name: TestHTTPErrorResponse
declarations.doc: Tests that an HTTP error results in an HTTPError instance being returned with the expected attributes.

declarations.name: TestHTTPRespBodyUnlimited
declarations.doc: This checks that maxRequestContentLength is not applied to the response of a request.

declarations.name: DialInProc
declarations.doc: DialInProc attaches an in-process connection to the given RPC server.

declarations.name: DialIPC
declarations.doc: DialIPC create a new IPC client that connects to the given endpoint. On Unix it assumes the endpoint is the full path to a unix socket, and Windows the endpoint is an identifier for a named pipe. The context is used for the initial connection establishment. It does not affect subsequent interactions with the client.

declarations.name: ServeListener
declarations.doc: ServeListener accepts connections on l, serving JSON-RPC on them.

declarations.name: ipcListen
declarations.doc: ipcListen will create a named pipe on the given endpoint.

declarations.name: newIPCConnection
declarations.doc: newIPCConnection will connect to a named pipe with the given endpoint as name.

declarations.name: ipcListen
declarations.doc: ipcListen will create a Unix socket on the given endpoint.

declarations.name: newIPCConnection
declarations.doc: newIPCConnection will connect to a Unix socket on the given endpoint.

declarations.name: ipcListen
declarations.doc: ipcListen will create a named pipe on the given endpoint.

declarations.name: newIPCConnection
declarations.doc: newIPCConnection will connect to a named pipe with the given endpoint as name.

declarations.name: NewCodec
declarations.doc: NewCodec creates a codec on the given connection. If conn implements ConnRemoteAddr, log messages will use it to include the remote address of the connection.

declarations.name: NewFuncCodec
declarations.doc: NewFuncCodec creates a codec which uses the given functions to read and write. If conn implements ConnRemoteAddr, log messages will use it to include the remote address of the connection.

declarations.name: closed
declarations.doc: Closed returns a channel which will be closed when Close is called

declarations.name: isBatch
declarations.doc: isBatch returns true when the first non-whitespace characters is '['

declarations.name: parseMessage
declarations.doc: parseMessage parses raw bytes as a (batch of) JSON-RPC message(s). There are no error checks in this function because the raw message has already been syntax-checked when it is called. Any non-JSON-RPC messages in the input return the zero value of jsonrpcMessage.

declarations.name: parsePositionalArguments
declarations.doc: parsePositionalArguments tries to parse the given args to an array of values with the given types. It returns the parsed values or an error when the args could not be parsed. Missing optional arguments are returned as reflect.Zero values.

declarations.name: parseSubscriptionName
declarations.doc: parseSubscriptionName extracts the subscription name from an encoded argument array.

declarations.name: Conn
declarations.doc: Conn is a subset of the methods of net.Conn which are sufficient for ServerCodec.

declarations.name: ConnRemoteAddr
declarations.doc: ConnRemoteAddr wraps the RemoteAddr operation, which returns a description of the peer address of a connection. If a Conn also implements ConnRemoteAddr, this description is used in log messages.

declarations.name: jsonCodec
declarations.doc: jsonCodec reads and writes JSON-RPC messages to the underlying connection. It also has support for parsing arguments and serializing (result) objects.

declarations.name: jsonrpcMessage
declarations.doc: A value of this type can a JSON-RPC request, notification, successful response or error response. Which one it is depends on the fields.

declarations.name: Modules
declarations.doc: Modules returns the list of RPC services with their version number

declarations.name: NewServer
declarations.doc: NewServer creates a new server instance with no registered handlers.

declarations.name: PeerInfoFromContext
declarations.doc: PeerInfoFromContext returns information about the client's network connection. Use this with the context passed to RPC method handler functions. The zero value is returned if no connection info is present in ctx.

declarations.name: RegisterName
declarations.doc: RegisterName creates a service for the given receiver type under the given name. When no methods on the given receiver match the criteria to be either a RPC method or a subscription an error is returned. Otherwise a new service is created and added to the service collection this server provides to clients.

declarations.name: ServeCodec
declarations.doc: ServeCodec reads incoming requests from codec, calls the appropriate callback and writes the response back using the given codec. It will block until the codec is closed or the server is stopped. In either case the codec is closed. Note that codec options are no longer supported.

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop stops reading new requests, waits for stopPendingRequestTimeout to allow pending requests to finish, then closes all codecs which will cancel pending requests and subscriptions.

declarations.name: serveSingleRequest
declarations.doc: serveSingleRequest reads and processes a single RPC request from the given codec. This is used to serve HTTP connections. Subscriptions and reverse calls are not allowed in this mode.

declarations.name: CodecOption
declarations.doc: CodecOption specifies which type of messages a codec supports. Deprecated: this option is no longer honored by Server.

declarations.name: PeerInfo
declarations.doc: PeerInfo contains information about the remote end of the network connection. This is available within RPC method handlers through the context. Call PeerInfoFromContext to get information about the client connection related to the current method call.

declarations.name: RPCService
declarations.doc: RPCService gives meta information about the server. e.g. gives information about the loaded modules.

declarations.name: Server
declarations.doc: Server is an RPC server.

declarations.name: TestServerShortLivedConn
declarations.doc: This test checks that responses are delivered for very short-lived connections that only carry a single request.

declarations.name: call
declarations.doc: call invokes the callback.

declarations.name: callback
declarations.doc: callback returns the callback corresponding to the given RPC method name.

declarations.name: formatName
declarations.doc: formatName converts to first character of name to lowercase.

declarations.name: isContextType
declarations.doc: Is t context.Context or *context.Context?

declarations.name: isErrorType
declarations.doc: Does t satisfy the error interface?

declarations.name: isPubSub
declarations.doc: isPubSub tests whether the given method has as as first argument a context.Context and returns the pair (Subscription, error).

declarations.name: isSubscriptionType
declarations.doc: Is t Subscription or *Subscription?

declarations.name: makeArgTypes
declarations.doc: makeArgTypes composes the argTypes list.

declarations.name: newCallback
declarations.doc: newCallback turns fn (a function) into a callback object. It returns nil if the function is unsuitable as an RPC callback.

declarations.name: subscription
declarations.doc: subscription returns a subscription callback in the given service.

declarations.name: suitableCallbacks
declarations.doc: suitableCallbacks iterates over the methods of the given type. It determines if a method satisfies the criteria for a RPC callback or a subscription callback and adds it to the collection of callbacks. See server documentation for a summary of these criteria.

declarations.name: callback
declarations.doc: callback is a method callback which was registered in the server

declarations.name: service
declarations.doc: service represents a registered object.

declarations.name: DialIO
declarations.doc: DialIO creates a client which uses the given IO channels

declarations.name: DialStdIO
declarations.doc: DialStdIO creates a client on stdin/stdout.

declarations.name: Closed
declarations.doc: Closed returns a channel that is closed when the RPC connection is closed. Deprecated: use subscription error channel

declarations.name: CreateSubscription
declarations.doc: CreateSubscription returns a new subscription that is coupled to the RPC connection. By default subscriptions are inactive and notifications are dropped until the subscription is marked as active. This is done by the RPC server after the subscription ID is send to the client.

declarations.name: Err
declarations.doc: Err returns the subscription error channel. The intended use of Err is to schedule resubscription when the client connection is closed unexpectedly. The error channel receives a value when the subscription has ended due to an error. The received error is nil if Close has been called on the underlying client and no other error has occurred. The error channel is closed when Unsubscribe is called on the subscription.

declarations.name: Err
declarations.doc: Err returns a channel that is closed when the client send an unsubscribe request.

declarations.name: MarshalJSON
declarations.doc: MarshalJSON marshals a subscription as its ID.

declarations.name: NewID
declarations.doc: NewID returns a new, random ID.

declarations.name: NotifierFromContext
declarations.doc: NotifierFromContext returns the Notifier value stored in ctx, if any.

declarations.name: Notify
declarations.doc: Notify sends a notification to the client with the given data as payload. If an error occurs the RPC connection is closed and the error is returned.

declarations.name: Unsubscribe
declarations.doc: Unsubscribe unsubscribes the notification and closes the error channel. It can safely be called more than once.

declarations.name: activate
declarations.doc: activate is called after the subscription ID was sent to client. Notifications are buffered before activation. This prevents notifications being sent to the client before the subscription ID is sent to the client.

declarations.name: close
declarations.doc: close is called by the client's message dispatcher when the connection is closed.

declarations.name: deliver
declarations.doc: deliver is called by the client's message dispatcher to send a notification value.

declarations.name: forward
declarations.doc: forward is the forwarding loop. It takes in RPC notifications and sends them on the subscription channel.

declarations.name: randomIDGenerator
declarations.doc: randomIDGenerator returns a function generates a random IDs.

declarations.name: run
declarations.doc: run is the forwarding loop of the subscription. It runs in its own goroutine and is launched by the client's handler after the subscription has been created.

declarations.name: takeSubscription
declarations.doc: takeSubscription returns the subscription (if one has been created). No subscription can be created after this call.

declarations.name: ClientSubscription
declarations.doc: ClientSubscription is a subscription established through the Client's Subscribe or EthSubscribe methods.

declarations.name: ID
declarations.doc: ID defines a pseudo random number that is used to identify RPC subscriptions.

declarations.name: Notifier
declarations.doc: Notifier is tied to a RPC connection that supports subscriptions. Server callbacks use the notifier to send notifications.

declarations.name: Subscription
declarations.doc: A Subscription is created by a notifier and tied to that notifier. The client can use this subscription to wait for an unsubscribe request for the client, see Err().

declarations.name: TestServerUnsubscribe
declarations.doc: This test checks that unsubscribing works.

declarations.name: waitForMessages
declarations.doc: waitForMessages reads RPC messages from 'in' and dispatches them into the given channels. It stops if there is an error.

declarations.name: HangSubscription
declarations.doc: HangSubscription blocks on s.unblockHangSubscription before sending anything.

declarations.name: largeRespService
declarations.doc: largeRespService generates arbitrary-size JSON responses.

declarations.name: MarshalText
declarations.doc: MarshalText implements encoding.TextMarshaler. It marshals: - "latest", "earliest" or "pending" as strings - other numbers as hex

declarations.name: UnmarshalJSON
declarations.doc: UnmarshalJSON parses the given JSON fragment into a BlockNumber. It supports: - "latest", "earliest" or "pending" as string arguments - the block number Returned errors: - an invalid block number error when the given argument isn't a known strings - an out of range error when the given block number is either too little or too large

declarations.name: UnmarshalJSON
declarations.doc: UnmarshalJSON implements json.Unmarshaler.

declarations.name: API
declarations.doc: API describes the set of methods offered over the RPC interface

declarations.name: DecimalOrHex
declarations.doc: DecimalOrHex unmarshals a non-negative decimal or hex parameter into a uint64.

declarations.name: ServerCodec
declarations.doc: ServerCodec implements reading, parsing and writing RPC messages for the server side of a RPC session. Implementations must be go-routine safe since the codec can be called in multiple go-routines concurrently.

declarations.name: jsonWriter
declarations.doc: jsonWriter can write JSON messages to its underlying connection. Implementations must be safe for concurrent use.

declarations.name: DialWebsocket
declarations.doc: DialWebsocket creates a new RPC client that communicates with a JSON-RPC server that is listening on the given endpoint. The context is used for the initial connection establishment. It does not affect subsequent interactions with the client.

declarations.name: DialWebsocketWithDialer
declarations.doc: DialWebsocketWithDialer creates a new RPC client that communicates with a JSON-RPC server that is listening on the given endpoint using the provided dialer.

declarations.name: WebsocketHandler
declarations.doc: WebsocketHandler returns a handler that serves JSON-RPC to WebSocket connections. allowedOrigins should be a comma-separated list of allowed origin URLs. To allow connections with any origin, pass "*".

declarations.name: pingLoop
declarations.doc: pingLoop sends periodic ping frames when the connection is idle.

declarations.name: wsHandshakeValidator
declarations.doc: wsHandshakeValidator returns a handler that verifies the origin during the websocket upgrade process. When a '*' is specified as an allowed origins all connections are accepted.

declarations.name: TestClientWebsocketLargeMessage
declarations.doc: This checks that the websocket transport can deal with large messages.

declarations.name: TestClientWebsocketPing
declarations.doc: This test checks that client handles WebSocket ping frames correctly.

declarations.name: TestWebsocketLargeCall
declarations.doc: This test checks whether calls exceeding the request size limit are rejected.

declarations.name: TestWebsocketOriginCheck
declarations.doc: This test checks that the server rejects connections from disallowed origins.

declarations.name: wsPingTestServer
declarations.doc: wsPingTestServer runs a WebSocket server which accepts a single subscription request. When a value arrives on sendPing, the server sends a ping frame, waits for a matching pong and finally delivers a single subscription result.

declarations.name: severableReadWriteCloser
declarations.doc: severableReadWriteCloser wraps an io.ReadWriteCloser and provides a Sever() method to drop writes and read empty.

declarations.name: List
declarations.doc: List returns the set of wallet this signer manages. Each wallet can contain multiple accounts.

declarations.name: MetadataFromContext
declarations.doc: MetadataFromContext extracts Metadata from a given context.Context

declarations.name: New
declarations.doc: New creates a new password protected Account. The private key is protected with the given password. Users are responsible to backup the private key that is stored in the keystore location thas was specified when this API was created.

declarations.name: NewSignerAPI
declarations.doc: NewSignerAPI creates a new API that can be used for Account management. ksLocation specifies the directory where to store the password protected private key that is generated when a new Account is created. noUSB disables USB support that is required to support hardware devices such as ledger and trezor.

declarations.name: SignTransaction
declarations.doc: SignTransaction signs the given Transaction and returns it both as json and rlp-encoded form

declarations.name: String
declarations.doc: String implements Stringer interface

declarations.name: Version
declarations.doc: Returns the external api version. This method does not require user acceptance. Available methods are available via enumeration anyway, and this info does not contain user-specific data

declarations.name: derivationLoop
declarations.doc: derivationLoop listens for wallet events

declarations.name: logDiff
declarations.doc: logDiff logs the difference between the incoming (original) transaction and the one returned from the signer. it also returns 'true' if the transaction was modified, to make it possible to configure the signer not to allow UI-modifications to requests

declarations.name: newAccount
declarations.doc: newAccount is the internal method to create a new account. It should be used _after_ user-approval has been obtained

declarations.name: startUSBListener
declarations.doc: startUSBListener starts a listener for USB events, for hardware wallet interaction

declarations.name: ExternalAPI
declarations.doc: ExternalAPI defines the external API through which signing requests are made.

declarations.name: ListRequest
declarations.doc: types for the requests/response types between signer and UI

declarations.name: ListResponse
declarations.doc: types for the requests/response types between signer and UI

declarations.name: Message
declarations.doc: types for the requests/response types between signer and UI

declarations.name: Metadata
declarations.doc: Metadata about a request

declarations.name: NewAccountRequest
declarations.doc: types for the requests/response types between signer and UI

declarations.name: NewAccountResponse
declarations.doc: types for the requests/response types between signer and UI

declarations.name: SignDataRequest
declarations.doc: types for the requests/response types between signer and UI

declarations.name: SignDataResponse
declarations.doc: types for the requests/response types between signer and UI

declarations.name: SignTxRequest
declarations.doc: SignTxRequest contains info about a Transaction to sign

declarations.name: SignTxResponse
declarations.doc: SignTxResponse result from SignTxRequest

declarations.name: SignerAPI
declarations.doc: SignerAPI defines the actual implementation of ExternalAPI

declarations.name: StartupInfo
declarations.doc: types for the requests/response types between signer and UI

declarations.name: UIClientAPI
declarations.doc: UIClientAPI specifies what method a UI needs to implement to be able to be used as a UI for the signer

declarations.name: UserInputRequest
declarations.doc: types for the requests/response types between signer and UI

declarations.name: UserInputResponse
declarations.doc: types for the requests/response types between signer and UI

declarations.name: Validator
declarations.doc: Validator defines the methods required to validate a transaction against some sanity defaults as well as any underlying 4byte method database. Use fourbyte.Database as an implementation. It is separated out of this package to allow pieces of the signer package to be used without having to load the 7MB embedded 4byte dump.

declarations.name: headlessUi
declarations.doc: Used for testing

declarations.name: ApproveListing
declarations.doc: ApproveListing prompt the user for confirmation to list accounts the list of accounts to list can be modified by the UI

declarations.name: ApproveNewAccount
declarations.doc: ApproveNewAccount prompt the user for confirmation to create new Account, and reveal to caller

declarations.name: ApproveSignData
declarations.doc: ApproveSignData prompt the user for confirmation to request to sign data

declarations.name: ApproveTx
declarations.doc: ApproveTx prompt the user for confirmation to request to sign Transaction

declarations.name: ShowError
declarations.doc: ShowError displays error message to user

declarations.name: ShowInfo
declarations.doc: ShowInfo displays info message to user

declarations.name: confirm
declarations.doc: confirm returns true if user enters 'Yes', otherwise false

declarations.name: readString
declarations.doc: readString reads a single line from stdin, trimming if from spaces, enforcing non-emptyness.

declarations.name: sanitize
declarations.doc: sanitize quotes and truncates 'txt' if longer than 'limit'. If truncated, and ellipsis is added after the quoted string

declarations.name: ArgsForValidation
declarations.doc: ArgsForValidation returns a SendTxArgs struct, which can be used for the common validations, e.g. look up 4byte destinations

declarations.name: ToTypedData
declarations.doc: ToTypedData converts the tx to a EIP-712 Typed Data structure for signing

declarations.name: GnosisSafeTx
declarations.doc: GnosisSafeTx is a type to parse the safe-tx returned by the relayer, it also conforms to the API required by the Gnosis Safe tx relay service. See 'SafeMultisigTransaction' on https://safe-transaction.mainnet.gnosis.io/

declarations.name: EcRecover
declarations.doc: EcRecover recovers the address associated with the given sig. Only compatible with `text/plain`

declarations.name: SignData
declarations.doc: SignData signs the hash of the provided data, but does so differently depending on the content-type specified. Different types of validation occur.

declarations.name: SignTextValidator
declarations.doc: SignTextWithValidator signs the given message which can be further recovered with the given validator. hash = keccak256("\x19\x00"${address}${data}).

declarations.name: SignTypedData
declarations.doc: SignTypedData signs EIP-712 conformant typed data hash = keccak256("\x19${byteVersion}${domainSeparator}${hashStruct(message)}") It returns - the signature, - and/or any error

declarations.name: UnmarshalValidatorData
declarations.doc: UnmarshalValidatorData converts the bytes input to typed data

declarations.name: cliqueHeaderHashAndRlp
declarations.doc: cliqueHeaderHashAndRlp returns the hash which is used as input for the proof-of-authority signing. It is the hash of the entire header apart from the 65 byte signature contained at the end of the extra data. The method requires the extra data to be at least 65 bytes -- the original implementation in clique.go panics if this is the case, thus it's been reimplemented here to avoid the panic and simply return an error instead

declarations.name: determineSignatureFormat
declarations.doc: determineSignatureFormat determines which signature method should be used based upon the mime type In the cases where it matters ensure that the charset is handled. The charset resides in the 'params' returned as the second returnvalue from mime.ParseMediaType charset, ok := params["charset"] As it is now, we accept any charset and just treat it as 'raw'. This method returns the mimetype for signing along with the request

declarations.name: sign
declarations.doc: sign receives a request and produces a signature Note, the produced signature conforms to the secp256k1 curve R, S and V values, where the V value will be 27 or 28 for legacy reasons, if legacyV==true.

declarations.name: signTypedData
declarations.doc: signTypedData is identical to the capitalized version, except that it also returns the hash (preimage) - the signature preimage (hash)

declarations.name: TestFuzzerFiles
declarations.doc: TestFuzzerFiles tests some files that have been found by fuzzing to cause crashes or hangs.

declarations.name: TestGnosisCustomData
declarations.doc: TestGnosisCustomData tests the scenario where a user submits only the gnosis-safe specific data, and we fill the TypedData struct on our side

declarations.name: TestGnosisCustomDataWithChainId
declarations.doc: TestGnosisCustomData tests the scenario where a user submits only the gnosis-safe specific data, and we fill the TypedData struct on our side

declarations.name: TestGnosisTypedData
declarations.doc: TestGnosisTypedData tests the scenario where a user submits a full EIP-712 struct without using the gnosis-specific endpoint

declarations.name: dispatch
declarations.doc: dispatch sends a request over the stdio

declarations.name: notify
declarations.doc: notify sends a request over the stdio, and does not listen for a response

declarations.name: ChainId
declarations.doc: ChainId returns the chainid in use for Eip-155 replay protection Example call {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"clef_chainId","params":[], "id":8}

declarations.name: DeriveAccount
declarations.doc: DeriveAccount requests a HD wallet to derive a new account, optionally pinning it for later reuse. Example call {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"clef_deriveAccount","params":["ledger://","m/44'/60'/0'", false], "id":6}

declarations.name: Export
declarations.doc: Export returns encrypted private key associated with the given address in web3 keystore format. Example {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"clef_export","params":["0x19e7e376e7c213b7e7e7e46cc70a5dd086daff2a"], "id":4}

declarations.name: Import
declarations.doc: Import tries to import the given keyJSON in the local keystore. The keyJSON data is expected to be in web3 keystore format. It will decrypt the keyJSON with the given passphrase and on successful decryption it will encrypt the key with the given newPassphrase and store it in the keystore. Example (the address in question has privkey `11...11`): {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"clef_import","params":[{"address":"19e7e376e7c213b7e7e7e46cc70a5dd086daff2a","crypto":{"cipher":"aes-128-ctr","ciphertext":"33e4cd3756091d037862bb7295e9552424a391a6e003272180a455ca2a9fb332","cipherparams":{"iv":"b54b263e8f89c42bb219b6279fba5cce"},"kdf":"scrypt","kdfparams":{"dklen":32,"n":262144,"p":1,"r":8,"salt":"e4ca94644fd30569c1b1afbbc851729953c92637b7fe4bb9840bbb31ffbc64a5"},"mac":"f4092a445c2b21c0ef34f17c9cd0d873702b2869ec5df4439a0c2505823217e7"},"id":"216c7eac-e8c1-49af-a215-fa0036f29141","version":3},"test","yaddayadda"], "id":4}

declarations.name: ImportRawKey
declarations.doc: ImportRawKey stores the given hex encoded ECDSA key into the key directory, encrypting it with the passphrase. Example call (should fail on password too short) {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"clef_importRawKey","params":["1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111","test"], "id":6}

declarations.name: ListAccounts
declarations.doc: List available accounts. As opposed to the external API definition, this method delivers the full Account object and not only Address. Example call {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"clef_listAccounts","params":[], "id":4}

declarations.name: ListWallets
declarations.doc: ListWallets will return a list of wallets that clef manages Example call {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"clef_listWallets","params":[], "id":5}

declarations.name: New
declarations.doc: New creates a new password protected Account. The private key is protected with the given password. Users are responsible to backup the private key that is stored in the keystore location that was specified when this API was created. This method is the same as New on the external API, the difference being that this implementation does not ask for confirmation, since it's initiated by the user

declarations.name: NewUIServerAPI
declarations.doc: NewUIServerAPI creates a new UIServerAPI

declarations.name: OpenWallet
declarations.doc: OpenWallet initiates a hardware wallet opening procedure, establishing a USB connection and attempting to authenticate via the provided passphrase. Note, the method may return an extra challenge requiring a second open (e.g. the Trezor PIN matrix challenge). Example {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"clef_openWallet","params":["ledger://",""], "id":6}

declarations.name: SetChainId
declarations.doc: SetChainId sets the chain id to use when signing transactions. Example call to set Ropsten: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"clef_setChainId","params":["3"], "id":8}

declarations.name: fetchKeystore
declarations.doc: fetchKeystore retrieves the encrypted keystore from the account manager.

declarations.name: UIServerAPI
declarations.doc: SignerUIAPI implements methods Clef provides for a UI to query, in the bidirectional communication channel. This API is considered secure, since a request can only ever arrive from the UI -- and the UI is capable of approving any action, thus we can consider these requests pre-approved. NB: It's very important that these methods are not ever exposed on the external service registry.

declarations.name: rawWallet
declarations.doc: rawWallet is a JSON representation of an accounts.Wallet interface, with its data contents extracted into plain fields.

declarations.name: ValidatePasswordFormat
declarations.doc: ValidatePasswordFormat returns an error if the password is too short, or consists of characters outside the range of the printable 7bit ascii set

declarations.name: Dependencies
declarations.doc: Dependencies returns an array of custom types ordered by their hierarchical reference tree

declarations.name: EncodeData
declarations.doc: EncodeData generates the following encoding: `enc(value₁) ‖ enc(value₂) ‖ … ‖ enc(valueₙ)` each encoded member is 32-byte long

declarations.name: EncodePrimitiveValue
declarations.doc: EncodePrimitiveValue deals with the primitive values found while searching through the typed data

declarations.name: EncodeType
declarations.doc: EncodeType generates the following encoding: `name ‖ "(" ‖ member₁ ‖ "," ‖ member₂ ‖ "," ‖ … ‖ memberₙ ")"` each member is written as `type ‖ " " ‖ name` encodings cascade down and are sorted by name

declarations.name: Format
declarations.doc: Format returns a representation of typedData, which can be easily displayed by a user-interface without in-depth knowledge about 712 rules

declarations.name: GetWarnings
declarations.doc: / getWarnings returns an error with all messages of type WARN of above, or nil if no warnings were present

declarations.name: HashStruct
declarations.doc: HashStruct generates a keccak256 hash of the encoding of the provided data

declarations.name: Map
declarations.doc: Map generates a map version of the typed data

declarations.name: Map
declarations.doc: Map is a helper function to generate a map version of the domain

declarations.name: Pprint
declarations.doc: Pprint returns a pretty-printed version of nvt

declarations.name: ToTransaction
declarations.doc: ToTransaction converts the arguments to a transaction.

declarations.name: TypeHash
declarations.doc: TypeHash creates the keccak256 hash of the data

declarations.name: dataMismatchError
declarations.doc: dataMismatchError generates an error for a mismatch between the provided type and data

declarations.name: isPrimitiveTypeValid
declarations.doc: Checks if the primitive value is valid

declarations.name: parseBytes
declarations.doc: Attempt to parse bytes in different formats: byte array, hex string, hexutil.Bytes.

declarations.name: typeName
declarations.doc: typeName returns the canonical name of the type. If the type is 'Person[]', then this method returns 'Person'

declarations.name: validate
declarations.doc: validate makes sure the types are sound

declarations.name: validate
declarations.doc: validate checks if the given domain is valid, i.e. contains at least the minimum viable keys and values

declarations.name: validate
declarations.doc: Validate checks if the types object is conformant to the specs

declarations.name: NameValueType
declarations.doc: NameValueType is a very simple struct with Name, Value and Type. It's meant for simple json structures used to communicate signing-info about typed data with the UI

declarations.name: SendTxArgs
declarations.doc: SendTxArgs represents the arguments to submit a transaction This struct is identical to ethapi.TransactionArgs, except for the usage of common.MixedcaseAddress in From and To

declarations.name: Type
declarations.doc: Type is the inner type of an EIP-712 message

declarations.name: TypedData
declarations.doc: TypedData is a type to encapsulate EIP-712 typed messages

declarations.name: TypedDataDomain
declarations.doc: TypedDataDomain represents the domain part of an EIP-712 message.

declarations.name: Asset
declarations.doc: Asset loads and returns the asset for the given name. It returns an error if the asset could not be found or could not be loaded.

declarations.name: AssetDigest
declarations.doc: AssetDigest returns the digest of the file with the given name. It returns an error if the asset could not be found or the digest could not be loaded.

declarations.name: AssetDir
declarations.doc: AssetDir returns the file names below a certain directory embedded in the file by go-bindata. For example if you run go-bindata on data/... and data contains the following hierarchy: data/ foo.txt img/ a.png b.png then AssetDir("data") would return []string{"foo.txt", "img"}, AssetDir("data/img") would return []string{"a.png", "b.png"}, AssetDir("foo.txt") and AssetDir("notexist") would return an error, and AssetDir("") will return []string{"data"}.

declarations.name: AssetInfo
declarations.doc: AssetInfo loads and returns the asset info for the given name. It returns an error if the asset could not be found or could not be loaded.

declarations.name: AssetNames
declarations.doc: AssetNames returns the names of the assets.

declarations.name: AssetString
declarations.doc: AssetString returns the asset contents as a string (instead of a []byte).

declarations.name: Digests
declarations.doc: Digests returns a map of all known files and their checksums.

declarations.name: MustAsset
declarations.doc: MustAsset is like Asset but panics when Asset would return an error. It simplifies safe initialization of global variables.

declarations.name: MustAssetString
declarations.doc: MustAssetString is like AssetString but panics when Asset would return an error. It simplifies safe initialization of global variables.

declarations.name: RestoreAsset
declarations.doc: RestoreAsset restores an asset under the given directory.

declarations.name: RestoreAssets
declarations.doc: RestoreAssets restores an asset under the given directory recursively.

declarations.name: String
declarations.doc: String implements stringer interface, tries to use the underlying value-type

declarations.name: String
declarations.doc: String implements stringer interface for decodedCallData

declarations.name: parseCallData
declarations.doc: parseCallData matches the provided call data against the ABI definition and returns a struct containing the actual go-typed values.

declarations.name: parseSelector
declarations.doc: parseSelector converts a method selector into an ABI JSON spec. The returned data is a valid JSON string which can be consumed by the standard abi package.

declarations.name: verifySelector
declarations.doc: verifySelector checks whether the ABI encoded data blob matches the requested function signature.

declarations.name: decodedArgument

declarations.name: Next
declarations.doc: Next returns the next node in the union of tries being iterated over. It does this by maintaining a heap of iterators, sorted by the iteration order of their next elements, with one entry for each source trie. Each time Next() is called, it takes the least element from the heap to return, advancing any other iterators that also point to that same element. These iterators are called with descend=false, since we know that any nodes under these nodes will also be duplicates, found in the currently selected iterator. Whenever an iterator is advanced, it is pushed back into the heap if it still has elements remaining. In the case that descend=false - eg, we're asked to ignore all subnodes of the current node - we also advance any iterators in the heap that have the current path as a prefix.

declarations.name: VerifyRangeProof
declarations.doc: VerifyRangeProof checks whether the given leaf nodes and edge proof can prove the given trie leaves range is matched with the specific root. Besides, the range should be consecutive (no gap inside) and monotonic increasing. Note the given proof actually contains two edge proofs. Both of them can be non-existent proofs. For example the first proof is for a non-existent key 0x03, the last proof is for a non-existent key 0x10. The given batch leaves are [0x04, 0x05, .. 0x09]. It's still feasible to prove the given batch is valid. The firstKey is paired with firstProof, not necessarily the same as keys[0] (unless firstProof is an existent proof). Similarly, lastKey and lastProof are paired. Expect the normal case, this function can also be used to verify the following range proofs: - All elements proof. In this case the proof can be nil, but the range should be all the leaves in the trie. - One element proof. In this case no matter the edge proof is a non-existent proof or not, we can always verify the correctness of the proof. - Zero element proof. In this case a single non-existent proof is enough to prove. Besides, if there are still some other leaves available on the right side, then an error will be returned. Except returning the error to indicate the proof is valid or not, the function will also return a flag to indicate whether there exists more accounts/slots in the trie. Note: This method does not verify that the proof is of minimal form. If the input proofs are 'bloated' with neighbour leaves or random data, aside from the 'useful' data, then the proof will still be accepted.

declarations.name: get
declarations.doc: get returns the child of the given node. Return nil if the node with specified key doesn't exist at all. There is an additional flag `skipResolved`. If it's set then all resolved nodes won't be returned.

declarations.name: hasRightElement

declarations.name: proofToPath

All necessary nodes will be resolved and leave the remaining as hashnode. The given edge proof is allowed to be an existent or non-existent proof.

declarations.name: unset
declarations.doc: unset removes all internal node references either the left most or right most. It can meet these scenarios: - The given path is existent in the trie, unset the associated nodes with the specific direction - The given path is non-existent in the trie - the fork point is a fullnode, the corresponding child pointed by path is nil, return - the fork point is a shortnode, the shortnode is included in the range, keep the entire branch and return. - the fork point is a shortnode, the shortnode is excluded in the range, unset the entire branch.

declarations.name: unsetInternal
declarations.doc: unsetInternal removes all internal node references(hashnode, embedded node). It should be called after a trie is constructed with two edge paths. Also the given boundary keys must be the one used to construct the edge paths. It's the key step for range proof. All visited nodes should be marked dirty since the node content might be modified. Besides it can happen that some fullnodes only have one child which is disallowed. But if the proof is valid, the missing children will be filled, otherwise it will be thrown anyway. Note we have the assumption here the given boundary keys are different and right is larger than left.

If root is the zero hash or the sha3 hash of an empty string, the trie is initially empty. Otherwise, New will panic if db is nil and returns MissingNodeError if the root node cannot be found. Accessing the trie loads nodes from the database or node pool on demand. Loaded nodes are kept around until their 'cache generation' expires. A new cache generation is created by each call to Commit. cachelimit sets the number of past cache generations to keep.

declarations.name: TryGet
declarations.doc: TryGet returns the value for key stored in the trie. The value bytes must not be modified by the caller. If a node was not found in the database, a MissingNodeError is returned.

declarations.name: TryUpdate
declarations.doc: TryUpdate associates key with value in the trie. Subsequent calls to Get will return value. If value has length zero, any existing value is deleted from the trie and calls to Get will return nil. The value bytes must not be modified by the caller while they are stored in the trie. If a node was not found in the database, a MissingNodeError is returned.

declarations.name: TryUpdateAccount

declarations.name: Update
declarations.doc: Update associates key with value in the trie. Subsequent calls to Get will return value. If value has length zero, any existing value is deleted from the trie and calls to Get will return nil. The value bytes must not be modified by the caller while they are stored in the trie.

declarations.name: getSecKeyCache

declarations.name: hashKey

declarations.name: SecureTrie
declarations.doc: SecureTrie wraps a trie with key hashing. In a secure trie, all access operations hash the key using keccak256. This prevents calling code from creating long chains of nodes that increase the access time. Contrary to a regular trie, a SecureTrie can only be created with New and must have an attached database. The database also stores the preimage of each key. SecureTrie is not safe for concurrent use.

The rlp-encoded value was >= 32 bytes: - Then the 32-byte `hash` will be accessible in `st.val`. - And the 'st.type' will be 'hashedNode' 2. The rlp-encoded value was < 32 bytes - Then the <32 byte rlp-encoded value will be accessible in 'st.val'. - And the 'st.type' will be 'hashedNode' AGAIN This method also sets 'st.type' to hashedNode, and clears 'st.key'.

declarations.name: Sync
declarations.doc: Sync is the main state trie synchronisation scheduler, which provides yet unknown trie hashes to retrieve, accepts node data associated with said hashes and reconstructs the trie step by step until all is done.

declarations.name: SyncPath
declarations.doc: SyncPath is a path tuple identifying a particular trie node either in a single trie (account) or a layered trie (account -> storage). Content wise the tuple either has 1 element if it addresses a node in a single trie or 2 elements if it addresses a node in a stacked trie. To support aiming arbitrary trie nodes, the path needs to support odd nibble lengths. To avoid transferring expanded hex form over the network, the last part of the tuple (which needs to index into the middle of a trie) is compact encoded. In case of a 2-tuple, the first item is always 32 bytes so that is simple binary encoded. Examples: - Path 0x9 -> {0x19} - Path 0x99 -> {0x0099} - Path 0x01234567890123456789012345678901012345678901234567890123456789019 -> {0x0123456789012345678901234567890101234567890123456789012345678901, 0x19} - Path 0x012345678901234567890123456789010123456789012345678901234567890199 -> {0x0123456789012345678901234567890101234567890123456789012345678901, 0x0099}

declarations.doc: Benchmarks the trie Commit following a Hash. Since the trie caches the result of any operation, we cannot use b.N as the number of hashing rouns, since all rounds apart from the first one will be NOOP. declarations.doc: Benchmarks the trie hashing. Since the trie caches the result of any operation, we cannot use b.N as the number of hashing rouns, since all rounds apart from the first one will be NOOP. As such, we'll use b.N as the number of account to insert into the trie before measuring the hashing. BenchmarkHash-6 288680 4561 ns/op 682 B/op 9 allocs/op BenchmarkHash-6 275095 4800 ns/op 685 B/op 9 allocs/op pure hasher: BenchmarkHash-6 319362 4230 ns/op 675 B/op 9 allocs/op BenchmarkHash-6 257460 4674 ns/op 689 B/op 9 allocs/op With hashing in-between and pure hasher: BenchmarkHash-6 225417 7150 ns/op 982 B/op 12 allocs/op BenchmarkHash-6 220378 6197 ns/op 983 B/op 12 allocs/op same with old hasher BenchmarkHash-6 229758 6437 ns/op 981 B/op 12 allocs/op BenchmarkHash-6 212610 7137 ns/op 986 B/op 12 allocs/op

declarations.name: tracer
declarations.doc: tracer tracks the changes of trie nodes. During the trie operations, some nodes can be deleted from the trie, while these deleted nodes won't be captured by trie.Hasher or trie.Committer. Thus, these deleted nodes won't be removed from the disk at all. Tracer is an auxiliary tool used to track all insert and delete operations of trie and capture all deleted nodes eventually. The changed nodes can be mainly divided into two categories: the leaf node and intermediate node. The former is inserted/deleted by callers while the latter is inserted/deleted in order to follow the rule of trie. This tool can track all of them no matter the node is embedded in its parent or not, but valueNode is never tracked. Note tracer is not thread-safe, callers should be responsible for handling the concurrency issues by themselves.

declarations.name: TestEtcdResetWork_ExpiredThenSuperseded
declarations.doc: TestEtcdResetWork_ExpiredThenSuperseded reproduces the real stale-overwrite scenario: this node acquires a token, the token expires, and another miner then acquires the token (which, per acquireToken, deletes the expired token and writes a fresh one). When the original — now stale — caller finally runs etcdResetWork, the stored token no longer matches, so the reset is rejected with ErrInvalidToken and the work value the new holder set is preserved.

declarations.name: TestEtcdResetWork_TokenMismatch

declarations.name: newTestEtcdAdmin
declarations.doc: newTestEtcdAdmin starts a single-node embedded etcd and returns a *wemixAdmin bound to it. It deliberately does NOT go through (*wemixAdmin).etcdInit: that path spawns the production etcdEventHandler goroutine, which is a process-wide singleton keyed off the package-level `admin` and is not designed to be started and torn down repeatedly inside tests. Since etcdResetWork only depends on a ready etcd client/server (etcdIsReady) and ReqTimeout(), we start the embedded server directly and set etcdReady ourselves.

declarations.name: TestNilLatestBlockHeightGuard_RejectedAtHandler
declarations.doc: Sending the same crafted payload (LatestBlockHeight=nil) through the hardened simulator: the boundary reject drops the message before wemixapi.GotStatusEx, so miningPeers never sees the nil-height entry that would later panic electNextMiner.

declarations.name: TestNilLatestBlockTdGuard_PreventsHandlerPanic
declarations.doc: Sending the same crafted payload (LatestBlockTd=nil) through both simulators: only the vulnerable one panics; the hardened one's nil guard blocks the panic.

declarations.name: TestNodeNameRebind_PreventsQuorumForgery
declarations.doc: Quorum-forgery defense: when an attacker sprays N spoofed NodeNames, the hardened path stores every accepted status under the attacker's registered node name. Result: post-hardening miningPeers drops below quorum.

declarations.name: TestRegression_NilLatestBlockHeightPanicsElectNextMiner
declarations.doc: Single-message DoS reproduction: a StatusEx with LatestBlockHeight=nil and Status="up" reaches miningPeers via wemixapi.GotStatusEx, then electNextMiner (wemix/miner_limit.go) calls p.LatestBlockHeight.Int64() and panics on the nil *big.Int. The Status=="up" short circuit is the only thing standing between a crafted payload and the deref, and it is attacker-controlled. Preserved so that removal of the handler-side boundary reject is flagged immediately.

declarations.name: TestRegression_NilLatestBlockTdPanicsHandler
declarations.doc: Single-message DoS reproduction: a StatusEx with LatestBlockTd=nil drives the pre-hardening body into a Cmp(nil) call, which panics. The production fix is a nil guard in handleStatusEx.

declarations.name: TestRegression_SpoofedStatusExPoisonsWorkKey
declarations.doc: Full attack chain reproduction (PRE-FIX mirror): spoofed StatusEx → forged consensus quorum → would-be wemixWorkKey poisoning. Preserved so that removal of the NodeName rebinding hardening is flagged immediately.

declarations.name: TestRegression_StaleConsensusHeightBlocked
declarations.doc: TestRegression_StaleConsensusHeightBlocked verifies the strict height regression guard in syncCheck: when a poisoned quorum drives findConsensusBlock to return a height below the local header, the would-be etcdPut(wemixWorkKey, ...) must be suppressed. Mirror source: wemix/sync.go, body around the if consensusHeight.Cmp(header.Number) < 0 { ... return nil } guard immediately above the newWork construction.

declarations.name: acquireTokenSyncPredicate
declarations.doc: acquireTokenSyncPredicate models the byte-equality Compare predicate inside acquireTokenSync.

declarations.name: captureProductionLogs
declarations.doc: captureProductionLogs swaps the ethereum/go-ethereum/log root handler with an in-memory buffer so that any log output emitted by production code during the attack reproduction is captured. The original handler is restored on test cleanup.

declarations.name: resetMiningPeers
declarations.doc: resetMiningPeers clears the package-level miningPeers sync.Map.

declarations.name: runHandleMinerStatusUpdateLikeProduction
declarations.doc: runHandleMinerStatusUpdateLikeProduction reproduces the production handleMinerStatusUpdate goroutine body (wemix/sync.go) so that each received status is stored into miningPeers exactly as production would. Mirror source: sync.go body around `miningPeers.Store(status.NodeName, status.Clone())`. Calling the returned stop function terminates the goroutine.

declarations.name: simulateHandleStatusEx_Hardened
declarations.doc: simulateHandleStatusEx_Hardened mirrors the current production handleStatusEx body (NodeName rebinding + nil guards). Mirror source: eth/protocols/eth/wemix_handlers.go handleStatusEx Returns: - panicked: any value recovered from a panic (nil if none) - dropped: true if the message was discarded by a boundary validation reject (e.g., nil LatestBlockHeight)
